Aladdin gradually wins her trust by showing the warmth and courage beneath his princely disguise, while he struggles to admit who he really is.

Jafar eventually steals the lamp and forces Genie to make him Sultan, then the most powerful sorcerer in the world. He imprisons Aladdin and threatens Jasmine and the Sultan. Aladdin escapes, outwits Jafar by exploiting his hunger for greater power, and causes him to wish himself into Genie’s role—thereby trapping Jafar in the lamp. With one wish remaining, Aladdin keeps his promise and frees Genie. The Sultan recognizes Aladdin’s character and changes the law, allowing Jasmine to choose her own husband; she and Aladdin can finally be together.

The musical celebrates freedom, integrity, and the courage to define oneself rather than accept a role imposed by society. It also contrasts genuine love and friendship with the emptiness of wealth, rank, and unchecked ambition.

moulin rouge.en:
In Belle Époque Paris, Christian, an idealistic American songwriter, arrives in Montmartre seeking a life devoted to truth, beauty, freedom, and love. He joins the Bohemians Toulouse-Lautrec and Santiago, who are devising a new stage spectacle for the Moulin Rouge. Across town, the glittering but financially imperilled nightclub depends on its star, Satine—the “Sparkling Diamond.” Its owner and master of ceremonies, Harold Zidler, expects her to charm the wealthy Duke of Monroth into financing the club.

When Satine mistakes Christian for the Duke, their intended business meeting becomes an unexpected creative encounter. Christian pitches the Bohemians’ show; Satine is drawn to both his talent and his sincerity. When the actual Duke arrives, Satine quickly presents the proposed production as a vehicle for his patronage. The Duke agrees to back it, but only on the understanding that he will possess Satine exclusively. Zidler accepts the bargain because the Moulin Rouge and its company need the money.

As rehearsals proceed, Christian and Satine fall deeply in love, conducting their relationship in secret. Satine dreams of becoming a legitimate actress, while Christian believes love should triumph over wealth and social power. The Duke grows increasingly possessive and suspicious, especially as the new show’s story begins to resemble the lovers’ real circumstances. Meanwhile, Satine’s worsening illness remains largely hidden, even as it drains her strength.

Fearing the Duke’s threats against Christian and the Moulin Rouge, Satine tells Christian that she never loved him, hoping he will leave Paris and live. Heartbroken, he returns on the opening night determined to confront her. During the performance, Satine reveals through their shared song that her love was genuine. The Duke’s hold is broken, but Satine collapses after the triumph of the show and dies in Christian’s arms. Christian is left to preserve their story in the work he has written.

six.en:
Six opens as Catherine of Aragon, Anne Boleyn, Jane Seymour, Anna of Cleves, Katherine Howard and Catherine Parr take the stage as a pop group. They announce a contest: whichever queen can prove that she suffered most during her marriage to Henry VIII will become the group’s lead singer. Catherine of Aragon begins, defiantly recounting her refusal to accept being discarded and sent away when Henry turns his attention to Anne Boleyn. Anne answers with an irreverent, fast-moving account of becoming Henry’s chosen wife, discovering his unfaithfulness, and being condemned to death.

Jane Seymour is initially dismissed as the queen with the happiest marriage, but she explains the pressure placed upon her to produce a son and the grief that followed. Anna of Cleves then describes arriving for a marriage that rapidly collapses, yet turns the annulment into a life of independence, comfort and freedom. Katherine Howard presents herself as flirtatious and carefree, but her story gradually reveals a childhood and adulthood shaped by exploitation, coercion and the loss of control over her own life. Catherine Parr, encouraged to speak last, resists defining herself through Henry at all. She describes her intellectual ambitions, her love for another man, and the compromises she made to survive as queen.

As the competition intensifies, the women begin to recognise its cruel premise: it asks them to measure pain against one another and keeps their identities tied to the same man. They abandon the search for a winner. Instead, they imagine alternative lives in which each can pursue her own hopes, relationships and talents, free from the roles assigned to her. The concert ends with all six queens standing together, no longer competitors but equal voices in a shared story.

The show explores solidarity rather than rivalry, urging women to reclaim narratives that have reduced them to relationships with powerful men. It also examines identity, autonomy, survival and the possibility of imagining a future beyond trauma.

miss saigon.en:
In April 1975, as Saigon nears collapse, Kim, a young orphan, is forced to work at Dreamland, a bar run by the opportunistic Engineer. American Marines crowd the club before their evacuation. Chris, a disillusioned sergeant, meets Kim after his friend John urges him to take her away from the chaos. Their brief encounter becomes love, and Chris promises to take her to America. Kim’s former arranged fiancé, Thuy, discovers them and threatens Chris, but the couple marry in a private ceremony.

The city falls before they can escape together. In the frantic evacuation outside the American Embassy, Chris is carried away while Kim is left behind. Three years later, in the renamed Ho Chi Minh City, Thuy has become a Communist official and tries to claim Kim as his wife. Kim reveals that she has borne Chris’s son, Tam, and refuses Thuy’s authority. When he threatens the child, she kills him and flees with Tam and the Engineer.

They eventually reach Bangkok, where Kim works in a club while the Engineer dreams of exploiting Tam’s American heritage to reach the United States. In Atlanta, John now helps children fathered by American servicemen find their families. He tells Chris that Kim survived and that he has a son. Chris, haunted by the separation, has married Ellen; he reluctantly reveals Kim and Tam to her. Ellen and Chris travel with John to Bangkok, hoping to meet Kim.

Kim believes Chris has come to reclaim her and take Tam to America. Ellen tells her that Chris is married, devastating Kim’s hopes. Determined that Tam must have a future beyond the poverty and uncertainty surrounding them, Kim brings him to Chris. She fatally shoots herself, asking Chris to take their son as she dies in his arms.

The musical explores love distorted by war, displacement, and unequal power. It also confronts the cost borne by survivors—especially mothers and children—when personal promises collide with history and national conflict.

west side story.en:
In Manhattan’s West Side, two rival street gangs claim the same neighbourhood: the Jets, led by Riff, and the Sharks, recently arrived from Puerto Rico and led by Bernardo. At a community dance intended to ease tensions, former Jet Tony sees Bernardo’s younger sister, Maria, and they fall instantly in love. Bernardo’s girlfriend Anita and Maria’s friend Chino sense the danger, while Riff warns Tony that any involvement with Maria will intensify the conflict. Despite this, Tony and Maria meet secretly beneath Maria’s fire escape and promise themselves to one another.

Riff proposes a rumble to settle the gangs’ dispute, and Tony tries to prevent violence by persuading Bernardo to meet peacefully. At the meeting, however, insults and resentment prevail. When the fight begins, Tony refuses to strike Bernardo, but Riff attacks him. Bernardo kills Riff, and Tony, overcome with grief and rage, kills Bernardo in return. The gangs scatter as police sirens approach.

Maria is devastated by her brother’s death but still loves Tony. Anita, furious at Tony and the Jets, urges Maria to leave him, yet agrees to deliver a message arranging for Tony and Maria to escape together. Tony hides with Doc, the kindly owner of a local drugstore, while Chino searches the streets with a gun, determined to avenge Bernardo. At the drugstore, Anita is harassed and humiliated by the Jets. In anguish, she falsely tells them that Chino has killed Maria.

Doc delivers the news to Tony, who runs into the street calling for Chino to kill him as well. He finds Maria alive, but Chino arrives and shoots Tony. Tony dies in Maria’s arms. Holding Chino’s gun, Maria condemns both gangs for the hatred that has destroyed the people they love. The Jets and Sharks, shocked by the tragedy, join together to carry Tony’s body away.

The musical explores how prejudice, territorial loyalty, and cycles of retaliation turn ordinary conflict into irreversible loss. Against that violence, Tony and Maria’s love represents the fragile hope that people might choose understanding over hatred.

sweeney todd.en:
Sweeney Todd, a barber unjustly transported to Australia by the corrupt Judge Turpin, returns to Victorian London under the name Sweeney Todd, determined to reclaim the life that was stolen from him. In Fleet Street, he encounters Mrs. Lovett, the proprietress of a failing pie shop, who recognizes him as Benjamin Barker. She tells him that Turpin lusted after Barker’s wife, Lucy, arranged Barker’s false conviction and exile, and then destroyed Lucy’s life. Their daughter, Johanna, now lives as Turpin’s unwilling ward. Todd vows revenge, while Mrs. Lovett hopes to turn their renewed partnership into romance.

Todd reopens his barbershop above Mrs. Lovett’s shop and waits for Turpin. Meanwhile, Johanna falls in love with Anthony Hope, a young sailor who met Todd on the voyage home. Anthony promises to rescue her from Turpin, but the Judge sends Johanna to the grim Fogg’s Asylum to keep her beyond Anthony’s reach. Todd’s first attempt at revenge fails when Anthony’s impulsive arrival interrupts Turpin’s shave. Furious, Todd resolves to kill not only the Judge but any customer who enters his chair. Mrs. Lovett turns the bodies into meat pies, and her business suddenly thrives.

As the death toll rises, Anthony plans Johanna’s escape from the asylum, while Tobias Ragg, Mrs. Lovett’s devoted assistant, becomes suspicious of Todd and the pies. The Beadle Bamford, investigating strange smells and complaints, visits the shop and becomes another victim. At last, Turpin comes to Todd’s barbershop, lured by a false message suggesting that Johanna wishes to see him. Todd kills the Judge, but in the chaos he also murders a beggar woman who has been haunting Fleet Street. He then learns from Mrs. Lovett that the beggar woman was Lucy, his wife. Devastated, Todd kills Mrs. Lovett and is himself slain by Tobias.

The musical explores vengeance as a force that consumes the person seeking it, turning justice into indiscriminate violence. It also exposes corruption, poverty, exploitation, and moral blindness in a society that treats human lives as disposable.

sunset boulevard.en:
In Hollywood, 1950, the dead Joe Gillis narrates from a swimming pool, then takes the story back six months. A struggling screenwriter unable to sell a script or keep up his car payments, Joe flees repossession agents and turns into the garage of a decaying mansion on Sunset Boulevard. There he meets Norma Desmond, a long-forgotten silent-film star living in isolation with her butler, Max von Mayerling. Norma mistakes Joe for a man hired to arrange the burial of her pet chimpanzee, but when she learns he is a writer, she hires him to revise Salome, her enormous screenplay for a triumphant return to the screen.

Joe initially treats the assignment as temporary shelter, but Norma draws him into her luxurious, suffocating world. Max secretly sustains her belief that the public still worships her by writing fan letters, and Joe discovers that Max was once Norma’s husband and director. Norma gives Joe expensive clothes, installs him in the house, and turns their arrangement into a possessive romance. Meanwhile, at Paramount Studios, Joe reconnects with Betty Schaefer, a young script reader engaged to his friend Artie Green. Betty recognizes Joe’s talent and persuades him to collaborate with her on a new story. Their late-night writing sessions grow into love.

Norma believes a visit to Cecil B. DeMille’s studio confirms that Hollywood is eager to film Salome. When she finds Joe’s script pages and learns of Betty, however, she attempts suicide. Joe stays, but soon realizes that remaining means surrendering his future. He tells Norma that the studio has no plans for her comeback and that Max’s fan mail is a deception. As Joe leaves the mansion, Norma shoots him. Surrounded by police and newsreel cameras, she descends the staircase believing she is performing for DeMille, ready at last for her close-up.

The musical explores fame’s destructive afterlife, the cruelty of an industry that discards its former idols, and the seductive power of illusion. It also sets Joe and Norma’s doomed bargain against Betty’s more hopeful belief in creativity and genuine connection.

evita.en:
In 1934, fifteen-year-old Eva Duarte leaves the small Argentine town of Junín for Buenos Aires with the tango singer Agustín Magaldi, determined to escape poverty and become somebody. Abandoned by Magaldi, she survives through relationships with increasingly influential men, trading affection, social ambition, and relentless calculation for access to the city’s entertainment world. Eva becomes a successful radio actress and, by 1943, meets Colonel Juan Perón at a charity concert following an earthquake. Their connection is immediate: Perón sees in Eva a charismatic ally who understands the aspirations of Argentina’s working class, while Eva recognises that his political rise can secure the power and recognition she has always sought. Together they build a formidable public image, though Perón’s military colleagues and Argentina’s elite regard Eva with suspicion and contempt.

When Perón is arrested by rivals who fear his growing influence, Eva rallies the descamisados—the working people who adore her—to demand his release. Their mass demonstration forces the authorities to yield, and Perón soon wins the presidency. As First Lady, Eva becomes a tireless public figure: she distributes aid through her foundation, champions women’s suffrage, speaks for workers, and undertakes a celebrated tour of Europe. Yet her prominence inflames opposition at home, and her ambition to become Vice President is blocked by the army and political establishment. The public devotion that carries her through each triumph cannot protect her from worsening illness.

As Eva’s health fails, she confronts the cost of the life she has built and struggles to retain the love of the Argentine people. She renounces the vice-presidential nomination, but continues appearing before crowds until she can no longer do so. After her death, Perón mourns the woman who transformed both his fortunes and the country’s political imagination, while the narrator Che persistently questions the nature of her achievements and the price paid for them.

The show explores ambition, class, celebrity, political power, and the uneasy divide between public myth and private reality. It asks whether Eva’s devotion to ordinary Argentines was liberation, self-invention, or both—and why a nation needs figures it can worship.

jesus christ superstar.en:
The final days of Jesus of Nazareth unfold through the troubled perspective of Judas Iscariot. In Jerusalem, Jesus’s growing following alarms Judas, who fears that the movement’s intensity will provoke Roman retaliation and destroy everything Jesus has tried to build. He is also disturbed by Jesus’s closeness to Mary Magdalene, whose compassion offers Jesus comfort amid mounting pressure. Jesus arrives in Jerusalem to an ecstatic welcome, but the celebration intensifies the concerns of the High Priests, Caiaphas and Annas. They decide that Jesus must be stopped before his influence leads to unrest.

As crowds continue to seek miracles, leadership, and answers from Jesus, he becomes increasingly isolated. He drives merchants and money changers from the Temple, then is overwhelmed by people demanding healing and salvation. Mary Magdalene tries to soothe him, while Judas’s anxiety hardens into a terrible decision. He meets Caiaphas and Annas and agrees to reveal where Jesus can be found, believing that handing him over may prevent a wider catastrophe.

At the Last Supper, Jesus confronts his disciples’ misunderstandings and foretells both Judas’s betrayal and Peter’s denial. Later, in the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus wrestles alone with fear, anger, and doubt as he faces the fate before him. Judas arrives with soldiers, identifies Jesus, and watches as he is arrested. Peter denies knowing Jesus, while Mary Magdalene remains grief-stricken.

Jesus is brought first before Pontius Pilate, who finds him difficult to judge and sends him to King Herod. Herod mocks Jesus and sends him back. Pilate, pressured by the crowd and haunted by visions of responsibility, orders Jesus to be scourged and crucified. Judas, devastated by the consequences of his betrayal, is consumed by guilt. Jesus is led to Golgotha, where he is crucified and dies.

The show explores faith, power, loyalty, betrayal, and the human cost of turning ideals into public movements. It presents its central figures as people struggling with fear, love, doubt, responsibility, and the consequences of their choices.

fiddler on the roof.en:
In the small Russian village of Anatevka, Tevye, a poor Jewish milkman, lives with his wife Golde and their five daughters. He tries to uphold cherished traditions while dreaming of a little more comfort for his family. When his eldest daughter, Tzeitel, is expected to marry the wealthy butcher Lazar Wolf, she confesses that she loves Motel Kamzoil, a timid tailor. Tevye is troubled by the match but ultimately supports the young couple, even inventing a dream to persuade Golde that their marriage is divinely approved.

Soon, Tevye’s second daughter, Hodel, falls in love with Perchik, an idealistic student and political radical who has come to Anatevka. Perchik challenges old customs, teaching the villagers new ideas and encouraging Hodel to dance with him publicly. When he leaves to join revolutionary activity, Hodel decides to follow him to Siberia after he is arrested. Tevye, though distressed by her departure, blesses her choice at the railway station.

The third daughter, Chava, falls in love with Fyedka, a Christian villager. Their relationship tests Tevye more deeply than the earlier marriages because it crosses the religious boundary he believes cannot be broken. Chava marries Fyedka without Tevye’s consent. Unable to accept the marriage, Tevye tells his family that Chava is dead to them, even as he is visibly torn by his love for her.

Meanwhile, hostility toward Anatevka’s Jewish community grows. A wedding celebration is violently disrupted, and the villagers eventually receive orders to leave their homes. As the community prepares to depart, Tevye and Golde gather their belongings and set out with their remaining family members. Chava and Fyedka appear and announce that they, too, will leave rather than remain among people who persecute others. Tevye cannot fully reconcile with Chava, but he quietly signals his affection before the family disperses into exile.

The musical explores the tension between tradition and change, showing how love, family, faith, and social upheaval reshape lives. Its characters struggle to preserve dignity and connection when the world they know is breaking apart.

guys and dolls.en:
In bustling Times Square, Nathan Detroit is scrambling to find $1,000 to secure a new location for his illegal floating crap game before Lieutenant Brannigan can shut it down. His fiancée, Miss Adelaide, has waited fourteen years for the wedding Nathan continually postpones, convinced that his evasions are making her physically ill. Nathan spots an opportunity in the fearless gambler Sky Masterson, who will wager on almost anything. He bets Sky $1,000 that Sky cannot persuade Sergeant Sarah Brown, the stern leader of the Save-a-Soul Mission, to have dinner with him in Havana. Sky accepts, but Sarah refuses him until he promises to bring enough sinners to the Mission’s upcoming meeting to save it from closure by General Matilda Cartwright.

In Havana, Sarah briefly abandons her rigid self-control, and she and Sky fall for one another. Back in New York, however, Sky discovers that Nathan has moved the craps game into the Mission. When Brannigan raids the place, Sarah assumes Sky has betrayed her and rejects him. Meanwhile, Nathan tries to flee from Adelaide’s wedding plans, only to find himself trapped by his own promises and by Adelaide’s determination.

Sky sets out to repair the damage. He tracks down the gamblers, including Nicely-Nicely Johnson, Benny Southstreet, Harry the Horse, and Big Jule, and challenges them to a high-stakes game: if he wins, they must attend the Mission meeting; if he loses, they take his money. Sky wins, and the gamblers arrive at the Mission, where Nicely-Nicely gives an unexpectedly fervent account of his reform. Sarah recognizes Sky’s sacrifice and accepts his love. Nathan finally agrees to marry Adelaide, and the two couples celebrate their weddings together.

my fair lady.en:
In Edwardian London, Professor Henry Higgins, a brilliant but insensitive phonetics expert, encounters Eliza Doolittle, a Cockney flower seller, outside Covent Garden. Intrigued by her accent and convinced that speech alone determines how society judges people, Higgins boasts to fellow linguist Colonel Pickering that he could pass Eliza off as a duchess after six months of instruction. Eliza, hoping to escape poverty and obtain work in a flower shop, arrives at Higgins’s home in Wimpole Street to accept the challenge. Higgins and Pickering take her in, while Higgins’s housekeeper, Mrs. Pearce, worries about the girl’s welfare.

The lessons are punishing. Higgins drills Eliza relentlessly in pronunciation, manners, and social conduct, while Eliza struggles with exhaustion and humiliation. A breakthrough comes when she masters difficult vowel sounds, and Higgins brings her to Ascot Racecourse to test her progress. There, Eliza’s polished appearance impresses the fashionable crowd, though an enthusiastic lapse into her old speech patterns startles them. Freddy Eynsford-Hill, captivated by her, begins pursuing her.

Higgins then presents Eliza at an embassy ball, where she succeeds so completely that even a Hungarian phonetics expert declares her a genuine lady. Higgins celebrates the triumph with Pickering but fails to acknowledge Eliza’s effort or uncertainty about her future. Hurt by their indifference, she leaves Higgins’s house after a fierce confrontation. She finds refuge with her father, Alfred P. Doolittle, who has unexpectedly become wealthy and respectable after Higgins’s casual intervention. Eliza later visits Mrs. Higgins and faces Higgins again, refusing to return to a life in which he treats her as an experiment. Freddy offers devoted affection, while Higgins insists that Eliza has become strong enough to choose her own path. Their unresolved relationship remains charged by mutual dependence, pride, and affection.

The musical explores class, language, gender, and the power society gives to outward appearances. It also asks whether personal transformation can be meaningful without respect, independence, and recognition.

sound of music.en:
In Salzburg, Austria, in 1938, Maria Rainer is an impulsive postulant at Nonnberg Abbey whose love of the hills and music makes convent discipline difficult. The Mother Abbess sends her to serve as governess to the seven children of the widowed Captain Georg von Trapp: Liesl, Friedrich, Louisa, Kurt, Brigitta, Marta, and Gretl. At the Captain’s household, Maria encounters rigid rules and children who initially test every new governess. Rather than punish them, she earns their trust through games, kindness, and singing, bringing warmth and laughter into a home shaped by grief and the Captain’s strict military manner.

Captain von Trapp is preparing to marry the wealthy Baroness Elsa Schraeder, encouraged by his friend Max Detweiler, who sees commercial potential in the children’s musical talent. Maria realizes that she has fallen in love with the Captain and retreats to the Abbey, believing she should return to religious life. The Mother Abbess counsels her to face her feelings honestly. Maria returns to the von Trapp home, where the Captain acknowledges his love for her; he ends his engagement to Elsa, and he and Maria marry.

During their honeymoon, Austria is annexed by Nazi Germany. On returning to Salzburg, the family learns that the Captain has been ordered to accept a commission in the German Navy. A principled Austrian patriot, he refuses. Max arranges for the family to perform at the Salzburg Festival, allowing them a chance to evade the authorities. After their appearance, the von Trapps escape through the Abbey, where the nuns help conceal them from pursuing soldiers. They flee into the mountains toward Switzerland, leaving their home behind rather than submit to the Nazi regime.

The musical explores the transforming power of love, music, and chosen family. It also sets private courage against political oppression, showing that moral conviction may require sacrifice and a leap into an uncertain future.

mary poppins.en:
In Edwardian London, the troubled Banks household lives at Cherry Tree Lane, where the children, Jane and Michael, long for warmth and attention from their busy, demanding father, George Banks. Their mother, Winifred, is preoccupied with finding a meaningful role beyond domestic life, while the household is run by the weary Mrs Brill and the loyal but anxious Robertson Ay. After yet another nanny leaves, Jane and Michael advertise for one who is kind, adventurous, and able to understand children. Into their lives flies Mary Poppins, an extraordinary nanny who takes charge with confidence, practicality, and a touch of magic. She is accompanied, often unwillingly, by her cheerful friend Bert, a jack-of-all-trades who observes the family’s difficulties with affection.

Mary leads Jane and Michael through remarkable adventures: toys come to life, statues dance, and ordinary outings become fantastical journeys. Yet her purpose is not merely to entertain them. She challenges the children to see the world differently and pushes George to recognize that his rigid devotion to work has distanced him from his family. George’s frustration grows after a disastrous visit involving the children and his employer, Mr Northbrook, at the bank. Convinced that his position and reputation have been ruined, he faces the collapse of the ordered life he has built.

As George confronts his failures, Mary helps the family rediscover the value of imagination, compassion, and shared time. Winifred begins to reconcile her public ambitions with her love for her family, while Jane and Michael gain greater confidence and understanding. When the Banks family finally comes together, George sees that success means more than professional advancement. Mary Poppins, knowing her work is done, prepares to leave Cherry Tree Lane, leaving the household changed but capable of continuing without her.

The musical explores the importance of family connection, emotional presence, and seeing wonder in everyday life. It suggests that people can change when they choose love, imagination, and human relationships over pride, routine, and ambition.

oklahoma.en:
Set in the Oklahoma Territory just before statehood, Oklahoma! begins on a bright morning at Aunt Eller’s farm, where cowboy Curly McLain arrives to ask Laurey Williams to the box social. Laurey is attracted to Curly but refuses to admit it, especially after he boasts about taking her in a handsome new surrey. To provoke him, she agrees to attend with Jud Fry, the brooding hired hand who lives in the smokehouse and has long fixated on her. At the same time, cowboy Will Parker hopes to marry the lively Ado Annie, but her father, Andrew Carnes, insists that Will must first prove he can support a wife. Will returns from Kansas City with money from selling his saddle and a host of extravagant stories, only to learn that Ado Annie has become entangled with Ali Hakim, a travelling peddler. Although Ali is eager to escape, he finds himself pressed toward marriage until Will’s determination and Ado Annie’s affection for him help resolve the confusion.

At the box social, rivalry over Laurey erupts into an auction for her picnic basket. Curly and Jud bid fiercely, and Curly wins, humiliating Jud before the community. Laurey begins to recognize both Curly’s sincerity and the danger in Jud’s jealousy. Afterward, she dreams of a future in which her hopes for love are threatened by Jud’s menacing presence. Curly later asks Laurey to marry him, and she accepts. On their wedding day, Jud arrives and tries to disrupt the celebration. He attacks Curly, but in the struggle Jud falls on his own knife and dies. Curly is briefly put on trial, where the gathered settlers defend him and he is acquitted. The newly married Curly and Laurey ride away together as the community celebrates the birth of a shared future.

The musical explores love tested by pride, jealousy, and uncertainty, alongside the humor and warmth of a close-knit frontier community. Its central theme is the movement from individual conflict toward belonging, optimism, and a new beginning.

funny girl.en:
Set in New York City during the rise of vaudeville and the Ziegfeld Follies, Funny Girl follows the determined, unconventional Fanny Brice as she pursues stardom despite being told that she is neither beautiful nor refined enough for the stage. From her modest beginnings in Brooklyn, Fanny’s comic instincts, powerful voice, and refusal to conform propel her toward increasingly prominent theatrical opportunities. Her mother, Rose Brice, and her loyal friend, Mrs. Brice’s poker-playing circle, offer support as Fanny navigates the excitement and insecurity of show business. At a party following one of her early successes, Fanny meets the handsome, sophisticated gambler Nick Arnstein. Though their worlds seem very different, they are immediately drawn to one another.

Fanny’s talent brings her to Florenz Ziegfeld’s extravagant Follies, where she becomes a celebrated star by turning even her assigned glamorous routines into distinctive comic triumphs. Nick re-enters her life, and their romance deepens despite his unease over Fanny’s growing fame and their unequal financial circumstances. They marry and begin a life that appears charmed, with Fanny’s career flourishing and the couple welcoming a daughter. Yet Nick struggles to establish himself in business and gambling ventures, while Fanny tries to protect him from humiliation by offering financial help. His pride prevents him from accepting it easily.

As Nick’s losses accumulate, he becomes involved in a risky bond scheme that collapses, leading to his arrest and imprisonment. Fanny remains fiercely devoted, using her success and money to support him, but their relationship cannot escape the strain created by his wounded pride and her public success. When Nick is released, he recognizes that he cannot remain in the marriage under those conditions. Fanny faces the prospect of losing him while returning to the stage, where she must transform personal heartbreak into performance.

The musical explores ambition, self-invention, and the cost of pursuing love alongside independence. It contrasts Fanny’s resilient confidence with the pressures that success and traditional expectations place on a relationship.

music man.en:
In July 1912, smooth-talking con man Professor Harold Hill arrives in River City, Iowa, intending to run his familiar swindle. He warns the townspeople that a new pool table will corrupt their boys, then offers the remedy: a boys’ band. Although he cannot read music or play an instrument, he sells the families uniforms, instruments, and an “instruction method,” planning to disappear with the proceeds before anyone expects a rehearsal. His old associate Marcellus Washburn, now settled in River City, helps him navigate the town and its suspicious Mayor George Shinn.

Hill’s greatest obstacle is Marian Paroo, the guarded town librarian and piano teacher. She immediately doubts his credentials and seeks proof that he is a fraud. Hill tries to charm her, but Marian resists, particularly when he makes grand claims about a “Think System” that supposedly teaches children to play simply by imagining the music. Meanwhile, he wins over the town: the quarrelsome school board becomes a singing barbershop quartet, local ladies find new purpose in civic projects, and young Tommy Djilas and Zaneeta Shinn grow closer.

Hill’s interest in Marian becomes sincere after meeting her shy younger brother, Winthrop, who is painfully self-conscious about his lisp. By presenting Winthrop with a cornet and treating him as a valued future bandsman, Hill gives the boy confidence and a sense of belonging. Marian begins to see that, even if Hill’s methods are dishonest, the hope he has stirred in the community is real. When Charlie Cowell, a traveling salesman who knows Hill’s past, arrives to expose him, Marian receives evidence of Hill’s deception but hesitates to use it.

At the Fourth of July celebration, the truth finally reaches River City. The townspeople confront Hill just as the children are meant to perform. Rather than flee, he faces them. The boys’ band produces a ragged but spirited performance, and Winthrop proudly plays among them. Moved by what Hill has brought to their children and their town, the people choose forgiveness, while Marian and Hill are united.

42nd street.en:
In 1933, wide-eyed Peggy Sawyer arrives in New York City from Allentown, Pennsylvania, hoping to find work on Broadway. She misses the initial audition for Pretty Lady, a lavish new musical directed by the formidable Julian Marsh, but the show’s juvenile lead, Billy Lawlor, notices her talent and helps her get a chance. Though impatient with her lateness and inexperience, Marsh ultimately puts Peggy in the chorus. As rehearsals intensify, she befriends the other dancers and develops a shy attraction to Billy, while beginning to learn the hard realities behind the glamour of the theatre.

Pretty Lady has problems of its own. Its leading lady, Dorothy Brock, is a fading star whose wealthy lover, Abner Dillon, is financing the production largely to keep her in the spotlight. Dorothy, however, is unhappy with Abner and still loves Pat Denning, her former partner. Her personal turmoil erupts during the company’s Philadelphia tryout, where tensions over money, jealousy, and the future of the production threaten to bring the show down. Peggy, caught up in the excitement and confusion, accidentally knocks Dorothy over during the performance. Dorothy’s ankle is broken, and Marsh angrily dismisses Peggy while declaring that the production is finished.

The company refuses to surrender. Realising that Peggy may be the only performer capable of replacing Dorothy, Marsh races to the station to stop her from returning home. He persuades the frightened young dancer to come back and take on the leading role, despite having only thirty-six hours to master songs, scenes, and demanding dance routines. Under enormous pressure, Peggy transforms from an unknown chorus girl into a poised leading lady. When Pretty Lady finally opens on Broadway, she triumphs, and the company celebrates both the hit show and the making of a new star.

The musical celebrates perseverance, collective effort, and the exhilaration of theatrical creation. It also contrasts Broadway’s glittering promise with the vulnerability, rivalry, and hard work beneath the footlights.

a chorus line.en:
At a Broadway theatre in New York City, a group of seventeen hopeful dancers arrives for the final stage of an audition for a new musical. The director, Zach, and his assistant, Larry, need to reduce the group to a chorus line of eight performers—four men and four women. Rather than simply judging technique, Zach asks the dancers to reveal who they are and why they chose this demanding career. At first guarded and competitive, they gradually begin to share deeply personal memories while rehearsing combinations and waiting for the decision that could change their lives.

Cassie, an experienced dancer who once had a romantic relationship with Zach, returns to the chorus after an unsuccessful attempt to become a star. She asks Zach for another chance, but he worries that her experience and emotional history make her unsuitable for a place in the ensemble. Elsewhere, Sheila describes growing up with an absent father and a difficult home life; Bebe recalls discovering dance as a refuge from loneliness; and Maggie tells of leaving home at a young age to pursue a dream that gradually became her entire identity. Paul, initially reserved, gives the most painful account: rejected and humiliated by his family after exploring his sexuality and performing in a drag club, he found safety and purpose in dance.

The audition is interrupted when Paul injures his knee during a routine. As he is taken away, the remaining dancers confront the possibility that their ambitions can be ended suddenly by circumstance. Zach ultimately makes his choices, dismissing some dancers and selecting the eight who will form the chorus. Cassie is among them. The chosen performers change into identical gold costumes and join the other dancers in a dazzling final number, no longer presented as separate individuals but as one perfectly synchronized line.

The musical explores ambition, identity, vulnerability, and the sacrifices demanded by a life in performance. It celebrates individual stories while also questioning what is lost when artists must become interchangeable parts of a larger spectacle.

wiz.en:
The Wiz reimagines The Wizard of Oz through an all-Black cast and a soul, R&B, and gospel score. Dorothy Gale, a young girl from Kansas, longs for a life beyond the limits of home but is frightened by the demands of growing up. When a tornado carries her and Toto to the Land of Oz, their house lands on Evillene’s sister, the Wicked Witch of the East, freeing the Munchkins from her rule. Addaperle, the Good Witch of the North, gives Dorothy the protective silver shoes and directs her along the Yellow Brick Road to the Emerald City, where the mighty Wiz may know how to send her home.

On the road, Dorothy rescues Scarecrow from a flock of crows; he joins her hoping the Wiz will give him a brain. They meet Tin Man, who wants a heart, and Lion, whose bravado conceals deep fear and who seeks courage. The four companions survive a deadly poppy field and other obstacles before reaching the Emerald City. There, the Wiz promises to grant their wishes only if they destroy Evillene, the Wicked Witch of the West.

The group enters Evillene’s domain, where she enslaves the Winkies in her factory. Evillene sends the Winged Monkeys after Dorothy, takes the silver shoes, and threatens to destroy her. Dorothy accidentally melts Evillene with water, releasing the Winkies, who rejoice in their freedom. Back in the Emerald City, the Wiz reveals that he is not a supernatural ruler but an ordinary man who has relied on spectacle and fear. Even so, he helps Scarecrow, Tin Man, and Lion recognize the intelligence, compassion, and courage they have already displayed. Glinda, the Good Witch of the South, finally tells Dorothy that the silver shoes have always held the means for her return. Dorothy uses them to go home, newly able to face life with confidence.

The show celebrates self-belief: its travelers discover that the qualities they seek are already within them. It also values friendship, liberation from oppression, and the courage to make one’s own way home.

joseph and the amazing technicolor dream.en:
Joseph, the favoured son of Jacob, is given a magnificent coat of many colours, provoking jealousy among his eleven brothers. Troubled by Joseph’s dreams, in which he foresees himself elevated above his family, the brothers plot to get rid of him. They seize Joseph, tear away his coat, and sell him to Ishmaelites travelling to Egypt. To conceal their crime, they smear the coat with goat’s blood and convince Jacob that Joseph has been killed by a wild animal. Jacob is devastated, while Joseph is taken far from home into an uncertain future.

In Egypt, Joseph is purchased by the wealthy Potiphar and rises quickly in his household. His success attracts the attention of Mrs Potiphar, who attempts to seduce him. When Joseph rejects her, she accuses him of misconduct, and Potiphar has him imprisoned. Even in prison, however, Joseph’s ability to interpret dreams brings him recognition. He correctly explains the dreams of Pharaoh’s Butler and Pharaoh’s Baker: the Butler will be restored to favour, while the Baker will be executed. The Butler is freed but initially forgets Joseph.

Two years later, Pharaoh is disturbed by dreams no one can explain. The Butler remembers Joseph, who is brought before Pharaoh and interprets the visions as a warning: Egypt will enjoy seven years of abundance followed by seven years of devastating famine. Impressed, Pharaoh appoints Joseph as his chief administrator. Joseph prepares Egypt, storing grain during the prosperous years so that the country can survive the famine.

When hunger reaches Canaan, Joseph’s brothers travel to Egypt seeking food. They do not recognise the powerful official standing before them, but Joseph recognises them. He tests their remorse and demands that they return with Benjamin, Jacob’s youngest son. After a tense final test involving a silver cup, Joseph reveals his identity. His brothers are overwhelmed with fear and guilt, but Joseph forgives them, and the family is reunited in Egypt.

The musical explores jealousy, betrayal, resilience, and forgiveness. It celebrates the possibility of transformation: suffering and separation give way to reconciliation, family renewal, and hope.

kinky boots.en:
In a struggling Northampton shoe factory, Charlie Price returns home after the sudden death of his father, believing he is only there to settle the estate before resuming his planned life in London with his fiancée, Nicola. Instead, he discovers that Price & Son is close to bankruptcy. The loyal workers, including factory manager Don and employee Lauren, face losing their jobs, while Charlie feels unprepared to inherit either the business or his father’s expectations. A chance encounter in London changes the course of his life: Charlie meets Lola, a charismatic drag performer whose glamorous high-heeled boots are too fragile to withstand the weight and movement of a man.

Recognizing an overlooked market, Charlie asks Lola to help transform the factory into a producer of sturdy, stylish boots for drag performers. Lola agrees, arriving in Northampton with her troupe, the Angels, and challenging the factory’s conservative culture. Her confidence clashes especially with Don’s hostility, but Lola also reveals a more vulnerable side: as Simon, she has endured rejection from her boxer father and still longs for acceptance. Charlie, meanwhile, struggles to lead the workers and to meet the demands of an upcoming Milan fashion show, where the factory must present its new collection or lose its last chance at survival.

As the deadline approaches, financial pressure and personal conflict divide the team. Charlie insults Lola during an argument, driving her away, and several workers abandon the project. Lauren confronts Charlie about the man he has become, while Nicola realizes that Northampton and the factory now matter to him more than their London future. Charlie recognizes his mistakes, asks for forgiveness, and chooses to continue the fight. The workers return, Lola reclaims her place beside Charlie, and Price & Son unveils its distinctive boots in Milan. Their success saves the factory, bringing its workers, Charlie, and Lola into a renewed sense of purpose and belonging.

The show explores self-acceptance, courage, and the freedom to live honestly despite other people’s expectations. It also celebrates empathy and collaboration, showing how a community can change when people recognize each other’s worth.

sister act.en:
In Philadelphia, Deloris Van Cartier is a brash, ambitious nightclub singer who dreams of becoming a star. When her gangster boyfriend, Curtis Shank, fails to deliver the glamorous future she expects, she decides to leave him. Before she can escape, however, Deloris witnesses Curtis and his henchmen commit a murder. Fearing for her life, she turns to the police and is placed under the protection of Officer Eddie Souther, a former schoolmate whose feelings for her soon reawaken.

Eddie hides Deloris in the last place Curtis would think to look: a struggling convent. Disguised as a nun and renamed Sister Mary Clarence, Deloris clashes immediately with the stern Mother Superior, who fears that the newcomer’s flamboyance will disrupt the sisters’ quiet, disciplined life. The convent’s choir is painfully out of tune, but Deloris sees an opportunity. Taking charge of the singers, she turns their timid hymns into energetic, joyful performances. Sister Mary Patrick embraces the transformation, Sister Mary Lazarus discovers a new confidence, and the shy Sister Mary Robert gradually finds the courage to let her powerful voice be heard.

The choir’s success attracts crowds to the church and brings hope to the convent, delighting Monsignor O’Hara but alarming Mother Superior, who believes the attention may expose Deloris. As Curtis’s men close in, Deloris must decide whether to flee once more or stand with the women who have become her friends. When Curtis abducts her, the sisters refuse to abandon her. Their rescue effort leads to a confrontation in which Deloris faces Curtis directly, while Eddie and the police finally bring the gangster’s crimes to an end. Safe at last, Deloris chooses to remain connected to the convent and its newly revitalised community.

The musical celebrates friendship, courage, and the strength found in unexpected communities. It also explores self-belief: Deloris and the sisters learn that each can find a voice, a purpose, and a place to belong.

shrek.en:
In a faraway kingdom, Shrek, a gruff green ogre, is sent away from his parents on his seventh birthday and grows up alone in a swamp, content to frighten anyone who comes near. His isolation is interrupted when Lord Farquaad, the ruler of Duloc, banishes the kingdom’s fairy-tale creatures to Shrek’s land. Wanting his swamp back, Shrek confronts Farquaad, who agrees to remove the exiles only if Shrek rescues Princess Fiona from a dragon-guarded tower and brings her to Duloc so Farquaad can marry her and become king.

Shrek reluctantly sets off with Donkey, an irrepressibly talkative animal who quickly decides they are friends. They reach the castle, where Shrek rescues Fiona from Dragon’s keep. Fiona is surprised that her saviour is an ogre rather than the handsome prince she expected, but she joins the journey to Duloc. Along the way, she and Shrek gradually discover warmth, humour, and vulnerability in one another. Yet Fiona conceals a secret: every night at sunset, she turns into an ogress because of a curse, and she believes only a kiss from her true love can restore her to the beautiful human princess she thinks she must be.

As Shrek prepares to leave Fiona with Farquaad, Donkey discovers her transformation and learns of the curse. Fiona overhears Shrek, who has misunderstood part of her conversation with Donkey and assumes she finds him repulsive. Hurt, Shrek withdraws and delivers her to Farquaad. On their wedding day, Shrek realizes that his feelings for Fiona are real and races to Duloc with Donkey and Dragon. He interrupts the ceremony just before sunset. Fiona transforms before Farquaad, who rejects her, but Shrek declares his love and kisses her. The curse is broken, leaving Fiona permanently in her ogress form; she accepts herself, and the fairy-tale exiles reclaim their freedom.

The show explores self-acceptance, belonging, and the courage to be loved as one truly is. It also challenges narrow ideas of beauty and celebrates friendship, compassion, and choosing one’s own happy ending.

charlie and the chocolate factory.en:
Charlie Bucket lives in a tiny house on the edge of town with his parents and four grandparents, where food is scarce but imagination is plentiful. Across the way stands Willy Wonka’s mysterious chocolate factory, sealed off from the public for years. When Wonka announces that five Golden Tickets have been hidden in chocolate bars, each granting a child a tour of the factory and an extraordinary prize, Charlie dreams of finding one despite his family’s poverty. The other ticket winners are the greedy Augustus Gloop, the spoiled Veruca Salt, the television-obsessed Mike Teavee, and the competitive Violet Beauregarde. Against all odds, Charlie discovers the final ticket.

Inside the factory, Wonka leads the children and their families through a dazzling world of edible landscapes, inventive machinery, and Oompa-Loompas. Yet each child’s worst habit becomes their undoing. Augustus cannot resist drinking from the Chocolate River and is sucked into a pipe. Violet insists on chewing an experimental meal-replacement gum, swells into a giant blueberry, and must be rolled away. Veruca demands a trained squirrel for herself, but the squirrels judge her a “bad nut” and send her down a rubbish chute. Mike volunteers to be transmitted by television, only to be shrunk to a tiny size.

Charlie, meanwhile, remains thoughtful and kind, but he faces a difficult test when Wonka’s grand plan becomes clear. Wonka has been searching for a child worthy of inheriting the factory, not merely someone dazzled by its sweets. Charlie’s humility, loyalty to his family, and capacity to care for others distinguish him from the other contestants. He learns that the factory’s wonders carry responsibility as well as delight, and that true fortune is not simply possession, but the chance to use opportunity generously.

The musical explores imagination, temptation, and the consequences of unchecked selfishness. At its heart, it celebrates kindness, family, and the moral strength to remain oneself when offered everything one could want.

producers.en:
In 1959 New York, once-successful Broadway producer Max Bialystock watches his latest disaster, Funny Boy, collapse on opening night. Desperate for a comeback, he meets Leo Bloom, a nervous accountant sent to inspect Max’s books. Leo notices that a dishonest producer could theoretically raise more money than a show needs, oversell shares, and profit if the production closes immediately—because no one would be left to demand returns. Max sees the possibility at once and persuades the reluctant Leo to become his partner.

Calling themselves Bialystock & Bloom, they set out to create the worst musical Broadway has ever seen. Their search leads them to Franz Liebkind, the eccentric author of Springtime for Hitler, an appallingly sincere celebration of Hitler and Nazi Germany. They secure the rights, charm and deceive a succession of wealthy elderly investors, and hire the flamboyant Roger De Bris and his assistant Carmen Ghia to direct. For the female lead, they engage Ulla, a glamorous Swedish performer who catches Leo’s attention and inspires him to grow more confident.

Everything seems designed for catastrophe. Yet during the opening performance, the audience interprets the extravagantly tasteless material as outrageous satire. Rather than recoiling, the public embraces it, and Springtime for Hitler becomes an enormous hit. Max and Leo’s plan collapses: their oversold shares leave them accountable to countless investors, while success brings scrutiny instead of the easy escape they expected.

As panic rises, Leo dreams of running away with Ulla, but Max refuses to abandon the show or their partnership. Their fraud is exposed, and they face trial. Leo accepts responsibility, while Max’s loyalty to his friend finally outweighs his hunger for money and acclaim. The two are imprisoned, where their irrepressible theatrical instincts lead them to stage another show—and ultimately begin again.

avenue q.en:
Princeton, a recent graduate with a B.A. in English and no clear direction, arrives in New York searching for an affordable home and a purpose. He finds both uncertainty and a room on Avenue Q, a shabby block inhabited by an eccentric community: idealistic kindergarten assistant Kate Monster; closeted banker Rod and his relaxed roommate Nicky; struggling comedian Brian and his fiancée, aspiring therapist Christmas Eve; internet-obsessed recluse Trekkie Monster; and building superintendent Gary Coleman. Princeton and Kate are immediately drawn to one another, while the neighbours commiserate over their stalled careers, money problems, loneliness, and difficult ambitions.

Kate dreams of opening a school for Monsters, but her job is precarious and her employer, Mrs. Lavinia Thistletwat, dismisses her aspirations. Brian tries to establish himself as a comedian, Christmas Eve struggles to build a therapy practice, and Nicky gently presses Rod to acknowledge what Rod refuses to admit about himself. Princeton’s insecurity complicates his romance with Kate. After a brief relationship with Lucy, an alluring newcomer encouraged by the Bad Idea Bears, Princeton distances himself from Kate and leaves Avenue Q to seek a grander destiny.

His search produces little except disappointment. Meanwhile, Kate’s hope of founding her school collapses when her savings are stolen by Trekkie Monster. The setbacks force the residents to confront their fears and the ways they have hurt one another. Princeton returns, helps the neighbours recover Kate’s money, and recognizes that purpose need not arrive as a single dramatic revelation. Kate and Princeton reconcile, Brian finds an opportunity to perform, and Rod finally allows himself a measure of honesty and connection. The community, still imperfect and still struggling, faces the future together.

The show explores the uneasy passage into adulthood: work, desire, identity, friendship, and the pressure to discover a meaningful life. Its central idea is that hardship and uncertainty are temporary, while mutual support can make them bearable.

rock of ages.en:
In 1987, on Los Angeles’s Sunset Strip, aspiring rock singer Drew Boley works as a barback at the Bourbon Room, a celebrated but financially troubled rock club owned by Dennis Dupree. Drew dreams of becoming a star and falls for Sherrie Christian, a young woman newly arrived from Kansas with hopes of making it in Hollywood. He gets her a job as a waitress at the Bourbon Room, and their mutual attraction grows amid the club’s raucous nightlife. Dennis’s venue, however, faces demolition: German developers Hertz Klinemann and his son Franz plan to replace it with a sterile retail development, aided by the ambitious city official Regina Koontz, who publicly campaigns against the Strip’s supposed moral decay.

The Bourbon Room’s last hope is a farewell concert by Stacee Jaxx, the wildly successful but self-absorbed frontman of Arsenal, who began his career there. Stacee’s manager, Paul Gill, arranges the appearance while quietly navigating the singer’s unpredictable behavior. At the club, Stacee seduces Sherrie, and Drew sees enough to believe she has betrayed him. Hurt and furious, he leaves the Bourbon Room and joins a boy band, abandoning his rock ambitions. Sherrie, ashamed and desperate after losing her job, becomes involved with strip-club owner Justice Charlier, who offers her protection and work.

As the developers move closer to destroying the Bourbon Room, Franz unexpectedly rejects his father’s plans after falling in love with Regina. Their romance transforms both of them, and Regina turns against the demolition scheme. Meanwhile, Drew and Sherrie confront the misunderstanding that separated them and rediscover their feelings. On the night of the final concert, Stacee reunites with Arsenal, and the Bourbon Room becomes the setting for a last, defiant celebration of the Sunset Strip. The threat to the club is defeated, and Drew and Sherrie embrace a future together while the music continues.

At its heart, Rock of Ages celebrates perseverance, love, and the courage to pursue a dream despite disappointment. It also pits individuality, community, and unruly rock-and-roll spirit against conformity, greed, and commercial destruction.

once.en:
In Dublin, a Guy who repairs vacuum cleaners by day plays heartfelt songs on his guitar in the evenings, but he has nearly given up performing after a painful breakup. One night on Grafton Street, a spirited young Czech woman, known simply as Girl, hears him sing and stops to challenge him: she recognizes the value of his music and refuses to let him abandon it. Though she is married and has a young daughter, Ivanka, living in the Czech Republic, Girl forms an immediate artistic connection with Guy. She brings him to her home, where she plays piano, and they begin writing music together.

Girl persuades Guy to retrieve his guitar from the shop where he sold it, then introduces him to a group of talented musicians. As they rehearse and arrange Guy’s songs, their informal gathering grows into a band. Guy’s father and the friends around them offer support, while Guy confronts lingering feelings for his former girlfriend in New York. Encouraged by Girl’s determination, he begins to believe his music could lead somewhere beyond the streets of Dublin.

The group books time at a recording studio, hoping to make a demo that will attract interest from America. During the recording sessions, Guy and Girl’s emotional intimacy deepens through their shared work, even as they avoid acting on their feelings. Guy considers travelling to New York to reconcile with his ex-girlfriend, while Girl works toward bringing her husband and daughter to Dublin so that her own family can be reunited. Their affection becomes inseparable from the songs they create, yet both recognize the obligations and lives that lie beyond their brief collaboration.

When the recording is complete, Guy prepares to pursue a new future in New York. Before leaving, he gives Girl a piano, an extravagant gift that acknowledges what she has given his music and his confidence. Girl, in turn, has helped him find the courage to move forward. They part without becoming a conventional couple, carrying the impact of their connection into separate futures.

The musical explores how creativity can restore a person’s sense of possibility after loss. It treats love not only as romance, but as a generous, temporary connection that can change two people’s lives.

next to normal.en:
In suburban America, Diana Goodman appears to be a devoted wife and mother, managing the routines of family life with her husband, Dan, their high-achieving daughter Natalie, and the seemingly cheerful teenage son, Gabe. Yet Diana’s reality is fractured by bipolar disorder, recurring depression, and the enduring trauma of a tragedy that occurred years earlier. She experiences visions of Gabe and struggles to distinguish memory from the present, while Dan tries desperately to preserve the image of a stable, loving household. As Diana’s condition worsens, she undergoes psychiatric treatment, including medication changes, therapy, and eventually electroconvulsive therapy. The treatment alters her memories but cannot fully erase the grief and unease embedded in her life.

Natalie, meanwhile, feels invisible beside her mother’s illness and her father’s constant vigilance. She throws herself into academic achievement, then finds a tenuous refuge with Henry, a kind, persistent schoolmate who sees beyond her guarded exterior. Their growing relationship is strained by Natalie’s anxiety, her need for control, and the emotional distance within the Goodman home. Diana begins to recover fragments of the past and confronts the family secret: Gabe died as an infant, and the son she has continued to see is a manifestation of grief and unresolved loss. Dan has long supported Diana’s belief in Gabe’s presence, unable to release either his son or the version of his marriage built around caring for Diana.

As memories return, Diana realizes that treatment alone cannot restore the life she and Dan once imagined. She chooses to leave the household temporarily to seek a future defined by her own stability rather than by illness, guilt, or dependence. Dan is left to face his grief without the role of caretaker, while Natalie begins to accept support from Henry and to make space for a life not wholly shaped by her family’s pain.

The musical examines mental illness, bereavement, memory, and the complicated ways families survive loss. It asks whether healing means forgetting, enduring, accepting help, or learning to live honestly with what cannot be repaired.

pippin.en:
A troupe of Players, led by the charismatic Leading Player, invites the audience to watch the story of Pippin, the eldest son of King Charlemagne. Fresh from the University of Padua, Pippin returns home determined to find an extraordinary purpose. His father offers him a place in battle, but Pippin finds warfare brutal and empty. He then pursues pleasure at the urging of his grandmother, Berthe, who embraces a carefree life in the countryside; yet this, too, leaves him dissatisfied. At court, Pippin becomes entangled in the ambitions of his stepmother, Fastrada, who wants her son Lewis to inherit the throne. She persuades Pippin that Charlemagne must be removed, and Pippin joins a plot against his father. When Charlemagne survives and Pippin unexpectedly takes power, he discovers that ruling is exhausting, messy, and impossible to do perfectly. Disillusioned, he gives the crown back to Charlemagne and wanders away without a direction.

Catherine, a widow who runs an estate and raises her young son Theo, finds Pippin despondent by the road and brings him home. Pippin gradually becomes close to Catherine and Theo, learning to value the rhythms of ordinary work, affection, and family life. Although he loves them, he fears that such a modest existence means he has failed to become extraordinary. He leaves, returning to the Leading Player and the Players, who promise him a spectacular final act: by stepping into a blazing display, he can achieve the ultimate, immortal fulfillment. Pippin approaches the moment of sacrifice, but Catherine and Theo interrupt. He refuses the Players’ prescribed ending and chooses Catherine instead. The troupe abandons them, taking away the theatrical world’s lights and illusions, but Pippin and Catherine remain together in the dark, ready to make their own uncertain future.

The musical explores the tension between grand ambition and everyday happiness. It questions seductive promises of glory, control, and perfect fulfillment, while suggesting that love, choice, and an imperfect shared life can hold deeper meaning.

tina.en:
A gifted young girl growing up in Nutbush, Tennessee, Anna Mae Bullock finds in her powerful voice a means of escape from a difficult home life. After leaving for St. Louis with her sister Alline, Anna Mae meets the ambitious bandleader Ike Turner. He recognizes her talent, renames her Tina Turner, and makes her the star of the Ike & Tina Turner Revue. As the group gains momentum, Tina’s electrifying performances bring success, acclaim, and a new public identity. She and Ike marry, and their career rises through relentless touring, recording, and increasingly prominent appearances.

Behind the glamour, however, Tina’s private life becomes dominated by Ike’s jealousy, manipulation, and violence. He controls the band, their money, and Tina’s choices, while expecting her to continue performing no matter how badly she is treated. Tina endures the pressure for years, trying to protect her children and retain some sense of herself amid the chaos of life on the road. A spiritual encounter and the support of friends give her a different way to see her future, but leaving Ike remains terrifying: he has the power, the contracts, and the name the world knows.

After a violent confrontation, Tina finally runs away with almost nothing. She chooses to keep the name Tina Turner but must rebuild her life from the ground up, facing debt, professional rejection, and uncertainty about whether audiences will accept her without Ike. Determined to define herself on her own terms, she works with manager Roger Davies, experiments with a new musical direction, and returns to the stage with a bold image and renewed confidence. Her comeback grows from small opportunities into international success, culminating in a triumphant performance that confirms she has reclaimed both her career and her independence.

The show is about survival, self-belief, and the struggle to reclaim identity from control and abuse. It celebrates resilience, personal freedom, and the transformative power of choosing one’s own future.

tootsie.en:
In present-day New York, gifted but combustible actor Michael Dorsey has become unemployable. After being fired by director Ron Carlisle and rejected at every audition, he vents to his roommate and friend, Jeff Slater, while their former girlfriend, struggling actress Sandy Lester, faces the same bleak prospects. When Michael learns that Sandy is auditioning for the role of the Nurse in Juliet’s Nurse, a Broadway-bound musical built around Shakespearean characters, desperation gives him an idea. Transforming himself into the poised, determined “Dorothy Michaels,” he auditions for producer Rita Marshall and wins the role that eluded Sandy.

Dorothy quickly proves far more successful than Michael has ever been. In rehearsal, she challenges Ron’s shallow, chaotic conception of the show and helps reshape the Nurse into a vivid leading character. Juliet’s Nurse becomes a hit, and Dorothy becomes an overnight Broadway sensation. Yet the new career brings complications. Dorothy forms a close friendship with the show’s leading lady, Julie Nichols, whose intelligence and independence deeply affect Michael. Michael falls in love with Julie but cannot honestly pursue her while living as Dorothy. Meanwhile, self-absorbed co-star Max Van Horn becomes romantically interested in Dorothy, and Jeff watches with growing alarm as Michael’s deception expands beyond anything either of them can manage.

As the production reaches its triumph, Michael’s double life threatens his relationships and his conscience. He recognizes that Dorothy’s success has given him a perspective he lacked: he has listened differently, treated women’s experiences with greater respect, and discovered the damage caused by using another identity to avoid his own failures. At a crucial performance, he abandons the disguise and publicly reveals that Dorothy Michaels is Michael Dorsey. The disclosure shocks the company, jeopardizes the show, and wounds Julie, who must decide whether Michael’s change is real. Michael accepts the consequences, apologizes without excuses, and begins trying to rebuild his life and relationships as himself.

The musical explores identity, ambition, honesty, and the cost of treating other people as means to an end. It follows Michael’s movement from self-absorption toward accountability, empathy, and the courage to be known without a disguise.

anastasia.en:
In 1906, the Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna leaves Saint Petersburg for Paris, comforting her young granddaughter, Grand Duchess Anastasia, with a music box and a promise that they will meet again. Eleven years later, revolution overturns the Romanovs’ world. During a ball at the palace, the family attempts to flee the Bolsheviks; Anastasia returns for the music box and is separated from them. News reaches Maria in Paris that the imperial family has been killed.

In 1927, Saint Petersburg—now renamed Leningrad—is tense, impoverished, and full of rumours that Anastasia survived. Dmitry, a resourceful con man, and Vlad Popov, a former member of the Imperial Court, decide to find a convincing young woman, present her as the lost Grand Duchess, and collect Maria’s reward. Their search leads them to Anya, an amnesiac street sweeper determined to travel to Paris because fragments of memory draw her there. Her resemblance to Anastasia and her unexplained knowledge of the old court persuade the two men to train her for their deception.

As Anya, Dmitry, and Vlad travel west, Anya learns the manners, history, and memories expected of a princess, while her connection with Dmitry deepens. Deputy Commissioner Gleb Vaganov pursues them, driven by his Bolshevik duties and by the legacy of his father, who helped destroy the Romanovs. Yet Gleb becomes increasingly unable to regard Anya merely as a political threat.

In Paris, Vlad reconnects with Countess Lily Malevsky-Malevitch, while Anya seeks an audience with the Dowager Empress. Maria has rejected many impostors and initially refuses to see her. Dmitry finally reaches her by recalling an encounter from the night Anastasia disappeared, then arranges Anya’s meeting with her grandmother. Anya’s memories, the music box, and their shared recognition reunite them. Gleb finds Anya but ultimately lets her live. Although Maria offers Anya a royal future, Anya chooses a life with Dmitry, and the public is told that Anastasia is dead.

starlight express.en:
In a child’s sleeping imagination, a railway world springs to life for a championship to decide the Fastest Engine in the World. Rusty, a modest steam engine, longs to prove himself but is dismissed as outdated by the boastful diesel champion Greaseball and the dazzling electric newcomer Electra. When Pearl, a beautiful first-class observation car, arrives to make her racing debut, Rusty is immediately drawn to her. Pearl likes his warmth and sincerity, yet she also dreams of belonging to a winning train, leaving her susceptible to the glamour and apparent power of his rivals.

The races begin, bringing together engines and coaches from across the railway. Rusty struggles with doubt while Greaseball dominates through swagger, intimidation and dirty tactics. Electra presents himself as the future, using his wealth, technology and entourage to seduce Pearl away from Rusty. Rusty’s friends, including Dinah, Buffy and the older steam engine Poppa, try to sustain his confidence; Poppa urges him to remember the mysterious Starlight Express, a force that represents belief beyond mere machinery.

Rusty is repeatedly humiliated and left without a partner. Pearl chooses Greaseball for the decisive contest, only to discover that his hunger for victory matters more to him than loyalty. The final race turns perilous as Greaseball and Electra’s schemes bring disaster to the competitors. With Pearl stranded and the others beaten or betrayed, Rusty must face the race alone. At his lowest point, he calls upon the Starlight Express and learns that the strength he seeks is already within him. Renewed by faith in himself, he races through the darkness, survives the dangers set before him and defeats both Greaseball and Electra.

Rusty finds Pearl rather than simply celebrating his victory, and she recognizes the courage and kindness she had overlooked. Together, they become the train Pearl had been searching for.

little mermaid.en:
In a kingdom beneath the sea, Ariel, the youngest daughter of King Triton, longs to know the human world beyond the ocean’s surface. Fascinated by objects salvaged from shipwrecks, she secretly visits Scuttle, a well-meaning seagull who offers wildly inaccurate explanations of human life. During a storm, Ariel sees Prince Eric aboard a ship and falls instantly in love. When the vessel is wrecked, she rescues Eric from drowning and brings him ashore, singing to him before disappearing. Eric survives, determined to find the mysterious girl with the beautiful voice.

Ariel’s desire to live among humans brings her into conflict with Triton, who forbids contact with the surface world and destroys her collection of human treasures. Devastated, Ariel turns to Ursula, the Sea Witch. Ursula offers Ariel a bargain: she will transform Ariel into a human for three days, but Ariel must surrender her voice. If Ariel receives “true love’s kiss” from Eric before the third sunset, she will remain human; otherwise, she will belong to Ursula forever.

On land, Ariel meets Eric, who is drawn to her despite her inability to speak. With help from Sebastian, Flounder, and Scuttle, she learns to move through the human world, while Eric begins to care for her. Ursula interferes by transforming herself into Vanessa, a beautiful woman who uses Ariel’s stolen voice to enchant Eric. Believing Vanessa is the girl who saved him, Eric prepares to marry her.

Ariel and her friends expose Ursula’s deception, and Ariel’s voice is restored. But the deadline has passed, and Ursula claims Ariel. Triton sacrifices his own freedom to save his daughter, giving Ursula control of the sea. Ariel and Eric refuse to surrender, and together with Ariel’s friends they confront Ursula. Her power is broken, Triton is restored, and Ariel is finally allowed to become human and marry Eric.

The musical explores the courage to pursue one’s identity and dreams, even when they challenge family expectations and familiar boundaries. It also celebrates love, sacrifice, and the possibility of understanding between very different worlds.

and juliet.en:
At the first performance of William Shakespeare’s new tragedy, Anne Hathaway objects to the ending and insists that Juliet deserves another possibility. In their newly improvised version, Juliet wakes in Verona’s tomb beside Romeo’s body but chooses life. When her parents decide she must be sent to a convent, she escapes for Paris with her Nurse, Angelique, and her friend May. Anne writes herself into the adventure as April, while Shakespeare continually tries to steer the tale back toward the romance and suffering he considers more dramatic.

In Paris, Juliet discovers an exhilarating world beyond the life that had been planned for her. At a lavish party she meets François Du Bois, a gentle young man pressured by his father, Lance, to marry suitably or enter the military. François is drawn to Juliet’s boldness, and Juliet enjoys the prospect of a new love; yet she soon realizes that being rescued by another romance is not the same as choosing her own future. May, meanwhile, feels constrained by the roles and language imposed on them, and finds a growing connection with François. Angelique reunites with Lance, whose stern public manner masks unresolved feelings and a warmer, more vulnerable self.

The writers’ dispute becomes inseparable from the characters’ struggles. Shakespeare introduces complications, including Romeo’s unexpected return, hoping Juliet will resume the love story he envisioned. Anne pushes back, defending Juliet’s right to determine her own ending. Juliet must confront what she truly wants—not merely which person she should choose—and she ultimately rejects the narrow choices others have set before her. François and May acknowledge their feelings, Angelique and Lance find a renewed chance at happiness, and Anne claims a fuller voice in shaping both the story and her marriage. Juliet finally steps forward alone, ready to live on her own terms.

The show centres on self-determination, second chances, and the courage to outgrow expectations. It treats love as meaningful but insists that identity, friendship, and personal agency need not be sacrificed for romance.

mj.en:
In Los Angeles in 1992, Michael Jackson prepares for the opening of his ambitious Dangerous World Tour. Rehearsals are underway at the Forum, where Michael works relentlessly with his creative team to perfect every number, costume change, and visual detail. Director Rob and tour manager Nick urge him to conserve his energy and make practical decisions, but Michael is determined to deliver an unprecedented show for his audience.

Into the rehearsal room comes Rachel, an MTV reporter assigned to profile Michael as the tour approaches. Her questions draw him beyond the immediate pressure of production and into memories of the path that shaped him. He recalls performing as a child with The Jackson 5 alongside his brothers, under the demanding authority of their father, Joseph Jackson. The young Michael discovers the exhilaration of the stage, but he also learns that success is tied to exacting discipline, constant rehearsal, and fear of disappointing the people around him.

As the present-day rehearsals continue, Michael revisits pivotal moments from his rise as a solo artist. He remembers his collaborations with producer Quincy Jones, the creation of landmark performances, and the intensity of pursuing perfection. He also confronts the emotional cost of his upbringing and fame: isolation, mistrust, the pressure to remain exceptional, and the complicated bond he still feels with Joseph. The boundaries between rehearsal, interview, and memory blur as songs and choreography carry Michael back into defining episodes of his life.

Rachel gradually sees that the performer before her is not simply constructing a concert, but wrestling with the forces that made him. By the final rehearsal, Michael has transformed private memories, pain, ambition, and artistic instinct into the spectacle he believes his fans deserve. The company unites around him as he prepares to step once more into the spotlight.

The show explores artistic drive, childhood pressure, family conflict, and the personal cost of public success. It presents performance as both Michael’s refuge and the arena in which he continually tries to prove himself.

something rotten.en:
Set in the theatrical world of Renaissance London, Something Rotten! follows brothers Nick and Nigel Bottom, struggling playwrights who are desperate to escape the shadow of the wildly successful William Shakespeare. Nick is ambitious, impatient, and determined to create a hit, while Nigel is a gentler poet whose talent emerges when he meets Portia, a bright, independent young woman with a puritanical father, Brother Jeremiah. Their romance is complicated by Jeremiah’s disapproval of the theater and by Nigel’s uncertainty over whether to follow love, family loyalty, or artistic ideals.

With their company facing financial ruin, Nick seeks help from the soothsayer Nostradamus, who predicts that the next great theatrical sensation will involve singing, dancing, and an elaborate spectacle—a “musical.” Trying to seize the future before Shakespeare does, Nick and Nigel begin writing a strange new production called Omlette: The Musical. Yet Nostradamus’s visions are muddled, and Nick mistakenly believes Shakespeare’s future masterpiece will be called Omelette. Meanwhile, Shakespeare learns that the Bottom brothers are trying to compete with him and uses their insecurity to his advantage.

As rehearsals progress, Nick becomes increasingly consumed by success, pushing the troupe toward a lavish, crowd-pleasing spectacle while neglecting Nigel’s more heartfelt writing.
