Their conflict peaks when Ana tests what Christian’s rules would truly mean for her, forcing both of them to confront whether desire without trust can become love.

The show treats romance, power, and sexual awakening as deliberately outrageous comic spectacle. Beneath the innuendo and chaos, it follows Ana’s push to define her own desires and limits—and Christian’s uneasy encounter with emotional openness.

dracula.en:
Jonathan Harker travels from England to Count Dracula’s remote Transylvanian castle to complete the purchase of a London property. The Count appears courteous but unsettlingly isolated, and when he discovers a portrait of Jonathan’s fiancée, Mina Murray, he becomes fixated on her. Jonathan soon realizes he is a prisoner: Dracula’s Brides prowl the castle, and Dracula feeds on Jonathan’s blood, restoring his youth. Jonathan escapes with his life and eventually reaches Budapest, where Mina joins him and they marry.

Dracula sails to England, arriving near Whitby, and re-establishes contact with his devoted but deranged servant, Renfield, an inmate at Dr. Jack Seward’s asylum. In London, Mina’s friend Lucy Westenra chooses Arthur Holmwood from among her three suitors—Arthur, Dr. Seward, and the American Quincey Morris. Dracula preys upon Lucy, draining her life and transforming her into a vampire. Professor Van Helsing is summoned to identify the danger. With Arthur, Seward, and Quincey, he confronts Lucy in her tomb and destroys her to free her from Dracula’s control.

Meanwhile, Dracula’s psychic bond with Mina deepens. Though she fears him and remains devoted to Jonathan, Mina is drawn to Dracula’s loneliness and promise of a different existence. Dracula feeds from her, and Van Helsing recognizes that she is now connected to the Count. The group uses this bond to track him back to Transylvania. They fight through Dracula’s Brides and pursue him to his castle. Mina chooses to go to Dracula, prepared to abandon her former life for immortality. Yet Dracula realizes that turning her would condemn her to the same cursed fate as his Brides. As the hunters close in, he asks Mina to end his existence. She kills him, and Jonathan finds her holding Dracula’s body as it dissolves.

The musical explores temptation, obsession, and the conflict between mortal love and the longing to escape death. It also frames Dracula’s destruction as an act of sacrifice: love becomes meaningful precisely because it refuses possession and accepts loss.

勸世三姊妹.en:
Deeply in debt and long estranged from home, the three Song siblings—worldly-wise eldest sister Kuo-chen, timid middle sister Kuo-mei, and the youngest, Kuo-hao, who dreams of becoming a drag queen under the name Angela—return to the family house in Huwei, Yunlin, hoping only to grab the deed. But their dying great-uncle's will sets a strange condition: whichever Song descendants learn the traditional soul-guiding funeral chant-and-dance and see him off may inherit a considerable fortune. Reluctantly, the three take up the ritual from scratch.

As they stumble through the chant, don the costume of the professional mourner, and squabble over the inheritance, the ritual keeps stirring memories of their broken family: a gambler-sorcerer father who vanished long ago and a mother who was once a celebrated spirit medium. Old resentments, misunderstandings, and shame surface one layer at a time.

Rooted in the folk funeral traditions of southern Taiwan, the show turns a dance begun for money into a rite of healing. In guiding the dead on their final journey, the three siblings finally learn to lay to rest the past—and the family bonds—they have never been able to say goodbye to.

你好 我是接體員.en:
In a mortuary that feels like the border between the living and the dead, the body-receivers spend their days shuttling between hospitals, accident scenes, and funeral halls, collecting those who have died by accident, suicide, violence, or alone and unclaimed. They clean and settle the bodies and face the families in their collapse, anger, guilt, and grief. To survive the weight of the work, the workers give each case an absurd nickname—a hanging is a “swing,” a jumper a “Peter Pan,” a charcoal-burning suicide “Little Black”—laughing to keep the fear at bay, yet never forgetting that every cold body was once a living person and the anchor of a family.

The story threads together several very different farewells: love left unspoken, affection worn down by hard reality, misunderstandings between husband and wife never resolved, and lives discovered only after a lonely death. The body-receiver watches families quarrel over inheritances and dodge the duty of care, but also sees people who, even in their grief, want to preserve one last shred of dignity for the departed.

Adapted from the mortuary memoirs of the Taiwanese writer “Da Shixiong,” the show wraps its farewells in dark humour. As the body-receiver sends off one stranger after another, we come to see that behind even the most undignified or absurd departure lies a story about home, and about love.

囍宴.en:
Wai-tung Gao, a Taiwanese man living in New York, has been happily together with his boyfriend Simon for years, yet has never told his parents back in Taiwan, who long for their only son to marry and give them a grandchild. To manage their expectations, Wai-tung enters a sham marriage with his friend Wei-wei, a fellow Taiwanese living in New York and a struggling artist—giving her a measure of support while buying himself some relief from the pressure to wed.

What begins as a convenient arrangement spins out of control when Wai-tung's parents suddenly fly to New York. Convinced the marriage is real, they insist on throwing a lavish traditional wedding banquet, and Wai-tung, Wei-wei, and Simon must each play the role expected of them, tiptoeing through relatives, elders, and custom. The banquet looks like a triumph, but beneath the surface it slowly prises open the longings, fears, and love each of them has kept buried.

Adapted from Ang Lee's classic film The Wedding Banquet, the musical uses one fake wedding to bring a tangle of secrets into the open, forcing the shut-out Simon, the role-playing Wei-wei, and Wai-tung—caught among love, family, and duty—each toward their hardest choice. In the end, this family, through truth and loss, comes to understand an acceptance and love they had never quite put into words.

神明便利商店.en:
Shen Yuanjun, an apprentice deity in heaven, is sent to the mortal world by the sea goddess Mazu with an unusual task: he must run a convenience store on Earth and gather a hundred thousand faithful followers before he can cultivate into a full-fledged god. The shop looks ordinary, but it is really a crossing-point between the divine and human worlds, its shelves stocked not only with instant noodles and snacks but with wonders like a “fortune-money ATM” and “half-sugar talisman water.”

Shen Yuanjun serves a stream of eccentric customers while juggling a parade of fellow gods who keep dropping by—the matchmaker Yue Lao, the god of wealth Caishen, the exam-blessing Wenchang, the stately Queen Mother of the West, the local Earth God, and the greedy, adorable Tiger God. Beneath the comic bustle, each visitor arrives carrying a very human story of love, family, dreams, and regret; and as Shen Yuanjun listens and helps, he slowly comes to understand ordinary human joys and sorrows—and to question what “becoming a god” really means.

Adapted from Xie Donglin's hit Taiwanese webcomic and staged in the Japanese-influenced “2.5-dimensional” style, the show suggests that when Shen Yuanjun learns to truly care about everyone who walks through his door, godhood stops being a matter of counting believers.

三個傻瓜.en:
At a top Indian engineering college, three misfit friends survive a world of rote learning, cutthroat competition, and relentless pressure by leaning on one another. Curious and irrepressibly independent, Rancho refuses to follow the rules and draws the ire of the director nicknamed “Virus”—dragging along photography-loving Farhan and the poor, anxiety-ridden Raju. The director’s daughter sides with Rancho, while the affected, foreign-accented Chatur competes with the brilliant Rancho, and a campus storm brews.

Rancho lives by the creed “chase excellence, and success will follow.” In his eccentric but sincere way, he repeatedly pulls Farhan and Raju back from the edge of despair—crushed by family expectations and fear—and leads them to question the absurdity of studying only for grades. When a fellow student, unable to bear the pressure, takes his own life, the three are forced to ask what education is really for: rankings, or the courage to live as oneself.

Years later, scattered across different lives, they wonder who will inherit the coveted pen passed down to the finest student—while Farhan and Raju set out to find the vanished Rancho, retracing a reckless, exhilarating youth. Weaving laughter and tears together, this stage adaptation of the beloved Indian film asks what success truly means: perhaps not the achievements others admire, but the courage to be true to yourself.

太空阿嬤.en:
In 2076, an antique spaceship called the Donggang crash-lands on the beach at Xuhai in Pingtung, southern Taiwan. Its pilot, the legendary 25-year-old astronaut Shi Xiaotian (Sora), believes her mission lasted only five months—until she steps onto solid ground and discovers that half a century has passed on Earth.

Waiting for her is not the youth she remembers but a household of impossibly mismatched family. Her old comrade Luis is now white-haired, while the daughter grown from her frozen eggs, Shi Saqi, is a fifty-year-old scientist—older than her own mother. This “reverse-aging” reunion pits rigorous data against brash intuition in a living-room war, and when the cyber-tang-ki granddaughter Arri, devoted to Taiwanese temple culture, joins in, three generations of women begin a struggle to live together across time, beneath the Dawu Mountains.

Just as the family starts to understand one another, a solar storm strikes and every AI system crashes, leaving loved ones stranded on the Moon with their lives on the line. Science fiction on the surface but rooted in Pingtung’s soil and folk faith, the show lets its “Space Amah” relearn, somewhere between the stars and the dust of home, how to be a mother and a family—and to truly know the land she left and must one day return to.

老男孩.en:
In the late 1990s, the five-member idol boy band Starlight Boys shot to fame on the strength of their hit single of the same name—only to be dissolved almost overnight when their management company collapsed. The five young men who once stood at the top of the stage scattered back into ordinary lives.

Years later, with the record industry long past its heyday, former member Lin Ziwen has become a music producer. His new boy band, New Boys, is about to debut with a cover of that same song, “Starlight Boys”—but on the eve of their launch, the members rebel against his brutal, high-pressure training and walk out one after another, leaving him with nothing. At his wit’s end, Lin Ziwen hatches an audacious, absurd idea: to track down his old bandmates and put the group back together.

Now middle-aged, thickened around the waist and each burdened with life’s own difficulties, these “old boys” are dragged back toward the spotlight. Set to nostalgic pop and threaded with bittersweet reunions, the musical voices a generation’s reluctance to let a dream die: the stage may no longer belong to them, but the youth they never finished singing deserves one more shot.

你的工作 你的休假.en:
After failing interview after interview, a burned-out young worker is finally hired by his dream employer, Company A, only to find that the crushing figure of “Work” cares nothing for his health or sanity, while the once-gentle “Day Off” who has always kept him company grows jealous and clingy.

Adapted from the manga by the Japanese artist Hiwa, this musical personifies “Work” and “Day Off” as two rival characters of opposite temperament—one domineering and unyielding, the other sunny, tender, and quietly devoted—each fighting for the protagonist’s attention. Caught between them, he is pulled ever deeper into a whirlpool where ideals and reality, duty and freedom tangle together, and he begins to wonder how, exactly, one is meant to weigh “success” against “happiness.”

With humour laced with heartache, the show turns the daily grind every office worker knows into a coming-of-age story that sways between “Work” and “Day Off.” As the protagonist learns to find a balance between the two, he slowly comes to see the life he actually wants.

別叫我成功 藝術界歸來的兒子.en:
Zheng Wanli—self-proclaimed umpteenth-generation heir of the Ming loyalist Koxinga and chairman of a Koxinga temple in central Taiwan—faces the demolition of his temple under an urban-renewal scheme. In a flash of inspiration, he decides to stage a grand “Koxinga Arts Festival,” a song-and-dance spectacle starring the hero himself, to draw the island’s attention and save the temple. But when his theatre-graduate son, Zheng Mahao, hears the news and returns from Taipei determined to direct the show and finally prove himself, father and son clash at every turn.

The father longs to protect his ancestors’ faith and home and to see his son become a “success”; the son aches to be recognized on his own terms. As their quarrels escalate, the historical struggle between Koxinga and his own father seems to replay itself offstage, with art, faith, and family love hopelessly entangled.

Driven by Taiwanese-language rap and hip-hop and inspired in spirit by Hamilton, the show sings the warmth and friction of temple-square life. As father and son gradually learn to hear each other, the meaning of “success” is rewritten—it need not be certified by anyone, so long as you can face yourself and the people you love.

我在詐騙公司上班.en:
A scam company is hiring. From a stack of applicants, the boss, Lai Er, plucks out a fresh graduate named Zeng Cheng—a young man so crushed by family debt that he cannot walk away. Honest to the bone, Zeng Cheng wants no part of it, yet he soon discovers a world so saturated with lies and cons that right and wrong seem to blur into nothing.

Under the meticulous training of the cool, capable manager Chen Xin, the man who cannot tell a lie is remade into a “chosen” master swindler. Even as he wades deeper into deception, he tries to hold on to the last shred of sincerity in his heart—and, amid all the cheating and double-crossing, dares to dream of true love and a chance to turn his life around. The boss Lai Er, the manager Chen Xin, and this crew of professional fraudsters all hide stories of their own.

Adapted from Xie Donglin’s hit comic, the show skewers workplace culture and the grey zones of human nature with songs that blend pop, ballad, and rap. When even a man who cannot lie learns to deceive, the audience laughs—and sees just how tangled the truth and lies of this world can be.

情人哏裡出西施.en:
In the final years of the Spring and Autumn period, King Goujian of Yue, bent on revenge against the state of Wu, plots to present the peerless beauty Xi Shi to King Fuchai as a honey trap to cloud his mind. But Fan Li, the minister charged with escorting her, falls for Xi Shi on the long road to Wu—legend has it the journey took three whole years, and that along the way Xi Shi even bore a child.

With the scheme thrown into disarray, a farcical tale of true and false, plan-within-plan begins: just who is the “Xi Shi” finally delivered into the palace to bewitch Fuchai—Xi Shi herself, or Dong Shi, Nan Shi, or Bei Shi? As everyone schemes and improvises, a matter on which two kingdoms’ fates depend collapses into uproarious comedy.

For the first time, All-U People Theatre joins forces with the celebrated Taiwanese-opera troupe Ming Hwa Yuan, blending traditional gezai opera with modern musical theatre in a mix of Mandarin and Taiwanese, old costumes and new songs. Rewriting this historical romance as outrageous farce, the show also uses its band of “Shi” sisters to overturn the old trope in which the women of a honey-trap plot are treated as nothing but pawns.

馬克斯威妖 我睡了我的面試官.en:
Taking as its starting point the thought experiment known as “Maxwell’s demon,” proposed by the physicist in 1871, the show follows a young woman, A, who has inexplicably lost her gift for science and often slips through wormholes in her dreams to glimpse a successful version of herself in a parallel world. Her waking life a mess, the story begins with a “job interview” she completes in a small hotel bed—“Well, I slept with my interviewer.”

Her scattered thoughts pull her back to a past shared with her closest friend, H: a girlhood full of boundless curiosity about the world, tangled feelings, and a once-bright future cut short by “regret.” As memory and dream fold over one another, she gradually sees how, step by step, she came to be where she is.

A one-woman musical in which a single performer holds up an entire universe, it wraps grand theories of physics and parallel time around one woman confronting her own wounds and the shadow of power. As it insists, “this is not some romantic city love story, but the everyday trace of a woman facing her scars”—a raw, self-mocking reckoning with fate, choice, and self-worth.

musical taru.en:
Nali and her friends set out for an ordinary day at the natural science museum. But on the night of a total lunar eclipse, every exhibit in the halls suddenly springs to life! In the magical chaos, a bumbling thief slips through the darkness and steals the fossil of the baby T. rex, TARU—sending TARU’s mother, the tyrannosaur TIRA, into a furious rampage that throws the whole museum into turmoil.

Nali and her companions must summon their courage and set off on a grand adventure to recover TARU and calm the raging dinosaur mother. Along the way, the once-static fossils and models become living, breathing creatures, and the museum turns into a playground of wonder and danger.

A Taiwan–Korea co-production for family audiences, the show is headlined by giant dinosaur fossil puppets—up to three metres tall and six metres long—combined with a dazzling stage of light and sound and high-energy song and dance. Across a hundred minutes of laughter and adventure, children discover not only the thrill of dinosaurs coming back to life, but a warm story about family, courage, and protecting the ones we love.

渡子江 死了都要愛.en:
“The whole world tells him to let go—but he’d rather love than rest in peace.” Even at the very end of his life, a man cannot release the one attachment in his heart, and so he stages a jaw-dropping “jailbreak” in the underworld, turning the realm of the dead completely upside down.

Adapted from Taiwanese funeral traditions, this original musical follows in his footsteps, station by station, through the legendary landscapes of the netherworld—the Grass Road, the Bridge of No Return, the Mountain of Broken Money, the Hill of Fierce Dogs—all the way to the Hall of Judgment where the dead are tried. The barriers and demons along the way are more than cheap scares; they are mirrors reflecting the obsessions and regrets of the living and the dead alike, and every unspoken love and remorse is dragged into the light on this journey across the river.

Rooted in the island’s view of life and death, this small-theatre musical turns “letting go”—the hardest thing of all—into a journey that has you laughing and crying at once. When a man is willing to storm all of hell for love, the story’s real question is this: just how long must we cling before we learn how to truly say goodbye?

我的爵視金曲夜.en:
At the Golden Bell Awards ceremony, performers are fondly looking back on how the golden songs of Taiwanese film and television have accompanied a generation through the years. Then, as the music drifts on, a mysterious host named “Little Lu” makes a flamboyant entrance and, without warning, drags the entire ceremony onto the stage of Taiwan’s first-ever jazz big-band programme, “Jazz A Golden Night.”

Under Little Lu’s baton, one beloved screen classic after another is rewoven into swinging, lavish jazz; the stage shuttles back and forth between the awards ceremony and a jazz nightclub, stringing together the collective memory and era-defining emotion these songs carry for Taiwan. The audience is swept into a musical journey at once nostalgic and fresh.

As the golden oldies play on and the stories unfold, the ceremony finally returns to its opening suspense—who will take home the Lifetime Achievement Award? Threading its tale through jazz standards, the show sings the golden age of Taiwanese entertainment into a warm love letter, offered to everyone these melodies have ever kept company.

si sol mi.en:
Once a girl who dreamed of becoming a magical-girl heroine, Ai-jia is now, in 1992, the star of a variety song-and-dance troupe in Shitou Township. In that era, a “Si-Sol-Mi” troupe like theirs had to perform for every occasion—warming up a wedding banquet one day, and singing and dancing a departed soul on its way at a funeral the next.

To grab a bigger share of a fiercely competitive market, Ai-jia and her partner Melody flash bright smiles and dazzling routines onstage while, behind the scenes, it is all daggers drawn and quiet warfare. Beneath the feathers and sequins lies the hard reality of these travelling entertainers: scraping a living, fighting for gigs, and trying to hold on to a shred of pride and their first love of the stage against the world’s scorn.

Set against Taiwan’s folk “Si-Sol-Mi” song-and-dance culture, the show portrays a band of performers hustling to survive amid the dust of ordinary life. As commerce and ideals keep pulling against each other, Ai-jia searches, show after show, for the girl she once was—the one who longed to be seen by the world, the one who wanted to be a magical girl.

記憶的星光.en:
When memory slips away a little at a time, how does a person—or a whole family—face what is being lost? Starlight of Memory is an original musical centred on dementia care, hoping that through song and the power of theatre, more people might come to understand, accept, and support those living with dementia and their families.

Unlike a conventional production, this show brings professional performers together onstage with people in the early stages of dementia—so that patients are not merely subjects to be talked about, but people who truly stand in the spotlight and tell their own stories in song. In the interweaving of music and drama, the names, faces, and memories that seemed carried off by illness are gently called back.

At its heart is a belief: that dementia does not mean losing everything. Even as memory dims, so long as there is music and love to keep one company, that “starlight of memory” belonging to each person can still light up the heart—and illuminate the road ahead for those who walk beside them.

夢幻雞排大冒險.en:
Sworn brothers A-qi and A-ba share one dream: to make the most delicious “dream fried chicken” in the world. Armed with a magical secret recipe, their chicken becomes a sensation, with lines forming at their stall—but their success draws the eye of the greedy “King Who Borrows and Never Repays.”

The king lays a trap, and A-ba is killed and turned into a ghost. What the spirit of A-ba cannot let go of is not the recipe, but an unresolved misunderstanding between him and A-qi; his one wish is to see A-qi once more and set things right. And so a fantastical adventure between the worlds of the living and the dead—by turns hilarious and touching—begins.

Adapted from the Taiwanese folk legend of the deities “Seventh Lord and Eighth Lord,” this children’s song-and-dance musical uses uproarious interaction and heartfelt friendship to sing lessons of keeping one’s word and cherishing one’s friends into young hearts. Across seventy minutes of adventure, children find not just ghosts and fried chicken, but a warm tale of trust, loyalty, and standing by one another beyond even death.

微笑半世紀.en:
Smile for Half a Century is a commemorative musical created for Acer's 50th anniversary. Through music and storytelling, it traces Acer's five-decade journey—from its founding and early growth to reform, transformation, and global expansion.

The production revisits key moments in Acer's history, including its early formation and later restructuring. Actor Kuo Tzu-chien portrays Acer Group founder Stan Shih. The story also includes the company's five founders, along with figures representing Wistron chairman Simon Lin and Pegatron chairman T.H. Tung, both of whom have substantial roles.

Shih serves as the project's "AI chief director" and composer, using AI as part of the creative process for both the anniversary theme song, "Believe and Make It Happen," and the musical itself.

Running about two and a half hours, the show presents Acer's story as more than a corporate anniversary. It looks back on a company that grew alongside the information age, faced change and reinvention, and helped bring Taiwan onto the global technology stage.

Built around the idea that innovation begins with belief and legends are shaped by perseverance, Smile for Half a Century pays tribute to the people who pursued a shared dream throughout Acer's history.

blbff.en:
Shao-bing, a high-school junior, is equally panicked about two things: how to write his university application, and the fact that he still hasn't found a girlfriend. Out of options, he simply pays An-de, an openly gay senior, to coach him through his application, and ropes in art-class prodigy Dai-dai to help him win over the girl he likes.

Three teenagers who would never otherwise cross paths are thrown together by this deal, forming what they grandly dub the “Get-a-Life Squad.” Through a string of comic misadventures, their anxieties about grades, social fear, identity, and sexuality are peeled open one by one—and what looked like a BL romance grows into the bond of true best friends (BFF).

Produced by Voleur du Feu Theatre and directed by Lin Chun-yi with songs by Chang Ching-yen, this original campus musical uses just five performers and songs written close to the hearts of Taiwanese teens, giving voice to a generation's longing to be understood and cared for.

honk.en:
Among a brood of ducklings, one hatches looking nothing like the rest—an odd shape, a strange honk—and from the very start he is mocked, shunned, and finally left all alone.

Setting out to find where he belongs, the little duckling meets all sorts along the way: a sweet-talking cat with sly intentions, a turkey terrified of ending up in the oven, and friends who accept him just as he is. Little by little, he comes to see that being “different” may be exactly what makes him one of a kind.

Adapted from Hans Christian Andersen's The Ugly Duckling and a winner of the Olivier Award for Best Musical, Honk! is staged here in a licensed Mandarin version by the If Kids Theatre, using warm songs to help children learn to accept themselves and be brave enough to be who they are.

love any way.en:
It's a couple's anniversary, and An-cheng and Joan, the owner of the “Love Anyway Bar,” are bustling about to throw boyfriend Tommy an unforgettable surprise. This is an immersive bar where the audience is drawn right into the story—dim lights, the smell of liquor, everything seemingly just romantic enough.

Then a mysterious man named Li Hao walks in. As he appears, the secrets hidden behind everyone's smiles begin to come loose one by one—betrayal, lies, and desire take turns on stage, and a carefully planned surprise threatens to spiral into an absurd, laugh-out-loud romantic battlefield.

An immersive original musical from the Andersen & Mozart Creative Society, written and directed by Jia Yu with music by Liu Yao-hsuan, it turns a bar into a stage and lets the audience watch, up close, a relationship get exposed and re-interrogated all in a single night.

三個不結婚的女人.en:
Three sisters live under one roof and could not be more different: eldest sister Si-rong is a sharp-looking rank-and-file police officer; middle sister Si-tong is a sharp-tongued beauty YouTuber; youngest Si-yu is a drama student and fangirl to the bone. They share one belief—staying unmarried needs no reason.

Under the shared understanding that “rather than a relationship you settle for, live a life you're particular about,” each woman faces her own hurdles in love, career, and life, treating singlehood as an active choice rather than a state of waiting to be picked.

Adapted from Kusanatsume's Taiwanese webcomic of the same name and brought to the stage by Wukou Creative, directed by Sun Zi-yi with songs by Chang Ching-yen, this episodic ensemble comedy sings an unapologetic freedom for everyone who refuses to settle.

不親愛家人.en:
On the eve of the Tomb-Sweeping holiday, the two He brothers are told to head back to the old family home to pay respects and deal with the property. Fei-yu, an airline ground-staffer, and Hao-yu, a middle-school P.E. teacher, mean to get it over with fast—only to learn, right then, that their parents are divorcing.

The reappearance of a childhood friend, Li Jia-dai, works like a key, opening a drawer this family has left shut for years, and the emotions and wounds never properly dealt with come flooding back over these few days home. Rather than a heartwarming reunion, it honestly lays bare the estrangement and awkwardness within a family.

An episodic musical produced by Gan-Ma-Jiang-Zhi Creative Studio, with story and lyrics led by Jiang Bai-ren, music by Kang He-xiang, and direction by Cui Tai-hao, each roughly hour-long installment sings the words we can never quite say to the people closest to us.

今晚 我想來點.en:
At the height of the 2021 pandemic, office drone Xiao-xiong watches his company fold overnight—laid off, unable to make rent, his life at rock bottom, with nothing in hand but a food-delivery recruitment flyer. With nowhere left to turn, he climbs onto a scooter and joins the riders weaving through the city.

Each “ding-dong” of an incoming order threads together three lively storylines: Yan-jun, a dazzling livestream teacher; Wen-yan, a hot-blooded senior rider mentoring newcomers; and a younger brother pining for Yan-jun who briefly wonders if he's been turned. Under the pandemic's magnifying glass, these little people's joys and mishaps turn both hilarious and poignant.

Voleur du Feu Theatre adapts the creators' own real stints as delivery riders, with Kao Tien-heng writing and directing and Chang Ching-yen composing, using broad comedy and an upbeat finish to leave a magical-yet-real record of a time when everyone's life was forced to flip.

大家都怎麼做音樂劇.en:
The lights come up, and playwright Kao Tien-heng and composer Chang Ching-yen simply walk on stage—playing no one but themselves—to demonstrate, live and from scratch, how an original musical gets made. This is a musical about making a musical.

How do you come up with a theme? What do you do when the script has more characters than actors? What happens if the mood has to swing from joy to anguish but you're not allowed to change the lyrics? Real dilemmas from the creative trenches are broken into plays-within-a-play—even how arrangement, orchestration, and choral vocals quietly cue the audience is laid bare for you to see.

A meta experiment from Voleur du Feu Theatre, written and directed by Kao Tien-heng with music by Chang Ching-yen, it walks the audience through a creator's “journey through hell,” sneaking a look at the backstage and bones of musical theatre amid the laughter.

小王子.en:
A broken-down plane makes a forced landing in an empty desert, and the exhausted pilot meets a curious boy there—one who comes from the faraway planet B612, the boy grown-ups call the Little Prince.

Amid the endless sand, the Little Prince recounts his travels since leaving his planet: the proud rose he both loved and resented, the absurd grown-ups each ruling their own little world, and the fox who taught him what it means to “tame” and that only with the heart can one truly see. His innocent questions gently interrogate a grown-up world that has long forgotten its first heart.

Adapted from Saint-Exupéry's beloved classic and staged in Mandarin under Korean license by C MUSICAL, performed by three actors and three live musicians, it closes on the tender image of the Little Prince leaving Earth to become every smiling star in the sky.

市場女人心 第一市場二部曲.en:
Douliu's Central Market, Taiping Old Street, First Market, and the Twin-Star Theater were once a bustling, thriving heart of town. Now, with industry moved on and people gone, the clamor has faded, leaving the old market and cinema to quietly guard a place full of memory—this is where three women's lives intertwine.

Performed entirely in Taiwanese, the piece uses one market and one cinema, and the people who walked the years alongside them, to sing the rise and fall of a once-flourishing district, and the quiet devotion of those who keep watch over this land and its human warmth through changing times.

A choral musical from the Yunlin Philharmonic Chamber Choir, continuing its own work First Market, it uses Taiwanese song and chorus to give a voice to a place slowly being forgotten.

換氣練習.en:
Creatures of the deep sea must endure crushing, unimaginable pressure just to survive. That pressure is transplanted onto a group of graduating high-schoolers—exams, social media, comparison with peers, the expectations of the world outside, every one of it enough to leave them gasping for air.

Lan-en, a senior who skips class to teach himself post-rock and psychedelic music at home, is dragged by ambitious cover-song influencer Sha-sha into a hastily formed band to enter an original graduation-song contest. TIDELINE comes together, and as these teens are gradually noticed, their clashing musical ideals and private pressures keep striking sparks.

Adapted from the Taiwanese picture book Ghost Shark's Yearbook, selected for the Bologna Book Fair, this original youth musical produced by Xu-Shi Project Theatre and directed by Sun Zi-yi turns the survival pressure of deep-sea creatures into a generation's fierce practice at catching its breath.

月亮雪酪.en:
On a sweltering summer night, everyone in the apartment block huddles under the air conditioning to keep cool—while up in the sky, the moon begins to melt, drop by drop. The kind-hearted resident-committee granny is the first to hear that mysterious dripping and discover the astonishing change.

Unwilling to let it go to waste, she gathers the melted moon-water drop by drop and makes it into a cool sherbet, while the moon rabbits, their home now lost, drift down to Earth in search of a new one. Behind the cool fairy tale hides a quiet reminder about global warming and the environment.

Adapted from Korean picture-book author Baek Hee-na's Dalshabet, this licensed family musical from C MUSICAL runs a brisk sixty minutes, letting grown-ups and children alike, amid neighborly warmth, think about our relationship with this planet.

水鬼學校和失去媽媽的水獺.en:
The old folks always say that at night the world turns to water, and water ghosts crawl up from the river to snatch children who wander outside. Yet after their classmate Xiao-pang drowns by accident, three schoolkids—Tadpole, Sweet-Potato, and Scar—slip down to the riverside anyway: they want to bring his soul back.

Led by an old man nicknamed the “old water ghost,” the three dive beneath the surface, meet an otter, and set up a “water-ghost school,” determined to teach the creature to speak—hoping that one day it might cry out “Mama” and ease the longing that Xiao-pang's mother cannot let go.

Adapted from the same-titled fantasy novel by National Award-winning writer Kan Yao-ming, this Hakka-language musical from Godot Theatre, directed by Chang Yang-hsuan with book and lyrics by Wang Jun-yi, sets a world above the water—ruled by rules and Mandarin—against a world below, where mother tongue and imagination run absolutely free.

漂浪半島.en:
A mysterious two-stringed moon lute, painted with an onion motif, opens a whirlpool in time, letting the Hengchun Peninsula of 2026 quietly overlap with 1996. On a coast howling with wind, modern rock crashes head-on into traditional Hengchun folk song.

Mia, a rock diva who has lost her voice, hides away in Hengchun to heal; and in 1996, Da-feng, a girl desperate to escape the peninsula and make it in Taipei, chases her own dream on the same soil. One aches to flee the bright lights, the other longs to break out of the barren quiet, and the two women of different eras mirror each other in the wind.

An original musical from Sing Sing Drama, with Hengchun folk song as its soul and a fusion of folk-rock and live band, directed by Wu Luo-ying and written by Shih Bai-jun, it sings a story of lost roots, homecoming, and the search for self amid the pull between tradition and the modern.

潘朵拉的音樂盒.en:
Some fine works are boxed away after their run and rarely seen again. This show simply pries the box back open—in one evening, four performers act, sing, and narrate their way through excerpts of five wildly different original Taiwanese musicals, with five stories, twenty roles, and eleven songs following one after another.

From a courtesan's act of loyalty in The Courtesan Weds, to a macho matchmaker god meeting a gay one in Tying the Red Thread; from a cellist hiding the father of her child in Zola's Recital, to woodland lovers toyed with by sprites in A Summer Dream, and five childhood friends recalling the past in an air-raid shelter in Anniversary—period comedy, fantasy, lyricism, and farce take turns on stage.

An original anthology produced by the Unlimited Power Drama Lab and written and directed by Lin Zhao-ming, built on the idea of “reopening forgotten good shows,” it pays tribute to years of original Taiwanese musical theatre.

無聲の海腳間仔.en:
In 1943, the shadow of war hangs over Minato-cho in Kaohsiung, and an air-raid siren suddenly tears through the night. In a place called the “seaside room,” three uprooted souls cling to one another: Chun-luo, a woman from Penghu stricken with consumption; her younger brother Hai-nan; and Wang-mei, an orphan girl from Meinong whose sister has mysteriously vanished.

They fill the cracks in one another's lives, barely holding on through the turmoil—until a censor named Nagawa Minato, of Pingpu descent yet holding Japanese status, has his fate cross violently with theirs over a street-side clash, in an age of colonization and oppression when even speaking freely was forbidden.

An original historical musical from Where Theatre, written and directed by Zhu Yu-chen, it weaves Taiwanese, Hakka, and Japanese into a multilingual dialogue of the era, singing the words the silenced could never speak—as if they all, in the end, flowed out to sea.

爬上頂樓看月亮.en:
A wistful Japanese folk song, “Oboro-zukiyo,” is softly sung on the rooftop of a century-old campus—and unexpectedly summons a ghostly senior from the Japanese colonial era, Chen-bao, who then possesses their classmate Zhi-zhi. Literary older sister Yu-en and science-minded younger sister Yu-ya are pulled into this century-spanning accident.

To save Zhi-zhi and to help Chen-bao recover her lost memories, the two sisters embark on an escape-room-style quest through the school's arts building. As a certain figure in Chen-bao's mind grows clearer bit by bit, the sisters are forced to face the knots between them they have never been able to put into words.

Produced by Voleur du Feu Theatre and directed by Dai Jun-fang, with original story and script supervision by Chien Li-ying, developed over three years of field research, it uses delicate female emotion to sing a song of longing that spans a hundred years.

生命最美好的5分鍾.en:
A music-loving reaper from the underworld carelessly gets the timing wrong, and young musician John ends up dead when his hour hadn't come—a soul who “wasn't meant to die” yet did. To make up for the blunder, the flustered reaper strikes a deal: for the five minutes a piece of music plays, you may travel through time and undo the mistake.

In those miraculous five minutes, the world-weary John shuttles again and again through time, meeting a middle-schooler exactly like his younger self, and running headlong—before a wedding invitation from an ex—into the true love he once let slip. Dreams, regret, and love intertwine, forcing him to face life's every shortfall.

Produced by Godot Theatre and directed by artistic director Liang Chih-min, written by first-prize-winning playwright Wang Mu-tien, with eighteen original songs, a live band, and even inline skating, magic, juggling, and group dance, it sings a tender question about whether life can ever be lived again.

當亞斯遇見人魚.en:
Hero, a boy with Asperger's traits who barely ever leaves the house, has shrunk his whole world into a single screen. That is, until he meets Man-man, a warm and free-spirited livestream girl online; sharing life through the screen, that closeness becomes a rare salvation in each of their gray days.

Then one day, without warning, Man-man announces she is ending her stream for good. To see her one more time, Hero—always hidden away at home—must summon the greatest courage of his life and step out through that long-shut door. One must overcome the fear of going out; the other is searching for a kindred soul.

Produced by Red Tide Theatre and commissioned by the National Taichung Theater, written and directed by Wang Ching-tun with music and lyrics by Liang Yun-jui, who also stars alongside Li Man, this original Mandarin musical—honed over some five years—tenderly embraces every kind of “special.”

蕾娜絲的修理小舖.en:
Tucked into a corner of the city sits a repair shop full of mystery. What it mends is no ordinary pot or pan, but things deliberately forgotten and long since broken—even a most precious sound from someone's life.

Three wounded people walk in, one after another. Mi-nuo, caged in self-blame, cradling a glass bird covered in cracks; Yi-fan, who under years of coldness and bullying has lived himself into a mere broken shadow; and Ai-ma, clutching an out-of-tune music box, held fast by a sense of helplessness. When their wounds collide inside the shop, each sees a familiar crack in the other.

The 67th work of Shang Theatre, an original musical where rock meets healing, it uses fantastical imagery to sing one tender truth: a crack is exactly where the light gets in.

跑跑殭丙仁.en:
The apocalypse arrives, and zombies fill the streets. A-jiang, a thirty-three-year-old shut-in, becomes an unlikely end-of-days hero thanks to the “experience points” he racked up playing horror games; alongside him are A-ren, a zombie extra whose own grandmother has turned, and A-bing, an old reporter set on recording news that still matters.

The three sprint on through the apocalypse, until the zombies come to outnumber the living and even begin to gain minds of their own, with endless time on their hands. As human darkness surfaces, an absurd yet piercing question is thrust forward: is it worse to live like the dead, or to die like the living?

An original musical from Spot Creative Workshop, written and directed by Kao Tien-heng with Chien Li-ying as script consultant, it is Taiwan's first zombie-themed musical—an over-the-top end-of-days comedy that hides a serious inquiry into the meaning of existence.

轟吧 全壘打.en:
There is a youth baseball team that has lost for years, never once tasting victory, mockingly called nothing more than “seagull feed.” Just when the team seems beyond hope, two coaches of clashing temperaments arrive: one a hot-blooded softie, the other Yu-an-na, an ice-cold woman coach who trusts nothing but the data.

Tugged between two utterly opposite coaching styles, this bunch of rowdy kids fights its way from a losing streak all the way to the national tournament. Through sweat, quarrels, and tears, they slowly learn to embrace their teammates and to believe in themselves, edging toward the moment they swing the hardest hit of their lives.

Adapted from the Korean musical Baseball King, Ocean Team! and licensed for a brand-new Mandarin version by AMcreative, it is Taiwan's first baseball family musical, made in cross-field collaboration with the Ball Sprout Foundation and coached by retired pro players—offered to children, and to every grown-up still reaching for a dream.

阿卡的兒歌大冒險.en:
Aka, a child who loves to sing, always drifts off to the nursery rhymes his mother hums at bedtime. One day he makes a big vow: to learn every nursery rhyme in the world, and to find one song that is uniquely, entirely his own. So he works up his courage and sets off on a round-the-island adventure.

Along the way he meets characters who step straight out of Taiwanese nursery rhymes: the pedicab driver and old lady squabbling over the fare in “Tricycle,” the “Tiger Auntie” who actually adores children despite her fearsome name, and the heroes of “Clay Doll,” “Little Donkey,” “Dark Sky” and more, each with a story of its own.

An original family musical co-produced by A Theatre Group and the eslite Performance Hall, it uses only the human voice and no instruments at all, combining a cappella with vocal percussion and physical interaction to let children hear, in Taiwanese nursery rhymes, the sheer magic of pure voice.

阿甯咕的爸鼻不見了.en:
With just three days of summer vacation left, Aningu still has a mountain of homework—and the hardest of it is an essay titled “My Father.” Unable to write a word, he grumbles that it wouldn't matter if the family had no dad at all—only for the trouble-making, tall-tale-telling Dad Luo to actually vanish into thin air.

It is as if the world had never held this man. Dad becomes a stranger sleeping in the park whom no one recognizes, even Mom and big brother turn different, and Aningu himself is close to forgetting him. In this disorienting state where the most familiar person becomes a stranger, he slowly learns to recognize who truly matters as family.

Adapted from writer Lo Yi-chun's essay collection The Youngest Son and produced by the Aningu Theatre, directed by Kao Tien-heng, this family musical is the third in the “Youngest Son Animated Theatre” series, singing—between the laughs—a song about family, companionship, and cherishing what we have.

青瞑猴 出外讀冊拼出頭.en:
A blind child in the countryside, scorned for being unable to see, refuses to accept that as his fate. He makes up his mind to leave his hometown and go away to study, carving out his own way to “make good” through others' strange looks and hurdle after real hurdle.

Performed entirely in Taiwanese and drawn from the true story of a blind child who left home to study against the odds, the piece has its laughs, its tears, and its conflicts, singing throughout the conviction of “never giving up”—determined to break, through song, people's fixed ideas about the visually impaired.

Created and performed by the Zhan-Yi Choir, an ensemble of visually impaired singers who perform without a conductor or accompaniment, it bills itself as Taiwan's first “visually-impaired Taiwanese-language musical,” joining chorus, drama, and music—for, as it puts it, every song is a beam of light.

into the woods.en:
A witch confronts a childless Baker and his Wife with the curse that hangs over their home: only by gathering four items—a cow as white as milk, a cape as red as blood, hair as yellow as corn, a slipper as pure as gold—within three days can they lift it and have a child. So they plunge into the woods, colliding with a cast of fairy-tale figures each chasing a wish: Cinderella, Jack of the beanstalk, Little Red Riding Hood, Rapunzel in her tower.

In Act One, wish after wish comes true and everyone lives “happily ever after.” But Act Two sends the bill: the widow of the slain giant comes crashing down for revenge, death and disorder follow, and the survivors—stranded in moral gray—finally learn to lean on one another and own the consequences of their choices.

A classic by Stephen Sondheim (music and lyrics) and James Lapine (book), it stitches beloved tales into a fable about what happens after the wish is granted, tenderly insisting that no one is alone.

little shop of horrors.en:
On rundown Skid Row, in a florist's shop with no customers, a clumsy clerk named Seymour tends a strange and mysterious plant. He names it Audrey II, after the coworker he secretly adores. The plant makes the shop an overnight sensation—but it hides a gruesome secret: it drinks only human blood and feeds only on human flesh.

In a low, seductive voice, the plant goads Seymour into feeding it, trading bodies for fame and Audrey's affection. To be rid of the sadistic dentist who abuses Audrey, Seymour slides step by step into complicity—while Audrey II grows ever larger and ever hungrier.

With music by Alan Menken and book and lyrics by Howard Ashman, adapted from the 1960 B-movie, and threaded by a trio of Skid Row girls like a Greek chorus, it turns a dark fable of all-devouring greed into a gleeful, cautionary rock comedy.

sunday in the park with george.en:
On the island of La Grande Jatte outside Paris, the pointillist painter George pours himself into building light and form out of countless tiny dots—while remaining blind to Dot, the lover and model at his side. Longing to be truly seen rather than a patch of color on his canvas, she eventually leaves for America carrying his child, and George finishes his masterpiece alone.

A century later, a weary, cynical contemporary artist—George's fictional great-grandson—is stuck between a creative block and the demands of commerce. Through a reunion with his aged grandmother and a return to the site of La Grande Jatte, he recovers the courage to connect and to move on.

With music and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim and a book by James Lapine, inspired by Seurat's famous painting and winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, it sings the solitude, the cost, and the inheritance of making art.

last five years.en:
A five-year love story, told through two timelines running in opposite directions at once. Cathy, an actress, sings backward from the heartbreak of the end toward the flutter of the beginning; Jamie, a rising novelist, sings forward from first sight toward divorce. The two cross paths, one in reverse, one going forward.

Jamie's career soars while Cathy's keeps stalling, and as ego and reality erode them bit by bit, the love goes quietly wrong. At the very center of the show, the two timelines finally meet at the wedding for their only duet—then part again, one walking toward betrayal and goodbye, the other frozen on the hopeful night of the first date.

Written entirely by Jason Robert Brown (music, lyrics, and book), this two-hander uses its ingenious reverse structure to let joy and sorrow take their bows in the very same moment.

25th annual putnam county spelling bee.en:
A county spelling bee opens in a school gymnasium, and six quirky kids take the stage, each carrying something unspoken: Olive, whose best friend is the dictionary while her parents stay absent; Barfee, an allergy-prone boy who spells with a “magic foot” on the floor; a defending champ; a spacey boy who turns out to be smarter than he thinks; a prodigy sick of always winning; and a politically precocious girl eager to please her two dads.

Round by round the spellers are eliminated—real audience members pulled on stage compete too—and each one who misspells gets a juice box and a hug on the way out. Along the way, private confessions open up every child's loneliness, longing, and growing up.

With music and lyrics by William Finn and a book by Rachel Sheinkin, grown from an improv show, it sings childhood's fixation on winning and its ache to be seen and loved, with warmth and wit.

urinetown.en:
A twenty-year drought has turned water into the scarcest of luxuries. Private toilets are banned, everyone must pay to use public amenities, and the corporation that monopolizes every restroom in town—Urine Good Company—keeps hiking the fees, squeezing the poor until they can barely breathe.

When the amenity worker Bobby watches his own mother arrested for being unable to pay, he rises up in revolt—and falls in love with Hope, the tycoon's daughter. The revolution seems to topple the tyranny, yet once the fees are scrapped and water flows unchecked, the supply runs dry after all. As the narrator warns from the start, this is a musical with no happy ending.

Created by Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis, forever breaking the fourth wall and poking fun at the musical form itself, it is an absurd satire skewering corporate monopoly, populism, and the cycle of environmental collapse.

billy elliot.en:
In 1984, a mining town in the northeast of England is caught in the agony of the miners' strike. Billy, an eleven-year-old boy who has lost his mother, is sent by his father to learn boxing—only to fall for the ballet class sharing the same hall, and start dancing in secret.

His father and brother, steeped in working-class values and old ideas of manhood, cannot accept a son who dances; but his ballet teacher, Mrs. Wilkinson, sees his gift and urges him to audition for the Royal Ballet School. Only when his father finally sees the boy dance does he waver—willing even to cross the strikers' picket line to scrape together the money for Billy's dream.

With music by Elton John and book and lyrics by Lee Hall, adapted from the film, it sings—amid a failing strike and a doomed colliery—one boy's hope of breaking free of class and gender to dance.

barnum.en:
In nineteenth-century America, the showman P.T. Barnum lives by the belief that there's a sucker born every minute, building his name on outsized spectacle and humbug—from a woman billed as 161 years old to General Tom Thumb and the Swedish Nightingale, Jenny Lind, he can always turn a tall tale into the most beguiling entertainment.

His practical wife, Charity, keeps pulling him back down to earth. A museum burned to the ground, a flirtation with Jenny Lind, and the wild swings of fortune all test their marriage. Through the ups and downs, Barnum finally partners with Bailey to launch the world-famous Barnum & Bailey Circus.

With music by Cy Coleman and lyrics by Michael Stewart, staged with all the dazzle of a circus, it sings the eternal tug between spectacle and truth, ambition and love.

parade.en:
In 1913 Atlanta, just after the Confederate Memorial Day parade, a thirteen-year-old factory girl named Mary Phagan is found murdered in the pencil factory where she works. Suspicion falls on the factory's superintendent, Leo Frank—a Jewish transplant from Brooklyn.

Amid a thick atmosphere of antisemitism, egged on by an ambitious prosecutor and a sensational press, a trial built on flimsy evidence convicts Leo and sentences him to death. In the wrongful ordeal, he and his Georgia-born wife Lucille only grow closer; the governor commutes his sentence at the cost of his own career, but cannot stop a mob from storming the prison in the summer of 1915 and lynching him.

With music and lyrics by Jason Robert Brown and a book by Alfred Uhry, adapted from the real Leo Frank case, it grieves over injustice, prejudice, and incitement—and the love that holds fast through catastrophe.

fun home.en:
A grown cartoonist, Alison, picks up her pen to look back on growing up—in a home that doubled as a funeral parlor, which she nicknamed the “Fun Home.” Three Alisons share the stage: the innocent girl, the college student discovering love, and the adult narrator trying to make sense of it all.

At college, Alison realizes she is a lesbian, falls for her first girlfriend, and comes out to her family—only to learn that her father Bruce, a man of near-obsessive control over beauty and household, has long hidden his own secret affairs with young men. Not long after she comes out, Bruce dies under a truck; Alison has always believed it was suicide.

With music by Jeanine Tesori and book and lyrics by Lisa Kron, adapted from Alison Bechdel's graphic memoir, it moves through a daughter's search to understand her father, touching family secrets, identity, and truths too hard to name.

carousel.en:
On the coast of Maine in 1873, Billy Bigelow, a carousel barker, and Julie Jordan, a gentle mill worker, fall for each other at first sight and marry in haste—and promptly both lose their jobs. Learning that Julie is pregnant and desperate to give the child a better life, Billy is talked by a bad friend into taking part in a robbery.

The robbery goes wrong, and rather than be captured, Billy takes his own life. In the afterlife he is granted a single day back on earth; fifteen years later he quietly returns to his daughter, and at her graduation—where she sits crushed and ashamed—offers a belated word of encouragement and love, and finds his redemption.

With music by Richard Rodgers and book and lyrics by Oscar Hammerstein II, adapted from Molnár's play Liliom, it uses songs like “You'll Never Walk Alone” to sing how love reaches across hardship and death.

la cage aux folles.en:
In Saint-Tropez on the French Riviera, above a nightclub famous for its drag revue, the club's owner Georges and its star drag queen Albin—stage name Zaza—have been partners for years. Then Georges's son announces he intends to marry the daughter of a conservative politician—whose father, no less, leads an anti-gay morality league.

To fool the in-laws, the son begs his father to hide his identity and send away Albin, the very person who raised him. Deeply wounded, Albin instead disguises himself as a proper, demure “mother” for the dinner, and nearly pulls it off. When the ruse collapses into chaos, the two families at last learn, amid the farce, to accept one another and to love.

With music and lyrics by Jerry Herman and a book by Harvey Fierstein, its proud anthem “I Am What I Am” carried the declaration of being oneself into the mainstream stage.

pirates of penzance.en:
On the Cornish coast of the Victorian era, young Frederic has just turned twenty-one and finished his apprenticeship—free at last to leave this absurdly tender-hearted band of pirates, go straight, and fall in love with Mabel, a Major-General's daughter. But the fine print says his indenture runs until his twenty-first birthday—and, born on the leap-day of February 29th, he has technically had only five birthdays.

Out of a ridiculous sense of duty, Frederic dutifully reports back to the pirates; learning that the Major-General lied about being an orphan, they vow revenge. As police and pirates square off, the sergeant's cry of “in the name of Queen Victoria” makes the pirates instantly surrender—for they turn out to be noblemen who have gone wrong, and so are pardoned and wed to the Major-General's daughters.

A classic comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, with patter songs like “I Am the Very Model of a Modern Major-General,” it gleefully mocks the Victorian worship of duty, honor, and institutions.

school of rock.en:
Dewey, a down-and-out rock musician, is kicked out of his own band and can't make rent, so—out of options—he steals his roommate's name and sneaks into an elite prep school as a substitute teacher.

Meant to just follow the syllabus, he instead discovers that his straight-laced, high-achieving students are secretly full of musical talent, and behind the principal's and parents' backs, trains the whole class into a rock band bound for the Battle of the Bands. Along the way he reignites a passion buried under academic pressure, and loosens the grown-ups' grip on “behaving.” When his false identity is finally exposed, it's the students who stand by him.

With music by Andrew Lloyd Webber, lyrics by Glenn Slater, and a book by Julian Fellowes, adapted from the Jack Black film, it lets the kids play and sing live, blasting out the purest energy of rock.

jekyll and hyde.en:
In late-nineteenth-century London, Dr. Henry Jekyll is determined to use science to cleave apart the good and evil in human nature—hoping to cure his mentally broken father. When the hospital board rejects his request to experiment on a human subject, he furiously tests the serum on himself, drinking it down and transforming into the brutal, bloodthirsty Edward Hyde.

From then on he leads a double life: an engagement to his upper-class fiancée Emma on one side, and, as Hyde, an entanglement with the tavern singer Lucy on the other, while taking bloody revenge on the board members who humiliated him. As Hyde grows stronger and Jekyll weaker, the personality nears collapse; at his own wedding, to end the demon within, Jekyll chooses to let himself be killed.

With music by Frank Wildhorn and lyrics and book chiefly by Leslie Bricusse, adapted from Stevenson's novella, it sings the eternal duel of good and evil through anthems like “This Is the Moment.”

young frankenstein.en:
Frederick Frankenstein, a professor of brain medicine, is so eager to distance himself from his infamous mad-scientist grandfather that he insists his surname be pronounced “Fronk-en-steen.” A will, however, summons him back to the family's gloomy castle in Transylvania.

Egged on by his hunchbacked assistant Igor and his blonde lab assistant Inga, he cannot resist the lure of his grandfather's notebooks, restarts the experiment, and really does create a monster. When the creature escapes and rouses the villagers, Frederick tries to prove it tamed with a “Puttin' on the Ritz” song-and-dance—which, of course, gets wildly out of hand.

Comedy legend Mel Brooks writes the music and lyrics and co-authors the book with Thomas Meehan, adapting his own 1974 black-and-white classic into a barrage of gags and dance numbers—the most uproarious tribute to old horror films.

kimberly akimbo.en:
Kimberly is about to turn sixteen—yet she wears the face of an old woman. She has a rare condition that ages her rapidly and leaves her precious little time. As her dysfunctional family moves to a small New Jersey town, she faces not only a body out of step with her age, but an alcoholic father, a self-absorbed pregnant mother, and a house full of lies.

At her new school, Seth—a boy who loves anagrams and musicals—becomes her first friend, giving her a taste of friendship and first love. But when her scheming aunt turns up and drags the family into a check-fraud scheme, Kimberly, seeing at last that her family can never truly support her, decides to seize what life she has and go chase experiences of her own.

With music by Jeanine Tesori and book and lyrics by David Lindsay-Abaire (from his own play), it sings, amid the bittersweet, the courage to seize the day and smile at goodbye.

suffs.en:
In early-twentieth-century America, a new, radical generation of suffragists can no longer stomach the slow, moderate path. The young Alice Paul, pushing to win the vote through a federal constitutional amendment, clashes head-on with Carrie Chapman Catt, the association president who favors a gradual, state-by-state strategy.

From the vast 1913 march on Washington to the “Silent Sentinels” picketing outside the White House, to arrest, imprisonment, hunger strikes, and violence, these women press on—while the movement's own generational rifts and racial exclusion (Black women pushed to the margins) cut just as sharp. In 1920 the Nineteenth Amendment finally passes—yet the show honestly notes that Black women remained long barred from the ballot, and the victory is far from complete.

Written entirely by Shaina Taub (music, lyrics, and book), who also stars, and drawn from real suffrage history, it sings the fervor, the cost, and the unfinished business of activism.

devil wears prada.en:
Fresh out of college and set on becoming a journalist, Andy knows nothing about fashion—yet somehow lands the job of assistant to Miranda, editor-in-chief of the top fashion magazine Runway. Her new boss is an ice-cold tyrant whose single word can send the whole office trembling.

In a workplace harsh to the point of absurdity, Andy is battered again and again, then—under the creative director's guidance—transformed, gradually winning Miranda's favor. The price is a deepening game of power, and a self and a relationship sacrificed along the way. When she sees firsthand how ruthless Miranda can be to climb, Andy finally realizes she has no wish to walk that road.

With music by Elton John and lyrics by Shaina Taub and Mark Sonnenblick, adapted from the bestselling novel and film, it sings an urban fable of ambition, selling out, and getting out in time.

just in time.en:
The lights come up and the stage becomes a nightclub, as the singer Bobby Darin sings his own life story straight to the audience. From a sickly boy in the Bronx whom doctors said wouldn't live long, to a superstar storming the charts, he turns his life into a race against time with hit after hit—“Splish Splash,” “Beyond the Sea,” “Mack the Knife.”

After his career peaks and he marries the film star Sandra Dee, a buried secret about his origins comes to light—the “sister” he always knew was in fact his birth mother. His life unravels, and he climbs back onto the stage again and again, until, at thirty-seven, a heart condition brings the sudden final curtain.

A biographical jukebox musical starring Jonathan Groff, with a book by Warren Leight and Isaac Oliver and direction by Alex Timbers, it uses Darin's classic songs to sing the dazzle and fragility of the American dream, and the tug between the stage persona and the true self.

beautiful.en:
At sixteen, Carole King works up the nerve to walk into a Manhattan music publisher with her own songs in hand—and steps straight into the golden factory of 1960s pop, the Brill Building.

She becomes a songwriting team, and a married couple, with lyricist Gerry Goffin, and shares a friendly rivalry with the partners Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil, together turning out one hit after another. But her husband's infidelity and restlessness finally break the marriage; stepping out of the shadow, Carole decides to stop being only a behind-the-scenes writer and to sing in her own voice, at last taking the stage at Carnegie Hall and blossoming into a true star.

A biographical musical with a book by Douglas McGrath, stringing together the classic songs of Carole King and her contemporaries, it sings how one woman found her own voice.

million dollar quartet.en:
On the night of December 4, 1956, at the Sun Records studio in Memphis, four names who would go on to shake popular music—Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Carl Perkins, and the wild, untamed newcomer Jerry Lee Lewis—happen to gather and jam together for one legendary night.

Narrated by Sam Phillips, the record-label owner who discovered them, song after song and memory after memory draw out each man's history with the little label and the choices each now faces: stay with the scrappy small studio, or jump to a deep-pocketed major. Amid the music and the tension, the spark of rock and roll's birth flows alongside Phillips's helplessness as he watches his stars slip away.

A jukebox musical with a book by Colin Escott and Floyd Mutrux, using the four legends' classic songs to recreate that fleeting night that changed the history of music forever.

marie curie.en:
A young Polish woman, Maria Sklodowska, crosses the sea to the Sorbonne in Paris, determined to make her mark in science. With Pierre Curie she falls in love and discovers the radioactive element radium, and together they take home the Nobel Prize.

But radium is soon mass-marketed by a businessman named Ruben as a glowing, almost miraculous cure-all. The factory women who paint it onto watch dials—among them Anne, Marie's friend and fellow Pole—begin, one after another, to sicken and die. As Anne fights to expose the truth, Marie is driven to the edge of her conscience: defend the discovery that made her name, or admit that radium kills.

A Korean original musical produced by LIVE, composed by Choi Jong-yoon, written by Cheon Se-eun, and directed by Kim Tae-hyung (Anne is a fictional character, echoing the real Radium Girls), it swept the Korean Musical Awards and reached London's West End in an English-language version in 2024. It sings of the conscience and responsibility hidden behind great scientific achievement, and of two immigrant women standing together against prejudice and injustice.

last empress.en:
In 1866, Joseon Korea is beset on all sides by the great powers. The young King Gojong takes a bride from the Min clan—the future Empress Myeongseong. Gifted in both intellect and beauty, she urges Gojong to rule in his own right, locking horns with her father-in-law, the regent Heungseon Daewongun, who holds the reins of power.

Through upheaval after upheaval—a soldiers' mutiny, the Sino-Japanese War—the Empress strives to protect her country through independent diplomacy, turning toward Russia to check Japan's ambitions. To a Japan bent on swallowing Korea, she becomes the greatest obstacle of all. In the 1895 Eulmi Incident, the Japanese minister Miura Gorō leads a band of ronin into Gyeongbokgung Palace; guards such as Hong Gye-hun give their lives in her defense but are overwhelmed, and the Empress is assassinated.

Adapted from Yi Mun-yol's play The Fox Hunt, composed by Kim Hee-gap, with lyrics by Yang In-ja and direction by Yun Ho-jin for ACOM, it was the first Korean original musical to reach Broadway (Lincoln Center) and London's West End, drawing more than two million theatergoers. It ends on the defiant anthem “Rise, My People,” singing a queen's resistance and tragedy in the face of foreign aggression.

hero the musical.en:
In 1909, in Vladivostok, Ahn Jung-geun and his fellow independence fighters cut off the ring fingers of their left hands and write “Korean Independence” in blood across the Korean flag, swearing to give their lives for their country. Learning that Ito Hirobumi—former Japanese prime minister and first Resident-General of Korea—is about to visit Harbin, Ahn resolves to strike down the man devouring his homeland.

With intelligence passed along by figures such as Seolhee, a former palace woman now working undercover as a spy, Ahn tracks Ito's movements. On October 26, 1909, at Harbin Station, he shoots Ito down and, crying “Long live Korean independence,” lets himself be seized. In the prison and courtroom of Lüshun, he insists he is no assassin but a lieutenant-general of the Korean Righteous Army, laying out Ito's crimes one by one; his mother, Jo Maria, sends word that he should meet death without fear.

A Korean original musical drawn from the true final year of the patriot Ahn Jung-geun, it premiered in 2009 to mark the centenary of his act. Directed by Yoon Ho-jin for ACOM, composed by Oh Sang-joon, with book and lyrics by Han Ah-reum (the role of Ahn was long played by star actor Jung Sung-hwa). It interweaves a freedom fighter's cause with the flesh-and-blood feeling of a son and a man, singing his undying wish for “peace in the East.”

man who laughs.en:
In late-17th-century England, where class runs iron-hard, a young boy named Gwynplaine is stolen by child-traffickers and has his mouth slashed into a face that “laughs” forever. Abandoned in a snowstorm, he rescues a blind baby girl, Dea, from beside her dying mother as he flees; a wandering showman, Ursus, takes both children in, raising them like a father and building a traveling troupe together.

Years pass, and the “man who laughs” becomes a celebrated clown, devoted to Dea. But when the Duchess Josiana sees his act she is entranced and sets out to seduce him—and at the same time, the secret of his birth surfaces: Gwynplaine is in truth the rightful heir of a fallen noble house. In an instant, three lives are turned upside down.

Adapted from the novel by the French master Victor Hugo, produced by EMK with music by Frank Wildhorn, lyrics by Jack Murphy, and book and direction by Robert Johanson, it opened in Seoul in 2018 to a sensation. Through songs like “Open Your Eyes,” it sets wealth against poverty and deformity against human dignity—just as it cries out that the paradise of the rich is built upon the hell of the poor.

frankenstein.en:
In the age of the Napoleonic Wars, Victor Frankenstein—a genius scientist scarred since childhood by loss—harbors a world-shaking dream: to create undying life. He befriends Henri Dupré, a brilliant surgeon skilled at grafting flesh, and the two pursue the work side by side—until, after the war, an accident takes Henri's life. On his deathbed, Henri entrusts his own body to his friend.

From Henri's body and head, Victor completes his experiment and succeeds in making life—only to flee in horror at the sight of the hideous creature and heartlessly abandon it. Scorned by its maker and the whole world alike, the Monster tastes nothing but loneliness, aching for a scrap of warmth and meeting rejection at every turn. Fallen into an underground fighting arena, watching those around it destroyed one by one, it finally burns the place down and swears revenge on the creator who cast it aside.

The two chase each other all the way to the frozen Arctic for a final reckoning; Victor kills the Monster with his own hands, yet calls it by the name “Henri.” A Korean original musical adapted from Mary Shelley's novel, written and directed by Wang Yong-beom and composed by Lee Seong-jun, it was the tenth-anniversary flagship of the Chungmu Art Hall (premiering in 2014); its principal actors each play dual roles, and in a dark, brooding, tragic key it asks where humanity ends and the beast begins—and who the real monster is.

mata hari.en:
In 1917, in a field outside Paris, a firing squad raises its rifles at a woman. Time rewinds nine months—to the glittering Belle Époque, where the exotic dancer Mata Hari, with a mysterious “temple dance,” has captivated all of high-society Europe and become its most sought-after star.

Able to move freely between the warring nations, she catches the eye of Colonel Ladoux, head of French intelligence, who half-coaxes, half-forces her into spying. Just then, on the banks of the Seine, she meets a young aviator, Armand, and falls in love; the clash between private passion and secret mission, together with Ladoux's manipulations, drives her step by step into a corner. When she crosses into German-occupied territory on forged papers to find her lover, she can no longer escape the net set for her—and in the end, condemned as a German spy, she becomes the scapegoat of a world at war.

A Korean musical composed by Frank Wildhorn with lyrics by Jack Murphy and a book by Ivan Menchell, produced by EMK (Seoul premiere 2016), drawn from the true life of the WWI courtesan-spy Mata Hari. Bookended by the execution scene, it sings a woman's reinvention, love, and sacrifice under the crushing weight of war and the machinery of the state.

ben hur musical.en:
In the year 26 AD, Jerusalem groans under the iron heel of the Roman Empire. Judah Ben-Hur, a young man of a noble Jewish house, is reunited with Messala—the childhood friend he grew up with, now returned in Roman armor. When Ben-Hur refuses to betray his own people and help crush the Jews, a crack opens in their friendship.

When an accident injures the Roman governor, Messala seizes the chance to frame the House of Hur for treason; to protect his family, Ben-Hur takes the blame and is condemned to slavery at the oars of a galley. Years later, having saved a Roman commander and won his freedom, he returns home to face Messala in a fateful, vengeful showdown at the chariot races before a roaring crowd. And this journey of blood and vengeance runs alongside the age of Jesus of Nazareth.

A Korean original musical adapted from Lew Wallace's novel Ben-Hur, with book, lyrics, and direction by Wang Yong-beom and music by Lee Sung-jun (the team behind Frankenstein). Beyond twisted friendship, betrayal, and revenge, it reaches for the universal questions of faith, redemption, and human dignity.

interview korean.en:
London. Eugene Kim, a bestselling mystery novelist, advertises for an assistant writer. A young man named Sinclair arrives for what looks like an ordinary interview—only for the questions and answers to peel back, layer by layer, the fathomless depths of the person across the table.

As the probing deepens, Sinclair seems to “become someone else” again and again before Eugene's eyes: now an innocent child, now a street tough, now a coquettish girl, now a cold observer—many strangers' souls housed in a single body. It is dissociative identity, carved out by the trauma of childhood abuse—and behind these selves there seems to lurk an unfinished murder case. The lines between truth and lie, memory and story, slowly collapse in the psychological duel between the two men.

A Korean original psychological-thriller musical, composed by Heo Suhyeon and written and directed by Chu Junghwa. Through taut, chamber-piece dialogue, it leads the audience into a labyrinth of trauma and identity, holding back the truth beneath the smile until the very last moment.

xcalibur.en:
In the 5th- and 6th-century Britain left behind by a departed Rome and beset by Saxon invasion, war rages and no true king remains. Legend holds that only the one destined can draw the holy sword Excalibur from the stone—and the one who draws it turns out to be an ordinary boy, Arthur.

Guided by the wizard Merlin, Arthur grows from a nobody into the King of Britain and builds the ideal kingdom of Camelot. Yet Lancelot, his most trusted knight, comes to harbor a forbidden love for Queen Guinevere; and Arthur's half-sister Morgana, nursing her rage over a destiny stolen from her, presses in with dark magic. Loyalty, love, and betrayal drive the newborn kingdom to the brink of collapse.

A Korean rock musical produced by EMK, drawn from the legend of King Arthur and the sword in the stone (reworked from the original Artus – Excalibur, itself rooted in Frank Wildhorn's Arthurian concept), it premiered in 2019 with stars including Kim Junsu in the role of Arthur. In sweeping rock, it sings an ancient tale of destiny, the burden of kingship, and forbidden love.

gwanghwamun sonata.en:
A man at the end of his life is led by a guide across the threshold between life and death, back to a spring in 1984 he still carries in memory—at a sketching contest at Deoksugung Palace in Seoul, where he once met his first love. The tender, turbulent Korea of the 1980s unfolds again before him, carried on song.

Through one familiar melody after another, he walks back through that youthful romance and faces anew the choices and regrets of a whole life—the things said and unsaid, the ones held onto and the ones let slip. As the memory reaches its end, in the lingering warmth of that first love he comes, at last, to make peace with his life.

A Korean jukebox musical built from the classic songs the late composer Lee Young-hoon wrote for singer Lee Moon-sae—“Gwanghwamun Love Song,” “Under the Shade of the Roadside Trees,” “Red Sunset,” “Old Love” and more—produced by CJ ENM (the 2017 revision written by Ko Sun-woong and directed by Lee Ji-na). In melodies a whole generation knows by heart, it sings first love, memory, and the choices and acceptance of a lifetime.

bright star.en:
Set in the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina, Bright Star moves between 1945–46 and 1923–24. In the later story, Billy Cane returns from World War II to his home near Hayes Creek, determined to become a writer. His devoted friend Margo Crawford has quietly encouraged his ambition, but Billy leaves for Asheville, where he submits a story to The Asheville Southern Journal.
