Its formidable editor, Alice Murphy, initially dismisses him, yet his talent and optimism persuade her to publish his work and offer him a place at the magazine. Billy becomes close to Alice’s assistant Lucy Grant and printer Daryl Ames, while Margo comes to Asheville hoping Billy will recognize what she means to him.

Alice’s guarded manner is explained through the past. As a teenager in Zebulon, she falls deeply in love with Jimmy Ray Dobbs, the son of Mayor Josiah Dobbs. Their romance leads to Alice’s pregnancy, and Jimmy Ray wants to marry her—but Mayor Dobbs, desperate to avoid scandal and protect his political ambitions, forbids the match and arranges for Alice’s newborn son to be taken from her. The Mayor himself carries the baby aboard a train in a suitcase and throws it from the moving carriage into the river below. The infant survives, however, and is found by a grieving couple who raise him as their own: Daddy Cane and his late wife.

Years later, Alice notices a familiar hand-knit sweater among Billy’s belongings—the very garment she made for the child she lost. The truth emerges: Billy is Alice and Jimmy Ray’s son. Alice confronts Jimmy Ray, who has lived for years believing their baby died, and reveals both Mayor Dobbs’s cruelty and Billy’s survival. Father and son meet, old grief begins to heal, and Billy and Margo choose one another as Alice and Jimmy Ray reclaim the love stolen from them. The story closes with both couples preparing for marriage.

The musical explores love’s endurance against shame, class pressure, and abuse of power. It also centers on identity, forgiveness, and the possibility that truth can restore families fractured by the past.

memphis.en:
In 1950s Memphis, Huey Calhoun, a restless young white man with a passion for rhythm and blues, wanders into Delray’s underground Beale Street club and is electrified by the music he hears there. He becomes captivated by Felicia Farrell, Delray’s gifted younger sister, who longs to escape the club circuit and become a recording artist. Despite Delray’s distrust and the danger of crossing racial lines, Huey promises Felicia he will help her reach a wider audience.

Huey’s relentless enthusiasm earns him a job at a radio station, where he defies convention by playing Black music for white listeners. His wildly energetic on-air persona turns his programme into a sensation, making him a local celebrity and opening a commercial path for the sounds he loves. He also brings Felicia into the studio, helping to launch her career. Their professional partnership becomes a romance, but their relationship provokes hostility from both the public and Huey’s mother, Gladys, who cannot accept Felicia.

As Huey’s influence grows, Felicia receives an opportunity to pursue national success in New York. Huey refuses to leave Memphis, believing his place is behind the microphone that has made him famous. Their conflicting ambitions, compounded by the violence and prejudice surrounding them, strain their bond. When Felicia is brutally attacked because of their relationship, she recognizes that remaining with Huey would continue to place them both in danger. She leaves for New York, where she finds success as a singer, while Huey’s career fades after the station abandons the music that made him matter.

Years later, Felicia returns to Memphis for a performance. Huey, no longer the star he once was, comes to see her. Their reunion acknowledges the love they shared and the irrevocable paths their lives have taken.

The musical explores how music can cross boundaries that society fiercely polices, while also showing that artistic progress does not erase personal risk or injustice. It examines interracial love, ambition, courage, compromise, and the price of trying to make a divided world listen differently.

tarzan.en:
After a shipwreck off the coast of West Africa, a baby boy survives while his parents are killed by the leopard Sabor. Nearby, the gorilla Kala mourns her own infant, taken by the same predator. Finding the orphaned child in the wreckage, she brings him to her troop and names him Tarzan. Kerchak, the troop’s stern leader, rejects the child as an outsider and warns that he can never truly belong, but Kala refuses to abandon him. Tarzan grows up learning the gorillas’ ways, supported by his energetic friend Terk, while constantly struggling to match the strength and agility of those around him.

As an adult, Tarzan proves his courage by confronting Sabor, yet his place in the troop remains uncertain. His world changes when an English expedition arrives in the jungle: Professor Porter, his curious daughter Jane Porter, and their guide, Clayton. Tarzan is astonished to meet humans who look like him, and Jane is equally fascinated by the intelligent, wild man she encounters. As she teaches him about the human world, Tarzan begins to communicate in her language and discovers objects and memories that connect him to the life he never knew. Their growing affection forces him to confront a choice between the family that raised him and the people to whom he seems physically connected.

Clayton, however, sees the gorillas not as living beings to understand but as valuable trophies. He manipulates Tarzan’s trust to locate the troop, then captures the gorillas and turns on Tarzan. In the ensuing struggle, Tarzan fights to rescue Kala, Terk, and the others. Kerchak is fatally wounded while defending his family, but before dying he finally recognizes Tarzan as his son and names him leader of the troop. Jane, prepared to return to England with Professor Porter, chooses instead to remain in the jungle with Tarzan.

tuck everlasting.en:
In 1893, eleven-year-old Winnie Foster feels trapped in the carefully ordered home she shares with her grieving Mother and Nana in Treegap, New Hampshire. Longing for a larger life, she slips away toward the woods just as a mysterious Man in the Yellow Suit arrives, determined to uncover a secret hidden there. At a spring deep in Treegap Wood, Winnie meets Jesse Tuck, a boy who appears seventeen. When he stops her from drinking, his family—Mae, Angus, and Jesse’s older brother Miles—takes Winnie with them and reveals the truth: eighty-five years earlier, the Tucks drank from the spring and ceased to age or die.

Though frightened at first, Winnie is welcomed into the Tucks’ wandering, unconventional life. She sees their joy, but also their isolation: Mae aches for her sons, Miles mourns the ordinary family life he lost, and Angus understands that a life without change has become a kind of stillness. Jesse, drawn to Winnie, urges her to wait until she is seventeen and then drink from the spring so they can remain together forever. Winnie begins to imagine that future, even as Angus explains that mortality gives life its movement and meaning.

The Man in the Yellow Suit follows Winnie and discovers the spring. He abducts her, planning to buy the wood, bottle its water, and sell immortality through his carnival. Mae rescues Winnie by striking him with a shotgun; he dies, and Mae is arrested. Winnie helps the Tucks escape after their jailbreak, while Constable Joe and his eager assistant Hugo pursue them. Before leaving Treegap, Jesse gives Winnie a bottle of spring water and asks her to join him one day. Years later, he returns and finds that Winnie chose a mortal life; at her grave, the Tucks recognize the fullness of the life she lived.

The musical explores the tension between the wish to escape time and the need to embrace it. It celebrates love, loss, family, freedom, and the idea that life is precious precisely because it changes and ends.

falsettos.en:
In 1979 New York City, Marvin has left his wife, Trina, for his lover, Whizzer, yet refuses to relinquish his image of a “tight-knit family.” He expects Trina, their young son Jason, Whizzer, and his psychiatrist Mendel to accommodate a new domestic arrangement on his terms. Instead, everyone chafes under Marvin’s need for control. Trina, exhausted and emotionally frayed, turns increasingly toward Mendel, while Jason struggles to understand his father’s choices and the instability they have brought into his life. Whizzer resists being cast in the role Marvin has designed for him, and their relationship becomes a contest of affection, anger, jealousy, and competing demands.

Mendel begins courting Trina and eventually marries her, offering her and Jason a steadier home. Marvin and Whizzer break apart after escalating conflict, leaving Marvin to confront the consequences of having alienated both his former wife and his lover. He gradually recognizes that his most urgent responsibility is to Jason, who is trying to form his own identity amid the adults’ upheaval.

Two years later, preparations for Jason’s bar mitzvah reunite the extended family. Marvin and Whizzer find their way back to one another, while Trina and Mendel settle into married life. Jason also forms a close bond with Whizzer. Their circle expands to include the neighbours Dr. Charlotte, a physician, and Cordelia, a caterer. For a time, this improvised family finds a workable tenderness: they argue, compete, celebrate, and care for one another despite their unorthodox connections.

That fragile peace is shattered when Whizzer collapses and becomes seriously ill. As his condition worsens, the family gathers around him, setting aside old resentments. Jason’s bar mitzvah proceeds under the shadow of Whizzer’s illness, and the ceremony becomes a painful marker of both Jason’s coming of age and the family’s shared loss. Whizzer dies surrounded by those who love him.

The musical explores the difficult work of making a family after conventional structures have failed. It considers love, maturity, Jewish identity, chosen kinship, and how illness can force people to confront responsibility, grief, and compassion.

she loves me.en:
In 1934 Budapest, Maraczek’s Parfumerie is a small, tightly run shop where assistant manager Georg Nowack works alongside the dependable Ladislav Sipos, eager delivery boy Arpad Laszlo, glamorous Ilona Ritter, and the polished but unreliable Steven Kodaly. Georg is devoted to an anonymous correspondent known only as “Dear Friend,” whose thoughtful letters offer him the romantic connection he cannot find in daily life. When Amalia Balash arrives seeking work, Georg objects to hiring her, and their sharp disagreements soon turn them into workplace enemies.

Amalia, however, is also writing to a mysterious “Dear Friend” through a lonely-hearts advertisement. Neither she nor Georg realizes that the cherished letters they exchange are addressed to each other. As Christmas approaches, the shop’s tensions deepen. Mr. Maraczek comes to suspect Georg of an affair with his wife, dismisses him, and only later discovers that it is Kodaly—not Georg—who has been the wife’s lover. Kodaly is let go, while a remorseful Maraczek asks Georg to return and promotes him to manager.

Meanwhile, Ilona finally sees Kodaly’s selfishness clearly and finds unexpected warmth with a kind optometrist named Paul, whom she meets one evening at the library. Georg arranges to meet his correspondent at the Café Imperiale, only to discover that “Dear Friend” is Amalia. Startled by the revelation and still bruised by their quarrels, he conceals the truth. Amalia believes she has been stood up, while Georg tries—awkwardly at first—to show her greater tenderness in person. Gradually, their hostility gives way to understanding. On Christmas Eve, Georg reveals that he is the man behind the letters, and Amalia accepts that the person she loves in words and the man she has come to love in life are one and the same.

The show explores how love can be obscured by pride, first impressions, and fear of disappointment. It celebrates emotional honesty, second chances, and the discovery that real intimacy requires seeing another person beyond the role they first seem to play.

nine.en:
In early-1960s Venice, celebrated film director Guido Contini approaches his fortieth birthday with nothing ready for the new film that everyone expects him to make. He has a cast, crew, producer, and a grand production planned, but no usable script—and no clear idea of what the film should be. His creative paralysis is inseparable from his private life. Guido’s wife, Luisa Contini, is exhausted by his evasions and infidelities, while his mistress, Carla Albanese, demands more of his attention and repeatedly intrudes upon the fragile order he tries to maintain. Hoping to restore his marriage and find inspiration, Guido takes Luisa to a spa near Venice, only for the press and members of his production to descend as well.

There, Guido is pressed by his formidable producer, Liliane La Fleur, and challenged by Stephanie Necrophorus, a critic eager to expose the emptiness behind his celebrity. He turns to Claudia Nardi, the elegant actress he imagines as his ideal leading lady and artistic saviour, but she sees that he has no finished story and refuses to become another illusion in his life. Guido’s thoughts increasingly blur memory, fantasy, and reality. Women from his past and present appear around him: his mother, whose love remains a powerful presence; Sarraghina, whose sensuality shaped his adolescent imagination; Carla, Luisa, Claudia, and the other women onto whom he has projected desire, comfort, guilt, and artistic inspiration.

As the chaos grows, Guido’s film and marriage both seem beyond repair. Luisa finally confronts the damage caused by his self-absorption and leaves him. Stripped of excuses and unable to hide in fantasies, Guido abandons the extravagant film he has been pretending to create. He returns instead to the memories of his younger self and begins to face the life he has avoided, searching for a more honest way to work, love, and live.

The show examines creativity under pressure, the cost of treating other people as material for one’s own dreams, and the uneasy boundary between imagination and escape. Its central journey is Guido’s painful movement from romantic self-invention toward accountability and emotional maturity.

1776.en:
In Philadelphia in the summer of 1776, the Second Continental Congress struggles to decide whether the thirteen colonies should break from Britain. John Adams of Massachusetts, impatient and combative, believes independence is the only possible course, but he has alienated many fellow delegates. Benjamin Franklin advises him to find a proposal that can unite the Congress. Adams persuades Richard Henry Lee of Virginia to introduce a resolution for independence, but Lee must return home to gain his colony’s support. Before leaving, he charges Adams, Franklin, and the reserved young Virginian Thomas Jefferson with drafting a Declaration. Jefferson longs to return to Virginia and his wife, Martha, yet accepts the task. As delegates debate, Adams faces resistance from conservative members such as John Dickinson of Pennsylvania, who fears that separation will bring ruin and war. Rumours of British military power, conflict on the frontier, and the absence of unanimous support deepen the crisis.

Jefferson produces a powerful draft, but the Congress subjects it to relentless revision. The most painful dispute concerns a passage condemning the slave trade. Edward Rutledge of South Carolina refuses to support independence if the clause remains, arguing that southern colonies will not accept it. Though Adams and Franklin are appalled, they recognize that the vote may fail without South Carolina. Jefferson reluctantly agrees to remove the passage. Meanwhile, Dickinson continues to oppose the resolution, but when Pennsylvania’s delegation changes position, he chooses not to obstruct the vote. The delegates then face the final test: whether to risk their lives, property, and political futures by signing a document that openly defies the Crown. One by one, the colonies cast their votes. With New York abstaining but the remaining colonies in favour, the resolution passes, and the delegates prepare to sign the Declaration of Independence.

The musical explores the difficult birth of collective action: idealism must contend with ego, fear, compromise, and competing regional interests. It celebrates courage and democratic debate while confronting the moral cost of achieving unity through unfinished justice.

damn yankees.en:
Joe Boyd, a middle-aged Washington, D.C., real-estate agent, loves two things: his devoted wife, Meg, and the perennially losing Washington Senators. When the Senators again fall to the New York Yankees, Joe impulsively wishes for one great home-run hitter who could save the team. The suave and sinister Mr. Applegate appears with an offer: in exchange for Joe’s soul, he will transform him into Joe Hardy, a handsome, twenty-two-year-old baseball phenomenon. Joe negotiates one protection—the right to cancel the bargain before a specified deadline—then leaves Meg behind and joins the Senators under his new identity.

Joe Hardy immediately becomes the sensation the team needs. Under manager Van Buren, the Senators begin an astonishing climb toward the pennant, while Hardy’s prodigious hitting turns him into a national celebrity. Yet every victory makes his separation from Meg harder to bear. He attempts to see her, but must conceal who he really is; Meg recognizes something familiar in the young player, while Joe struggles to sustain the lie that his old self has simply vanished.

Determined to make Joe surrender his escape clause, Applegate sends his glamorous assistant, Lola, to seduce him. Lola has been trained to get whatever she wants, but Joe’s steadfast love for Meg unsettles her. As the team closes in on the Yankees, Applegate plots to keep Joe bound to their bargain and prevent the Senators from winning honestly. Joe ultimately finds the courage to reject the glamorous life and reclaim the ordinary one he abandoned. With Lola’s unexpected sympathy and a clever use of the agreement’s terms, he outwits Applegate, returns to Meg as Joe Boyd, and helps guide the Senators into the World Series.
bard

The musical pits ambition, celebrity, and instant gratification against loyalty, integrity, and love. It also celebrates belief in an underdog team while suggesting that a meaningful life cannot be bought at the cost of one’s soul.

bat boy.en:
In Hope Falls, West Virginia, teenage spelunkers Rick, Ron, and Ruthie Taylor discover a strange, feral creature in a cave. After the Bat Boy attacks Ruthie, Sheriff Reynolds takes him to local veterinarian Dr. Thomas Parker. Dr. Parker’s compassionate wife, Meredith, insists on caring for the terrified boy, names him Edgar, and—with help from their daughter Shelley—teaches him to speak, dress, read, and live among people. Edgar proves eager to learn and deeply grateful for the affection Meredith offers him, while Shelley gradually sets aside her initial disgust and becomes his closest companion. Dr. Parker, however, resents Edgar’s growing place in his household.

As Edgar’s transformation continues, he attempts to present himself to Hope Falls as a civilized young man. The townspeople initially respond with excitement, but fear and prejudice soon surface, especially after livestock are found dead and drained of blood. Edgar struggles to control an instinctive hunger for blood, and Dr. Parker exploits the town’s suspicions, turning public opinion against him. When Edgar is rejected and threatened, Shelley chooses him over the community and flees with him into the woods. Away from Hope Falls, the two confess their love and briefly imagine a life beyond the town’s hostility.

Their escape ends when Meredith finds them and reveals the secret that has governed her life: years earlier, Dr. Parker raped her, and Edgar is their son. Edgar and Shelley are therefore half-siblings. Dr. Parker’s guilt, rage, and attempts to hide the truth have helped create the violence surrounding Edgar’s return. The townspeople arrive as the revelations unfold, and the confrontation becomes catastrophic. Edgar, crushed by the loss of Shelley and the collapse of the family he longed for, turns his anguish on Dr. Parker and ultimately destroys both his father and himself.

The musical explores the longing to belong in a society quick to fear and exclude those it labels monstrous. It also examines inherited trauma, family secrecy, prejudice, and the painful conflict between civilized ideals and violent impulses.

spring awakening.en:
In a provincial German town, Wendla Bergmann begins to sense the changes of adolescence but receives only evasions from her mother when she asks how life begins. At the boys’ school, brilliant, defiant Melchior Gabor clashes with authoritarian teachers, while his anxious friend Moritz Stiefel is overwhelmed by sexual dreams, academic failure, and fear of disappointing his father. Melchior tries to help Moritz by writing down what he knows about sex, but Moritz’s confusion only deepens as school discipline and parental pressure close in around him.

Elsewhere, Wendla and her friends Martha and Thea struggle beneath the constraints of their homes; Martha reveals the violence she suffers from her father. Moritz meets Ilse Neumann, a former classmate who has escaped an abusive household and now lives among artists, but he cannot imagine a future beyond his shame. After learning he has failed his examinations, Moritz is rejected by his parents and takes his own life. His death devastates Melchior, who is blamed when the adults discover his essay.

Melchior and Wendla grow close after meeting in the woods. Their attraction leads them into a sexual encounter that Wendla does not fully understand, because no adult has given her truthful knowledge. When she becomes pregnant, her mother finally tells her what has happened. Melchior is sent away to a reformatory school, while Wendla is taken to undergo an abortion. She dies from the procedure.

In the reformatory, Melchior is haunted by Moritz’s memory and learns of Wendla’s death. Moritz urges him to abandon life, but Wendla’s spirit calls Melchior back toward the future. He chooses to leave the dead behind and continue living, joined by other young people who have also endured fear, desire, loss, and awakening.
mtishows

The musical portrays adolescence as a period of urgent curiosity colliding with secrecy, punishment, and adult control. Its central themes are sexual awakening, institutional repression, abuse, grief, friendship, and the difficult choice to keep living after devastating loss.

in the heights.en:
In Washington Heights, Manhattan, Usnavi de la Vega opens his bodega on a sweltering summer morning and introduces the people who make his block feel like home: his cousin Sonny, the warm-hearted Abuela Claudia, salon owner Daniela and Carla, Rosario’s Car Service owners Kevin and Camila Rosario, their daughter Nina, driver Benny, and Vanessa, the young woman Usnavi quietly loves. Usnavi dreams of returning to the Dominican Republic, while Vanessa longs to escape her difficult home life and move downtown to pursue fashion. Nina, celebrated by the neighborhood for attending Stanford, returns carrying a secret: she has left college after struggling with isolation and money. Her parents, devastated but determined, consider selling their business to pay for her education, while Kevin objects to Nina’s growing romance with Benny.

A winning lottery ticket worth $96,000 is sold at Usnavi’s bodega, turning the neighborhood upside down with speculation. Vanessa unexpectedly has the money for a downtown apartment, and Usnavi, imagining a new life in the Dominican Republic, plans to close the store and leave. But the heat brings a blackout, and during the darkened night Nina and Benny reaffirm their love, while Usnavi finally tells Vanessa how he feels. The following day, Abuela Claudia dies, leaving the community grieving and Usnavi shaken. Her memory and a small inheritance give Usnavi the means to pursue his plans, yet they also remind him how deeply his life is rooted in the block.

As residents confront rising rents, uncertain futures, and the prospect of separation, Nina chooses to return to Stanford with her family’s support, determined to create opportunities for others. Vanessa delays her departure, and Usnavi decides that his future is not elsewhere: he will remain in Washington Heights, reopen the bodega, and build a life with Vanessa amid the people who have sustained him. The community gathers to celebrate, preserving its bonds even as the neighborhood changes.

The show explores home, belonging, ambition, and the difficult choices involved in pursuing a future without abandoning one’s roots. It also celebrates community as a source of memory, resilience, love, and collective possibility.

color purple.en:
In rural Georgia in 1909, fourteen-year-old Celie is abused by her father, Alphonso, who takes away the two children she bears. When Albert Johnson, known as Mister, seeks a wife, Alphonso gives Celie to him in place of her younger sister, Nettie. Celie enters Mister’s harsh household as an unpaid servant, caring for his children while enduring his violence. Nettie briefly joins her, but Mister drives her away after she rejects his advances; he then hides every letter she sends to Celie.

Years pass. Mister’s son Harpo falls in love with the formidable Sofia, whose refusal to submit contrasts sharply with Celie’s learned silence. Harpo tries to dominate Sofia, but she leaves him; later, after striking the mayor in self-defence, she is brutally punished and forced into domestic service for the mayor’s wife, Miss Millie. Celie’s life shifts when Shug Avery, Mister’s glamorous singer lover, arrives ill at the house. Shug initially dismisses Celie but comes to recognise her kindness and intelligence. The two grow close, and Shug offers Celie tenderness, desire, and a glimpse of another life.

Shug eventually discovers Nettie’s hidden letters. Celie learns that Nettie has become a missionary in Africa alongside Samuel and Corrine, caring for Celie’s children, Adam and Olivia, who had been adopted after Alphonso took them away. Empowered by the news and by Shug’s love, Celie confronts Mister, leaves his house, and goes to Memphis with Shug. There she turns her skill at sewing pants into a thriving business, gains financial independence, and reclaims her home after learning that Alphonso was not her biological father.

Mister, chastened and lonely, gradually changes, while Sofia regains her freedom and reconciles with Harpo. At last, Nettie returns from Africa with Adam and Olivia, and Celie’s family is reunited.

The musical explores survival in the face of abuse, racism, poverty, and separation. It celebrates sisterhood, self-worth, queer love, forgiveness, and the hard-won freedom to define one’s own life.

dreamgirls.en:
In 1962, Effie White, Deena Jones, and Lorrell Robinson arrive at Harlem’s Apollo Theatre as the Dreamettes, hoping to win Amateur Night and begin a recording career. They lose the contest, but ambitious manager Curtis Taylor, Jr. notices them and secures them work as backup singers for flamboyant soul star James “Thunder” Early. Effie’s brother, C.C. White, writes their songs, while Jimmy’s agent Marty helps keep the touring act moving. After their first recording is appropriated and made popular by a white group, Curtis resolves to build an independent operation that will control the Dreamettes’ future.

As their profile rises, Curtis reshapes the trio into the Dreams. He moves the gentler, more conventionally marketable Deena into the lead position, pushing Effie to the background despite her extraordinary voice. Curtis and Deena begin an affair, while Effie—who loves Curtis and is carrying his child—finds herself increasingly isolated. Lorrell becomes entangled with Jimmy, whose career and personal life deteriorate as Curtis tries to polish the label’s image. On the night the Dreams are to make their Las Vegas debut, Effie refuses to perform after learning that Curtis has sidelined her completely. Curtis fires her and replaces her with Michelle Morris.

Years later, the Dreams become major pop stars under Deena’s lead, but success brings further fractures. C.C. resents Curtis’s commercial control, Lorrell recognizes the limits of her relationship with Jimmy, and Deena grows tired of being treated as Curtis’s creation rather than an artist in her own right. Effie struggles alone as a mother and singer until C.C. helps revive her career with “One Night Only.” Curtis attempts to suppress the record, but its success exposes his weakening hold. Deena leaves him to pursue acting, and the original trio reunites for a farewell performance, with Michelle joining them in solidarity.

The musical examines ambition, artistic ownership, love, and betrayal amid the machinery of fame. It asks what success costs when powerful people shape both an artist’s voice and identity.

ragtime.en:
At the dawn of the twentieth century, three households move through a rapidly changing New York. In New Rochelle, Mother manages the home while Father leaves on an Arctic expedition; their Little Boy, Mother’s Younger Brother, and Grandfather watch an ordered world begin to shift. In Harlem, ragtime pianist Coalhouse Walker Jr. searches for Sarah, the woman he loves. On the Lower East Side, Tateh, a Jewish immigrant from Latvia, struggles to support his Little Girl through silhouette-making and factory work.

Mother discovers Sarah and her newborn child abandoned near her house. Moved by compassion, she brings them into her care. Coalhouse comes to New Rochelle seeking Sarah and learns that he has a son. Though Sarah initially refuses him, his steady visits and music gradually reopen the possibility of their life together. When Coalhouse’s new Model T is vandalized by racist firemen, however, he insists that the men who harmed him be held accountable. Their refusal to offer justice turns his personal grievance into a public confrontation.

Sarah rushes forward at a campaign rally to plead Coalhouse’s case to a visiting vice-presidential candidate, but the candidate’s guards mistake her for an assassin and beat her to death. Devastated, Coalhouse gathers a band of followers and takes over J. P. Morgan’s library, demanding that his car be restored and that the responsible fire chief be surrendered. Younger Brother, transformed by the violence and injustice around him, joins Coalhouse’s cause. Mother attempts to save Coalhouse’s life through negotiation, but he ultimately gives himself up after securing protection for his son; he is then killed.

Elsewhere, Tateh escapes exploitation, discovers success by creating moving-picture entertainments, and becomes a prosperous producer. Father returns unable to regain his former place, while Mother grows increasingly independent. After Father dies during wartime, Mother and Tateh marry and form a new family with their children and Coalhouse’s son.

company.en:
At Bobby’s 35th birthday party in New York City, his married friends wonder why he remains unattached. Bobby moves through a series of visits and memories involving five couples—Sarah and Harry, Susan and Peter, Jenny and David, Amy and Paul, and Joanne and Larry—while the friends’ affectionate concern often becomes pressure for him to settle down. Sarah struggles with Harry’s drinking, yet insists that their difficult marriage is still worth preserving. Peter privately admits to Bobby that he has been unfaithful to Susan, then retreats from the truth. Jenny and David’s relationship exposes the mundane irritations that coexist with intimacy, while Amy panics on her wedding day and nearly abandons Paul before deciding to marry him.

Bobby also dates three single women. April, a naïve airline stewardess, is eager to please but cannot offer the deeper connection Bobby claims to want. Marta, a sophisticated young woman intoxicated by New York City, fascinates him with her independence; their brief encounter promises possibility but ends with her departure. Kathy, a warm and practical woman leaving New York for a new life, asks Bobby to go with her. He hesitates, unable to choose either commitment or solitude, and she leaves alone. Throughout these encounters, Bobby is welcomed into other people’s homes and lives but remains an observer, protected by charm and emotional distance.

As his friends gather again for another birthday celebration, their questions become harder for Bobby to evade. He begins to recognize that avoiding pain has also meant avoiding love. Instead of imagining marriage as a trap or a perfect refuge, he accepts that real connection requires vulnerability, compromise, and the willingness to be needed.

The musical explores loneliness amid companionship, the pressures surrounding marriage, and the fear of emotional commitment. It ultimately suggests that love is imperfect and risky, but isolation is not a safer alternative.

gypsy.en:
In Seattle, Rose Hovick drives her daughters, Baby June and Baby Louise, through the vaudeville circuit with an unyielding determination to make them stars. June is bright, gifted, and the centre of Rose’s carefully drilled child act; Louise, older and painfully shy, trails behind her. After Rose quarrels with her father over money, she takes the girls on the road and meets Herbie, a former agent now selling candy. Herbie becomes their manager and Rose’s devoted partner, building “Baby June and Her Newsboys” around June while Louise remains largely invisible.

Years pass, but Rose refuses to let the act grow up even as vaudeville declines and the children become young women. June, suffocated by the routine and Rose’s control, runs away with Tulsa, one of the boys in the act, to pursue her own career. Rose reacts by transferring every abandoned hope to Louise. Herbie, who wants a settled life and marriage, agrees to help Rose launch a new Louise-centred act, but Rose’s grand plans collapse when bookings disappear and the family is left stranded in Wichita.

To earn money, Rose pushes Louise into a burlesque house after a performer cannot go on. Louise initially panics, yet, encouraged by the other strippers—Tessie Tura, Mazeppa, and Electra—she learns that success depends on finding a distinctive “gimmick.” She turns her awkwardness into a teasing, self-possessed persona and emerges as Gypsy Rose Lee. Her popularity grows rapidly, while Rose, unable to accept that Louise’s success belongs to Louise alone, attempts to control the new act. Herbie finally leaves, appalled by Rose’s treatment of her daughter. In Gypsy’s dressing room at Minsky’s, Louise confronts Rose, demanding to know whether Rose’s lifelong ambitions were ever truly for her children. Rose is forced to acknowledge the dreams and identity she has pursued through them.

The musical examines ambition, parental control, and the price paid when love becomes entangled with achievement. It also traces Louise’s hard-won independence and Rose’s painful recognition of her own unmet desires.

newsies.en:
In 1899 New York City, Jack Kelly is the charismatic leader of a rough-knit group of newsboys who buy and sell copies of Joseph Pulitzer’s New York World. Jack longs to escape the city for Santa Fe, while his best friend Crutchie and the other newsies struggle to survive day by day. When Davey Jacobs and his young brother Les begin selling papers to help their family after their father is injured, Jack takes them under his wing. At the same time, Pulitzer raises the price the newsies must pay for their papers, shifting the cost of his business onto children who can scarcely afford to lose a cent.

Outraged, Jack and Davey unite Manhattan’s newsies in a strike. Their call spreads across the city, drawing support from Brooklyn’s leader, Spot Conlon, and from Katherine Plumber, an ambitious young reporter who recognizes the story’s importance. Katherine and Jack grow close as she helps turn the boys’ complaint into public news. Pulitzer answers ruthlessly: his men disrupt the strike, Crutchie is seized and sent to the Refuge, and Jack is offered money and a chance to flee if he abandons the others. For a moment, fear and the promise of freedom divide him from his friends.

Jack ultimately returns when he sees the newsies’ determination and learns that Katherine is Pulitzer’s daughter, working against her father’s injustice. With Katherine’s reporting and a daring plan to publish their own newspaper, the newsies expose Pulitzer’s treatment of them to the city. Their campaign attracts the attention of Governor Theodore Roosevelt, forcing Pulitzer to negotiate. He agrees to buy back unsold papers, reducing the financial risk that has trapped the boys. The strike ends in victory, and Jack chooses solidarity and a future with his friends over running away.
mtishows

The show’s themes are collective action, courage, and the belief that people dismissed as powerless can demand dignity. It also explores friendship, chosen family, and Jack’s movement from private escape toward shared responsibility.

hello dolly.en:
In turn-of-the-century Yonkers, New York, the indefatigable widow and matchmaker Dolly Gallagher Levi arrives at the hay and feed store of the wealthy, gruff Horace Vandergelder. Horace wants a new wife and has engaged Dolly to arrange a meeting with Irene Molloy, a widowed milliner in New York City. Dolly, however, quietly intends to become Horace’s bride herself. She also agrees to help Ambrose Kemper, a young artist who loves Horace’s niece, Ermengarde, despite Horace’s disapproval of their marriage.

When Horace leaves for New York to court Irene, his overworked clerks, Cornelius Hackl and Barnaby Tucker, seize their chance for a day of freedom in the city. Cornelius resolves to find romance, and the pair soon call at Irene’s hat shop, where Cornelius meets Irene and Barnaby meets her anxious assistant, Minnie Fay. Their flirtation is interrupted when Horace unexpectedly arrives. Cornelius and Barnaby hide in the shop, while Dolly maneuvers the increasingly bewildered guests through a series of explanations and near-discoveries. Horace’s planned engagement to Irene collapses as she becomes drawn to Cornelius instead, and Minnie finds unexpected happiness with Barnaby.

Dolly directs the whole company to the Harmonia Gardens Restaurant, where she makes a triumphant return after a long absence. There, misunderstandings multiply: Horace finds Cornelius and Barnaby enjoying the evening he believes they cannot afford, Irene and Minnie reject his authority, and Ambrose confronts him over Ermengarde. Dolly reveals that Horace has been cheated by his own rigid assumptions, while ensuring that the younger couples can marry. Back in Yonkers, Horace recognizes both his loneliness and his love for Dolly. She accepts him, on the condition that he welcome change, allow Cornelius to become his business partner, and give Ermengarde and Ambrose his blessing.
concordtheatricals

The musical celebrates the choice to rejoin life after grief, isolation, or routine. It values generosity, independence, romantic courage, and the pleasure of making room for other people’s happiness.

kiss me kate.en:
In Baltimore, a theatre company prepares to open its new musical, with director-producer-star Fred Graham playing Petruchio opposite his former wife, glamorous leading lady Lilli Vanessi, as Katharine. Their professional reunion is charged from the start: Lilli resents Fred’s flirtation with Lois Lane, the young actress playing Bianca, while Fred refuses to conceal his lingering attachment to Lilli. Lilli announces that she is engaged to the wealthy General Harrison Howell, yet a private moment with Fred rekindles old feelings. When Fred accidentally sends her flowers accompanied by a sentimental card intended for Lois, Lilli’s hopes collapse into fury.

Meanwhile, Lois’s boyfriend and co-star, Bill Calhoun, has skipped rehearsal to gamble. Deep in debt, he signs an IOU using Fred’s name. Two gangsters arrive at the theatre to collect the money and, when they learn that Fred does not owe it, insist on staying close until the debt is repaid. Opening night proceeds, and the boundaries between the backstage quarrels and the onstage story become increasingly blurred. Fred and Lilli’s arguments spill into performance; at one point, Fred humiliates Lilli before the audience, turning an apparent dramatic moment into a very real confrontation.

Determined not to endure Fred’s treatment, Lilli prepares to leave with General Howell. The gangsters, however, prevent her departure because the company must keep performing if Fred is to earn enough to cover Bill’s debt. Bill finally finds a way to settle his obligation, freeing Fred and the production from the criminals’ control. With the show’s climax approaching, Fred faces the prospect of losing Lilli for good. He appeals to her pride, her talent, and the love they have tried to deny. Lilli returns to the stage, and the two reunite as the performance reaches its conclusion.
concordtheatricals

The musical explores love as a contest of wit, pride, jealousy, and vulnerability, especially when private emotions must be managed in public. It also celebrates theatre itself: a place where performance and real life collide, and where reconciliation becomes possible.

camelot.en:
In a forest outside Camelot, the uneasy King Arthur awaits Guenevere, the bride chosen for him. Both try to escape the ceremony: Arthur hides in a tree, while Guenevere dreams of the simpler life she expects to lose. Arthur initially introduces himself as “Wart,” then wins her over with his vision of Camelot. Their unexpected affection turns duty into love, and they marry. With Guenevere’s encouragement, Arthur shapes a new order of knighthood: the Round Table, founded on the belief that strength must serve justice rather than conquest.

Years later, the celebrated French knight Sir Lancelot Du Lac arrives, certain that he is the perfect knight. Guenevere finds his pride unbearable and arranges for him to be challenged in a tournament, but he defeats the finest knights in Camelot. His courage and purity gradually transform her contempt into love. Lancelot, equally devoted to Guenevere, struggles against feelings he considers a betrayal of Arthur, while Arthur hopes the attraction will fade without destroying the fellowship he has built.

The danger instead grows within Arthur’s own family. Mordred, Arthur’s bitter illegitimate son, returns to court intent on exposing weakness and overturning the ideals of the Round Table. He discovers Guenevere and Lancelot together and turns their affair into a political weapon. Lancelot flees; Guenevere is condemned to burn at the stake under the laws Arthur himself has sworn to uphold. Torn between the woman he loves, his friend, and the rule of law, Arthur allows the sentence to stand. Lancelot rescues Guenevere, and civil war becomes unavoidable.

Before the final battle, Arthur meets Tom of Warwick, a boy inspired by Camelot’s ideals and eager to become a knight. Arthur charges him to remember and spread the vision of the Round Table, preserving its promise even as Camelot falls.
bard

The musical explores the tension between private desire and public duty, and the cost of trying to live by ideals in an imperfect world. It also insists that a noble vision can endure beyond the failure of the people who first attempted it.

brigadoon.en:
Lost while hunting in the Scottish Highlands, New Yorkers Tommy Albright and Jeff Douglas hear music drifting from an unknown village and follow it to Brigadoon. There they find a lively fair and villagers whose dress and customs seem to belong to another age. Andrew MacLaren and his daughters, Fiona and Jean, are preparing for Jean’s wedding to Charlie Dalrymple. Jean’s rejected admirer, Harry Beaton, broods nearby, while the worldly dairymaid Meg Brockie takes an immediate interest in Jeff. Tommy, although engaged to Jane Ashton in New York, is drawn to Fiona; during a day spent together among the hills, their attraction rapidly becomes love.

Tommy notices that the dates in the MacLaren family Bible are two centuries old. Mr. Lundie, the schoolmaster, explains Brigadoon’s secret: it emerges for only one day every hundred years, preserving its people from the changes of the outside world. No resident may leave, or Brigadoon and everyone in it will vanish forever. An outsider, however, might remain if love gives him the strength to abandon his former life.

Jean and Charlie marry amid celebration, but Harry disrupts the festivities after trying to claim Jean for himself. Desperate and embittered, he threatens to flee the village and destroy its miracle. The men pursue him; he dies during the chase, and the wedding day turns to mourning. Tommy resolves to stay with Fiona, but Jeff challenges him—and reveals that he accidentally caused Harry’s fatal fall. Shaken and unable to break completely with his old life, Tommy leaves as Brigadoon disappears into the mist.

Four months later, Tommy cannot forget Fiona. He ends his engagement to Jane, returns with Jeff to the Highlands, and finds only empty landscape. Then music returns, Mr. Lundie appears, and Tommy is welcomed into Brigadoon to reunite with Fiona.
mtishows

The musical centers on love as a force strong enough to demand choice, sacrifice, and faith. It contrasts a changing, skeptical modern world with an idealized community preserved by devotion, while asking whether a person can truly leave behind the life they have always known.

aida.en:
In the Egyptian Museum, Amneris’s statue comes to life and recalls the ancient story that shaped her reign. In Egypt, Captain Radames returns from an expedition with captured Nubian women, among them Aida, who conceals that she is Nubia’s princess. Radames gives her to Princess Amneris as a servant. Amneris is engaged to Radames, but their relationship is shallow, while Radames is increasingly drawn to the proud, defiant Aida. Aida, meanwhile, resists her growing feelings for the Egyptian officer and seeks a way to protect the Nubians held in bondage.

Radames’s father, Zoser, schemes to place his son on Egypt’s throne by hastening Radames’s marriage to Amneris and arranging the Pharaoh’s death. As political pressure mounts, Aida becomes a source of courage for the captive Nubians. When Radames and Aida finally acknowledge their love, their happiness is shadowed by the war between Egypt and Nubia. Aida’s father, King Amonasro, is captured, and she reunites with him while continuing to hide his identity. He urges her to use Radames’s devotion to help their people escape.

Radames plans to renounce power and flee with Aida to Nubia. But Zoser and the Egyptian forces discover the plot. Amonasro escapes, while Radames is arrested for treason. Amneris, devastated yet newly aware of the emptiness of the life prepared for her, offers Radames a chance to save himself if he will abandon Aida and accept their marriage. He refuses. The priests condemn him to be buried alive. Aida secretly joins him in the tomb, choosing to die beside him rather than live without him. In the present, Amneris accepts her responsibility as Pharaoh and uses her power to bring peace between Egypt and Nubia.
mtishows

The musical explores love tested by war, duty, class, and political power. It also contrasts personal sacrifice with the possibility that compassion and courage can end inherited conflict.

american idiot.en:
In Jingletown, USA, three restless friends—Johnny, Will, and Tunny—feel trapped by dead-end routines, family pressures, and the relentless noise of television culture. Calling himself the Jesus of Suburbia, Johnny dreams of escape. The three set out for the city, but their plan fractures almost immediately when Will learns that his girlfriend, Heather, is pregnant. He stays behind, promising to build a life with her, while Johnny and Tunny leave in search of possibility.

City life fails to provide the liberation Johnny and Tunny imagined. Tunny, overwhelmed and purposeless, is drawn to military recruitment and enlists. He is sent to war, where he is seriously wounded and loses a leg. During his recovery, he meets the Extraordinary Girl, a nurse whose tenderness gives him a reason to imagine a future beyond violence and loss.

Johnny remains in the city and falls for a young woman he calls Whatsername. Their relationship offers intimacy amid his isolation, but Johnny is increasingly consumed by drugs and by St. Jimmy, the charismatic, destructive figure who embodies his reckless impulses. Johnny’s addiction, anger, and self-sabotage strain his connection with Whatsername until she leaves him rather than be pulled into his downward spiral. Afterward, Johnny confronts St. Jimmy and rejects the life that has hollowed him out. He briefly tries to fit into a conventional working world, but finds that its promises of security do not answer his deeper confusion.

Back in Jingletown, Will becomes immobilised by depression and escapism. Heather, exhausted by his neglect and inability to participate in their new family life, leaves him. Eventually, Johnny returns home. Tunny also comes back, now changed by war but accompanied by the Extraordinary Girl. The three friends reunite, carrying the consequences of their choices and facing adulthood without the certainty they once sought.

The musical explores alienation, disillusionment, and the search for identity in a world shaped by media, war, addiction, and limited opportunity. It contrasts rage and escape with the difficult, unfinished work of love, responsibility, and self-acceptance.

godspell.en:
A discordant crowd of would-be philosophers argues over competing visions of truth until their voices collapse into chaos. John the Baptist arrives, calling the people to “Prepare Ye,” and gathers them into a new community. Jesus enters, asks John to baptize him, and then invites the company to join him in building a life shaped by mercy, trust, and shared responsibility. The group responds with exuberance, discovering a sense of purpose as they begin to follow him.

Jesus teaches through a sequence of playful parables, which the company turns into games, improvised scenes, comic routines, and songs. He urges them to settle conflicts, refrain from judging others, give without calculation, pray sincerely, and treat every person with the same care they would wish for themselves. The followers repeatedly test, misunderstand, and rediscover these lessons, but the ensemble grows closer as they learn to support one another. Judas, who has also served as John the Baptist, remains beside Jesus through much of this journey; their friendship gives the communal playfulness an increasingly uneasy undercurrent.

As the atmosphere darkens, Jesus condemns hypocrisy and mourns a world that resists compassion. At a final meal, he gathers his friends, blesses bread and wine, and asks them to remember him. Judas leads Jesus away, and the company watches helplessly as their teacher is taken to be crucified. Afterward, the grieving followers carry Jesus’ body away together. Yet the community he formed does not simply disperse: the company returns with renewed determination, carrying forward the teachings and affection that united them.

The show explores how a fractured group can become a community through empathy, forgiveness, and active love. It also contrasts joyful fellowship with betrayal, loss, and the difficult responsibility of living by one’s convictions.

assassins.en:
At a sinister carnival shooting gallery, the Proprietor invites a succession of discontented Americans to solve their problems by buying a gun and aiming at the President. John Wilkes Booth, Charles Guiteau, Leon Czolgosz, Giuseppe Zangara, Samuel Byck, Lynette “Squeaky” Fromme, Sara Jane Moore, and John Hinckley accept the invitation, joining an uneasy company that moves freely across different eras of American history. The Balladeer follows their stories, setting their private resentments against the public events they will violently interrupt.

Booth, embittered by the collapse of the Confederacy and his own thwarted ambitions, kills Abraham Lincoln at Ford’s Theatre, then retreats with David Herold to a barn, where he tries to turn murder into a heroic act. Guiteau, vain and deluded, stalks President James Garfield at a railway station, convinced that his act will make him famous and politically indispensable. Czolgosz, a lonely factory worker drawn to Emma Goldman’s radical politics, wrestles with whether killing President William McKinley can make a meaningful difference. Zangara, tormented by poverty and physical pain, fires at Franklin D. Roosevelt in Miami and is seized by the crowd.

Elsewhere, Fromme and Moore bungle separate attempts on President Gerald Ford; Hinckley frames his desire to impress Jodie Foster as a grand romantic gesture; and Byck records furious messages for Leonard Bernstein and President Richard Nixon before attempting to hijack an airplane and crash it into the White House. Each assassin finds brief fellowship with the others, but no lasting resolution.

The action finally reaches the Texas School Book Depository in 1963, where Lee Harvey Oswald prepares to take his own life. The assassins appear to him, urging him instead to shoot President John F. Kennedy. Oswald fires, and the Balladeer’s attempt to restore order is overwhelmed by the consequences of that act.

The musical portrays violence as an extreme response to humiliation, loneliness, frustration, and a belief that the country has denied its promises. Its assassins seek recognition and control, yet their imagined victories expose the destructive cost of turning private grievance into public violence.

merrily we roll along.en:
At a glittering 1976 Hollywood party, film producer Franklin Shepard appears to have everything: wealth, fame, a new hit, and the company of his leading lady, Meg. Yet the evening exposes the wreckage beneath the success. His former writing partner, Charley Kringas, is absent after a bitter break, while Mary Flynn—once Franklin’s closest friend—arrives resentful, lonely, and drunk. Franklin’s wife, Gussie Carnegie, confronts him about Meg, and Mary’s furious toast condemns the shallow world Franklin has chosen before she leaves.

The action then moves backward through the years. In New York, Franklin’s marriage to Beth Shepard collapses amid his affair with Gussie and his growing attraction to Hollywood money and influence. He and Charley, once an admired songwriting team, disagree increasingly over artistic ambition: Franklin wants commercial opportunities, including selling their work for film, while Charley believes their partnership should remain devoted to theatre. Mary tries to keep peace between them, though she quietly loves Franklin and watches helplessly as his choices push the three friends apart.

Earlier still, the trio celebrate professional breakthroughs, including the success of Franklin and Charley’s musical. Gussie, then married to producer Joe Josephson, draws Franklin into a more glamorous and compromising life. As Franklin becomes less available to Beth, Charley, and Mary, each friendship and marriage begins to carry the seeds of its later failure.

Finally, the story reaches 1957, when Franklin, Charley, and Mary are young neighbours in New York, full of confidence and shared purpose. On a rooftop, they make a pact to pursue their dreams together: Franklin will compose, Charley will write lyrics and plays, and Mary will write a novel. With the city spread beneath them, they imagine a future untouched by disappointment.

The musical examines how success, romantic desire, and compromise can erode loyalty and artistic ideals. By ending at the friends’ hopeful beginning, it makes their later losses feel both poignant and tragically foreseeable.

grand hotel.en:
In 1928 Berlin, the Grand Hotel receives a glittering procession of guests, each hiding a private crisis behind elegance and ceremony. Colonel Doctor Otternschlag, a wounded, morphine-dependent observer, watches as the hotel’s lives briefly collide. Otto Kringelein, a timid bookkeeper dying from a terminal illness, resolves to spend his savings extravagantly before it is too late. The charming but penniless Baron Felix von Gaigern befriends Otto and helps him enter the hotel’s luxurious world, while secretly planning to steal jewels from the fading Russian ballerina, Elizaveta Grushinskaya.

Elizaveta arrives convinced that her career and desirability have ended. Her devoted companion Raffaela tries to protect her from humiliation and financial disaster, but Felix’s attention restores Elizaveta’s sense of possibility. He abandons his intended theft and shares a romantic night with her, promising a future he cannot honestly provide. Elsewhere, Flaemmchen, an ambitious typist who dreams of becoming a film star, accepts compromising work from Hermann Preysing, the ruthless General Director of Saxonia Mills. Preysing is desperate to secure a business merger and turns increasingly aggressive when his plans begin to fail.

Otto, newly awakened to pleasure and friendship, is drawn to Flaemmchen, who recognizes his gentleness despite their unequal circumstances. Felix sees a chance to help them both: he intends to steal money from Preysing, then send Otto and Flaemmchen away together. But Preysing catches Felix during the attempted robbery and kills him. The death is treated as an inconvenience to be contained; Elizaveta, unaware of Felix’s fate, leaves Berlin expecting their reunion, while Otto and Flaemmchen depart toward an uncertain but hopeful future. Around them, hotel staff continue their routines, and guests keep arriving.

The musical explores the precariousness beneath wealth, glamour, and social status. It sets fleeting love and human connection against mortality, exploitation, loneliness, and a world that carries on with startling indifference.

city of angels.en:
In late-1940s Hollywood, screenwriter Stine is adapting his detective story for the movies while battling the demands of powerful producer Buddy Fidler. As Stine struggles to protect his work from rewrites, casting pressures, and commercial compromise, the hard-boiled film he is writing unfolds alongside his life. Its hero is Stone, a Los Angeles private investigator who begins the story wounded on a hospital gurney, then recalls the case that brought him there.

A wealthy, seductive client, Alaura Kingsley, hires Stone to locate her missing stepdaughter, Mallory. With the help of his devoted secretary, Oolie, Stone enters the Kingsley family’s treacherous world of wealth, jealousy, blackmail, and murder. He encounters Alaura’s resentful husband Luther, her stepson Peter, the dangerous Big Six, and a succession of criminals, officials, and possible suspects. The more Stone investigates Mallory’s disappearance, the more the case becomes a trap: evidence points toward him, enemies close in, and the people who appear most helpful prove capable of betrayal. Stone’s loyalty to Oolie and his growing recognition of Alaura’s duplicity leave him increasingly isolated.

Meanwhile, Stine’s marriage to Gabby frays as Hollywood absorbs him. Gabby resents being left behind in New York and later arrives in Los Angeles, where Stine’s compromises—and his attraction to the glamorous world around him—make reconciliation difficult. Buddy repeatedly alters the screenplay, pushing Stine to transform its characters and ending into something safer and more marketable. Stine’s frustrations spill into the fictional story, where Stone begins to resist the manipulations imposed on him. As the two narratives converge, Stone exposes the conspiracy behind Mallory’s disappearance and clears his name, while Stine finally confronts Buddy over who controls the story. Both men must decide whether survival requires surrendering their principles or reclaiming their own voices.

The musical examines the conflict between artistic integrity and commercial power, especially in a Hollywood where image and profit distort truth. It also plays with identity, desire, loyalty, and betrayal, showing how creators and characters alike can become trapped by the stories others demand of them.

titanic.en:
At Southampton’s Ocean Dock, the RMS Titanic prepares to depart on her maiden voyage to New York. Thomas Andrews takes pride in the unprecedented scale of the liner he designed, while J. Bruce Ismay celebrates its commercial prestige and Captain E. J. Smith accepts the burden of commanding it. Crew members including stoker Frederick Barrett, lookout Frederick Fleet, wireless operator Harold Bride, officer Murdoch, and Chief Steward Henry Etches take up their posts. Across the decks, passengers of every class board with radically different expectations: Kate McGowan and other Third Class emigrants imagine a new life in America; Alice and Edgar Beane hope that proximity to wealth will elevate their status; and First Class figures such as John Jacob Astor, Benjamin Guggenheim, and Isidor and Ida Straus enjoy the privileges they believe their position ensures.

As the ship sails into the Atlantic, private ambitions and pressures emerge. Barrett longs to leave the hardship of the coal mines behind. Murdoch considers the responsibility of leadership, while Andrews sees in the ship a culmination of human progress. Ismay urges greater speed, hoping the crossing will demonstrate Titanic’s superiority. In the wireless room, Bride and his colleagues handle the steady stream of messages, including warnings of ice ahead. The warning signs do not overcome the confidence of those directing the voyage.

Late on 14 April, Fleet spots an iceberg. Despite urgent action on the bridge, Titanic collides with it, and Andrews quickly understands that the damage will doom the ship. The orderly world of the voyage collapses into confusion as officers uncover the inadequacy of the lifeboats and passengers struggle to comprehend the danger. Women and children are sent toward the boats; men confront separation, duty, fear, and sacrifice. Some cling to convention and wealth, while others discover courage or despair. As the ship sinks, individual stories converge in a final ordeal of loss and survival.
concordtheatricals

The musical explores human faith in progress meeting the limits of nature and circumstance. It also examines class, aspiration, responsibility, love, and the moral choices made when certainty vanishes.

once on this island.en:
Storytellers on a Caribbean island begin with the tale of Ti Moune, an orphaned child who survives a fierce storm and is raised with tenderness by Mama Euralie and Tonton Julian. The island is governed by four powerful gods: Asaka, Mother of the Earth; Agwe, god of Water; Erzulie, goddess of Love; and Papa Ge, Demon of Death. As Ti Moune grows into a curious, hopeful young woman, the gods debate whether love or death holds greater power. Their wager will be decided through her life.

During another violent storm, Daniel Beauxhomme, a wealthy young grand homme from the other side of the island, crashes his car near Ti Moune’s village. She finds him badly injured and, overwhelmed by love, pleads for his life. Papa Ge offers a bargain: Daniel will live if Ti Moune gives him her life when he comes to claim it. She accepts. Once Daniel recovers, his people return him to the protected world of the grands hommes, leaving Ti Moune behind.

Determined to be reunited with him, Ti Moune crosses the dividing line between the peasant side and the wealthy side of the island. Daniel welcomes her into his home, and their love becomes impossible for the upper-class community to ignore. Yet his father, Armand Beauxhomme, regards Ti Moune as an unacceptable match, while Daniel is expected to marry Andrea Devereaux. Under pressure, Daniel chooses Andrea and asks Ti Moune to leave.

Papa Ge returns to demand his payment, offering Ti Moune a way out: she can kill Daniel and live. She refuses, insisting that genuine love cannot destroy the beloved. Papa Ge takes her life instead. The gods transform Ti Moune into a tree whose roots and branches break through the wall dividing the island’s people, creating a path between the two communities.
mtishows

Love, sacrifice, and the struggle against death stand at the center of the show. It also confronts divisions of class and colour, ultimately imagining compassion and human connection as forces capable of crossing boundaries.

pajama game.en:
At the Sleep-Tite Pajama Factory in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, the workforce is pressing management for a long-delayed seven-and-a-half-cent hourly raise. The workers’ frustration is sharpened by the relentless efficiency demands of Vernon Hines, the factory’s time-study man, and by the hard-line refusal of company president Myron Hasler to increase wages. Into this tense workplace arrives Sid Sorokin, the new superintendent, determined to prove himself in an unfamiliar town. His first clash is with Katherine “Babe” Williams, the principled leader of the Union Grievance Committee, when she investigates his confrontation with a worker. Their political loyalties place them on opposing sides, but an immediate attraction soon complicates the dispute.

At the company picnic, Sid’s concern for Babe during Hines’s reckless knife-throwing act helps bring them closer. Later, at Babe’s home, they admit their feelings and begin a romance despite her warning that the wage struggle may divide them. The warning proves correct: Hasler rejects the union’s demand, the workers begin a slowdown, and Babe causes a factory-wide stoppage. Sid, under pressure to maintain production, fires her. Hurt but still in love, both try unsuccessfully to separate private feeling from public conflict.

Meanwhile, Hines’s obsessive jealousy of Hasler’s secretary, Gladys Hotchkiss, turns their unstable relationship into comic chaos. At Hernando’s Hideaway, Sid obtains access to Hasler’s ledger and discovers the truth: Hasler has already built the cost of the raise into the company accounts while withholding it from the workers. When defective pajama production and the prospect of lost customers increase the pressure, Sid confronts Hasler with evidence of the deception. He forces an agreement: the workers will receive their seven-and-a-half-cent raise, though not retroactively.

The settlement reunites Sid and Babe, while Hines resolves to trust Gladys. The factory community celebrates both the labor victory and the prospect of happier relationships.
mtishows

The musical explores the collision between love and loyalty when personal desires are tested by workplace inequality. It also treats collective action, dignity at work, and mutual trust with a buoyant comic spirit.

bye bye birdie.en:
When rock-and-roll idol Conrad Birdie is drafted into the U.S. Army, his departure threatens to ruin Albert Peterson, the anxious songwriter and manager whose business depends on the singer’s success. Albert’s sharp, long-suffering secretary and girlfriend, Rosie Alvarez, devises a publicity scheme: Conrad will record Albert’s new song, “One Last Kiss,” and perform it on television before giving a farewell kiss to a randomly selected teenage fan. The chosen girl is Kim MacAfee of Sweet Apple, Ohio, who has just begun going steady with the jealous Hugo Peabody and is trying to present herself as newly grown-up.

Albert, Rosie, Conrad, and the press descend on Sweet Apple, where the planned kiss quickly unsettles the MacAfee household. Kim is thrilled by the attention, Hugo is humiliated, and Kim’s father, Harry MacAfee, alternates between outrage over Conrad’s influence and delight at the prospect of appearing on national television. Meanwhile, Albert’s domineering mother, Mae Peterson, continues to interfere in Albert and Rosie’s relationship, pushing him to abandon Rosie and reinforcing his habit of avoiding adult commitments.

Conrad’s arrival sends the town into a frenzy. His rebellious swagger fascinates the teenagers and infuriates the adults, while the actual farewell kiss becomes ever harder to stage. Hugo confronts Conrad, Kim’s feelings are tested, and a confused chain of events turns the television event into a public disaster. Conrad escapes the chaos, leaving Albert’s carefully arranged campaign in ruins and exposing the tensions among the couples and families involved.

In the aftermath, Albert finally recognizes how thoroughly fear and his mother’s influence have controlled him. He chooses Rosie, and the troubled relationships begin to find their footing as Sweet Apple returns to normal.

The show satirizes celebrity worship, generational conflict, and the tendency of adults to panic over youthful culture. It also follows its characters’ uneven movement toward independence, honest commitment, and a more mature sense of love.

kiss of the spider woman.en:
In an Argentine prison, Luis Alberto Molina, a sensitive window dresser serving an eight-year sentence, survives the brutality of confinement through fantasies of glamorous films and their luminous star, Aurora. To him, Aurora is many women at once: a radiant singer, a tragic lover, and, most terrifyingly, the Spider Woman, whose kiss brings death. His fragile refuge is disrupted when Valentín Arregui Paz, a tortured Marxist revolutionary, is thrown into his cell. Ill, furious, and determined not to betray his comrades, Valentín rejects Molina’s chatter and draws a line across the floor to keep him away.

Yet Molina quietly tends to Valentín after the guards’ interrogations, soothing him with stories and visions of Aurora. Their guarded conversations gradually reveal private wounds: Valentín’s longing for Marta, the woman he loves, and Molina’s yearning for affection from Gabriel, a waiter who has never returned it. The Warden, hoping to extract information about Valentín’s political network, exploits Molina’s concern for his ailing mother and promises him a chance at release if he can obtain useful intelligence. Molina is caught between fear, hope, and a loyalty he does not initially understand.

When poisoned food weakens both men, Molina protects Valentín from further interrogation and nurses him through the fever. Their intimacy deepens into love, and Valentín eventually entrusts Molina with a message for his comrades outside the prison. Molina agrees to carry it after his release, despite the danger. Once free, he attempts to make the calls, but prison agents follow him. Wounded in the street, Molina imagines Aurora waiting for him; the Spider Woman embraces him with her fatal kiss. Back in prison, Valentín endures renewed torture but retreats into a final vision of freedom and reunion.

The musical explores how imagination can preserve dignity amid terror, isolation, and political repression. It contrasts fear with compassion, showing love and solidarity emerging between two people whom the world has taught to distrust one another.

full monty.en:
In Buffalo, New York, the closing of the steel mills has left Jerry Lukowski, Dave Bukatinsky, and countless other workers without jobs, money, or direction. Jerry’s situation is urgent: he is behind on child-support payments to his estranged wife, Pam, and risks losing time with their young son, Nathan. Dave, meanwhile, feels diminished by unemployment and embarrassed by his weight, straining his relationship with his wife, Georgie. When Jerry and Dave secretly observe Georgie and her friends at a Chippendales-style show at Tony Giordano’s club, they realize that women will eagerly pay to see male performers strip. Jerry proposes a homemade rival act, promising that their men will be more authentic—and that they will go “the full monty.”

They begin recruiting a mismatched group of men: lonely security guard Malcolm MacGregor; former supervisor Harold Nichols, who hides his unemployment from his wife, Vicki; Ethan Girard, whose easy confidence masks his own vulnerabilities; and Noah “Horse” T. Simmons, an older retired mill worker. Their unlikely rehearsals are guided by Jeanette Burmeister, a blunt, seasoned pianist who sees potential beneath their awkwardness. As the men learn to dance, they confront fears that go far beyond performing: Jerry’s anxiety about being a failure as a father, Dave’s shame about his body, Malcolm’s isolation, Harold’s terror of disappointing Vicki, and the group’s ingrained ideas about masculinity.

Complications threaten the show and the men’s friendships, but their mutual support gradually changes them. Jerry comes to understand that Nathan needs honesty and commitment rather than grand promises, while Dave begins to accept Georgie’s love and his own worth. On opening night, with their families and the women of Buffalo filling the club, the six men take the stage. After teasing the audience with the question of whether they will truly bare everything, they find the nerve to finish their act together.

The musical explores unemployment, self-worth, friendship, intimacy, and the pressures men place on themselves to appear strong. Its central triumph is the men’s decision to trade shame and isolation for trust, courage, and solidarity.

drowsy chaperone.en:
In the apartment of the Man in Chair, a devoted musical-theatre fan seeks comfort by playing the cast recording of a fictional 1928 musical, The Drowsy Chaperone. As he narrates and interrupts the action, the story unfolds at the Long Island estate of the wealthy Mrs. Tottendale, where Broadway star Janet Van De Graaff is preparing to marry oil tycoon Robert Martin. Janet intends to abandon the stage, alarming her producer, Mr. Feldzieg, who fears losing the star of Feldzieg’s Follies. Feldzieg enlists two Gangsters, disguised as pastry chefs, to sabotage the marriage, and orders the flamboyant Latin lover Aldolpho to seduce Janet. Meanwhile, Janet’s Drowsy Chaperone is meant to keep the bride and groom apart until the ceremony, but is more interested in drinking and causing mischief.

Robert, desperate to prove himself worthy, performs a blindfolded roller-skating feat while Janet tests his trust with a disguised flirtation. The prank backfires: Robert believes Janet has betrayed him and calls off the wedding. Feldzieg presses his advantage, hoping Janet will return to the theatre, while Kitty, his ambitious but untalented companion, dreams of taking Janet’s place in the Follies. Aldolpho arrives to carry out his seduction, but instead becomes captivated by the Chaperone. The Gangsters’ threats and Feldzieg’s schemes unravel amid escalating confusion, as George, Robert’s anxious best man, struggles to keep the ceremony from collapsing.

At last, Janet and Robert recognize that their love survives Janet’s foolish test. They reunite just as Trix the Aviatrix lands her plane at the estate. With the original minister unavailable, Trix conducts the wedding, and the Chaperone and Aldolpho also pair off. The show’s happy ending is disrupted when the record skips and the Man in Chair’s apartment briefly loses power, but the music resumes and the wedding reaches its exuberant conclusion.
mtishows

The show celebrates the restorative pleasure of musical theatre, fantasy, and a neatly engineered happy ending. It also affectionately satirizes theatrical clichés—romantic misunderstandings, melodramatic plots, glamorous stars, and improbable rescues—while finding emotional solace in them.

a gentlemans guide to love and murder.en:
In 1909, Lord Montague “Monty” D’Ysquith Navarro sits in prison on the eve of his possible execution, writing the account of how he became the Ninth Earl of Highhurst. Two years earlier, after the death of his mother, the impoverished Monty learns from Miss Shingle that he belongs—through his disowned mother—to the powerful D’Ysquith family. He is eighth in line to the earldom, but Lord Adalbert D’Ysquith coldly rejects him when Monty seeks recognition. Embittered, and eager to win the mercenary Sibella Hallward, who refuses to marry a poor clerk, Monty resolves to remove the relatives standing between himself and the title.

A series of extraordinary mishaps and carefully engineered deaths follows. Monty first sends the clergyman Reverend Lord Ezekial D’Ysquith plunging from the top of a church bell tower, then engineers increasingly unlikely ends for the other heirs: the do-gooding Lady Hyacinth D’Ysquith de Haut-Picq, sent on ever more dangerous charitable missions overseas, drowns in the harbor when the gangplank gives way beneath her; the actress Lady Salome D’Ysquith Pumphrey dies onstage; the weightlifting Major Lord Bartholomew D’Ysquith is crushed beneath an overloaded barbell; and Henry D’Ysquith, a devoted beekeeper, is stung to death by his own bees. Along the way, Monty meets the warm, intelligent Phoebe D’Ysquith, and their affection grows into love.

As his path clears, Monty becomes engaged to Phoebe, while Sibella—now unhappily married to Lionel Holland—reappears and resumes their affair. Monty’s double life nearly collapses when both women arrive at his rooms on the same evening. Meanwhile, the final D’Ysquith heir, Lord Adalbert, survives an assassination attempt and turns against Monty. Monty eventually inherits the earldom, but is arrested for murdering Lord Adalbert after Sibella’s husband is found dead in Monty’s home. At trial, Sibella unexpectedly provides an alibi, and Monty is acquitted. He discovers, however, that Phoebe has secretly preserved the evidence of his crimes, leaving him beholden to both women.

The musical turns ambition, inherited privilege, and murder into dark farce. It asks whether social status can corrupt an apparently ordinary man—and whether love, desire, and self-interest can ever be cleanly separated.

natasha pierre and the great comet of 18.en:
In Moscow, the young and idealistic Natasha Rostova arrives with her cousin Sonya, hoping to reunite with her fiancé, Andrey Bolkonsky, who is away with the army. Andrey’s stern father, Prince Bolkonsky, and his sister Marya reject Natasha, making her wait for his return. Lonely and humiliated, Natasha finds brief comfort among Moscow society, especially with the warm-hearted Pierre Bezukhov, a wealthy but unhappy man trapped in a loveless marriage to the glamorous, manipulative Hélène. At an opera, Natasha is dazzled by the spectacle and becomes the target of Hélène’s brother Anatole Kuragin, an irresistibly charming but reckless officer. Though Anatole is already secretly married, Hélène encourages his pursuit, while his friend Dolokhov helps devise a plan for him and Natasha to elope.

Anatole’s attention awakens Natasha’s longing for freedom, romance, and certainty. She convinces herself that she loves him and breaks with Andrey, despite Sonya’s desperate warnings. Marya D. tries to protect Natasha, but Natasha refuses to listen. On the night of the planned elopement, Sonya alerts Marya D., who calls on Pierre for help. Pierre confronts Anatole and forces him to leave Moscow, ending the scheme before Natasha can run away. The truth devastates Natasha: Anatole has deceived her, her engagement to Andrey is ruined, and the life she imagined has collapsed. In despair, she attempts suicide with arsenic but survives.

Pierre visits Natasha during her recovery. He does not excuse what happened, yet he sees her suffering with compassion rather than judgment. He tells her that, if he were free, he would ask for her hand, offering a fragile possibility of forgiveness and renewed life. Natasha is left changed by the consequences of her choices, while Pierre begins to recognize the tenderness and purpose missing from his own life.
