The musical explores desire, self-deception, betrayal, and the painful collision between youthful fantasy and reality. It ultimately finds grace in empathy: people may wound one another and themselves, yet compassion can create the possibility of survival and transformation.

scottsboro boys.en:
In 1955, an unnamed Lady waits at a bus stop, holding a cake box whose contents stir an overwhelming memory. The world around her gives way to a minstrel-show frame led by the Interlocutor, Mr. Bones, and Mr. Tambo, who introduce the story of Haywood Patterson and eight other Black youths: Olen Montgomery, Clarence Norris, Ozie Powell, Willie Roberson, Eugene Williams, Andy Wright, Roy Wright, and Charles Weems. In 1931, the boys ride a freight train toward Memphis when it is stopped in Alabama. Victoria Price and Ruby Bates, two white women travelling on the train, are discovered by police and accuse the boys of rape. The boys are arrested in Scottsboro, hurried into court, represented ineffectively, convicted despite the absence of a credible defence, and sent to Kilby Prison to await execution.

Haywood becomes the group’s voice, insisting on their innocence while the youngest, Eugene, is haunted by the prospect of the electric chair. At the last moment, the convictions are overturned, but freedom does not follow. A new trial brings attention, outside supporters, and a celebrated defence lawyer, Samuel Leibowitz; it also exposes the hostility of the Alabama courtroom and the difficulty of securing justice within it. Ruby Bates repudiates her accusation, yet the proceedings continue to turn against the boys. Years pass through repeated trials, imprisonment, violence, illness, and separation. Haywood learns to read and write, clings to dignity, and dreams of home, while the others are gradually released, escaped, or broken by the system. He remains imprisoned the longest, eventually emerging into a changed America only to find that his past has not released him.

The musical confronts racial injustice, state power, and the devastating human cost of a system that denies people a fair hearing. Its minstrel-show form turns performance itself into an indictment, asking how suffering is remembered, witnessed, and turned into public spectacle.

light in the piazza.en:
In the summer of 1953, Margaret Johnson travels through Italy with her adult daughter, Clara. While visiting Florence’s Piazza della Signoria, Clara’s hat is caught by the wind and lands at the feet of Fabrizio Naccarelli, a warm-hearted young Florentine. An immediate attraction grows between them, but Margaret is determined to prevent it from becoming serious. Clara appears innocent and impulsive for her age because a childhood accident left her with an intellectual disability, a fact Margaret has long concealed and managed through constant protection.

 To keep the pair apart, Margaret abruptly takes Clara to Rome, but Fabrizio follows them. His father, Signor Naccarelli, initially regards Clara as a promising match for Fabrizio, especially compared with Fabrizio’s unhappy brother Giuseppe and Giuseppe’s resentful wife Franca.

 Margaret’s anxiety deepens as Fabrizio and Clara’s romance intensifies. She worries that Clara cannot understand marriage or sexual intimacy, and that Fabrizio will eventually discover what has been hidden from him. Meanwhile, Margaret confronts the emptiness of her own marriage to Roy, who has remained in America, and begins to recognize how much of Clara’s life she has controlled out of fear.

 Fabrizio asks Clara to marry him, and Clara, moved by love and the possibility of independence, accepts. Margaret tries to halt the wedding by telling Signor Naccarelli about Clara’s condition. After meeting Clara and seeing the sincerity between the young couple, he chooses not to stop the marriage. When Fabrizio learns the truth, he is shocked, but he ultimately decides that his love for Clara matters more than Margaret’s objections. As Clara and Fabrizio prepare to begin their life together in Italy, Margaret faces the painful, liberating necessity of letting her daughter go.

The musical explores love as a leap beyond certainty, judgment, and social expectation. It also examines a mother’s fear of loss, the boundary between protection and control, and the possibility of freedom found through accepting another person as they are.

caroline or change.en:
In Lake Charles, Louisiana, in 1963, Caroline Thibodeaux spends her days in the overheated basement of the Gellman home, washing clothes for a white Jewish family while raising four children on a meagre wage. The basement becomes a heightened inner world, animated by the Washing Machine, Dryer, Radio, Moon and Bus, as Caroline endures the exhausting routine of work and the resentments she rarely permits herself to voice. Upstairs, eight-year-old Noah Gellman is grieving his late mother and struggling to accept Rose Stopnick Gellman, his well-meaning new stepmother. His father, Stuart Gellman, remains distant in his own grief, leaving Noah to seek comfort in Caroline’s steady, unsentimental presence.

Noah idolises Caroline and repeatedly comes downstairs to be near her. Their bond has limits that Noah cannot fully understand: Caroline cares for him but will not become the mother he wants her to be. When Rose learns that Noah often leaves coins in his trouser pockets, she tells Caroline to keep any change found in the laundry rather than return it. Caroline initially resists taking money from a child, but her financial need—and the needs of her children, including her outspoken teenage daughter Emmie—make refusal increasingly difficult. Noah begins deliberately leaving coins behind, believing the gesture will draw him closer to Caroline.

The arrangement breaks when Noah hides a twenty-dollar bill in Caroline’s laundry supplies. Caroline takes it, and Noah’s discovery of the loss leads to a painful confrontation. His hurt and sense of betrayal collide with Caroline’s anger at being reduced to a servant whose dignity and hardship remain invisible. Around them, news of civil-rights activism, racial violence, and President Kennedy’s assassination makes the wider upheaval impossible to ignore. Emmie embraces the possibility of a changed future, while Caroline faces the uncertain cost of change in her own life.
mtishows

The musical examines race, class, grief, family, and the unequal emotional burdens hidden within domestic life. It asks whether personal affection can survive structures of power—and what it takes to claim dignity when the world is beginning to transform.

passion.en:
In 1863 Italy, Captain Giorgio Bachetti arrives at a remote military outpost after a passionate affair in Milan with Clara, a beautiful married woman. Their relationship is sustained through letters and brief visits, and Giorgio believes their love offers an escape from the dullness and isolation of army life. At the fort he meets Colonel Ricci, the kindly Doctor Tambourri, and Fosca, the colonel’s cousin: a frail, intensely unhappy woman who suffers from seizures and lives largely secluded from the other officers. Fosca is immediately drawn to Giorgio. At first he responds with pity and discomfort, especially after she becomes overwrought at the thought that he might leave. Yet, urged by the doctor and colonel to treat her gently, Giorgio begins visiting her and reading to her.

Fosca’s attachment soon becomes consuming. She writes Giorgio a declaration of love and demands emotional devotion in return; he recoils, insisting that he cannot love her. Meanwhile, Clara’s letters and a clandestine visit renew Giorgio’s happiness, though their affair remains constrained by her marriage and his military obligations. Fosca grows increasingly desperate, interpreting Giorgio’s distance as cruelty and falling seriously ill. When Giorgio tries to end their connection, she attempts to take her own life. Overcome by guilt and compassion, he agrees to see her again.

As Fosca gradually recovers, Giorgio’s feelings change in ways he cannot easily explain. He comes to recognize the depth, intelligence, and absolute vulnerability beneath her demands. Clara offers him sensual joy and tenderness, but Fosca forces him to confront a love stripped of comfort, beauty, and self-protection. When Giorgio is ordered to leave the fort, Fosca begs him to take her with him. In a final emotional confrontation, he acknowledges that he loves her. She dies in his arms, and Giorgio is left shattered, haunted by the force of what they shared.

The musical explores passion as an overwhelming, transformative force rather than a pleasant romantic ideal. It contrasts desire, duty, pity, illness, beauty, and mortality, asking whether love’s deepest truth may lie in the willingness to be changed by another person completely.

big fish.en:
Edward Bloom has spent his life turning every memory into a larger-than-life adventure. As he lies ill in hospital, his adult son, Will, struggles to reconcile the exuberant storyteller he knows with the father he feels he has never truly understood. Preparing for the birth of his own child, Will becomes increasingly determined to learn which parts of Edward’s extraordinary tales are real—and why Edward has always seemed more comfortable with fantasy than honesty.

Edward’s stories begin with his restless youth in Ashton, Alabama, where he leaves home seeking a life beyond the ordinary. He encounters Karl, a gentle giant; a witch whose glass eye reveals glimpses of the future; and the isolated, idealistic town of Spectre, whose residents invite him to stay forever. Continuing his journey, Edward meets Amos Calloway, a charismatic ringmaster with a surprising secret, and agrees to work for him in exchange for clues about Sandra, the beautiful woman Edward is certain he is meant to marry. Edward pursues Sandra with flamboyant devotion, eventually winning her heart and building a life with her despite the disruptions of war and adulthood.

As Will presses Edward for facts, their conversations uncover the strain beneath the family’s affection. Will suspects that Edward’s frequent absences concealed betrayals, especially after hearing of Jenny Hill, a woman connected to one of Edward’s old adventures. Yet the truth is more complicated: Edward’s tales may be embellished, but the emotions and loyalties within them are genuine. In Edward’s final days, Will finds a way to enter his father’s imaginative world rather than reject it. He creates a final story in which Edward escapes the hospital, journeys to the river, and is greeted by the friends, strangers, and legends who have filled his life. Edward becomes the great fish of his own tale, and Will finally understands the love behind the storytelling.

The musical explores the tension between fact and imagination, and the ways families try to know one another across disappointment and time. It ultimately suggests that stories can preserve emotional truth, allowing love, memory, and identity to outlast a life.

prom.en:
After a disastrous opening night leaves four fading Broadway performers desperate for attention, Dee Dee Allen, Barry Glickman, Angie Dickinson, and Trent Oliver search for a public cause that can restore their reputations. Their press agent, Sheldon Saperstein, finds a news story from Edgewater, Indiana: Emma Nolan, a high-school student, has been barred from bringing her girlfriend to the prom. The PTA, led by Mrs. Greene, has cancelled the dance rather than permit Emma to attend with a female date. The performers descend on Edgewater, convinced they can become heroes while attracting press coverage.

Emma is already isolated by classmates and hurt by the public scrutiny, while her girlfriend Alyssa Greene remains closeted. Alyssa is Mrs. Greene’s daughter and fears losing her mother’s approval if their relationship becomes known. Principal Tom Hawkins supports Emma and tries to secure an inclusive prom through official channels, but the visiting actors’ flamboyant protests initially create more conflict and make Emma’s situation harder. Dee Dee in particular treats the campaign as a performance opportunity, while Barry recognizes that Emma’s experience echoes his own painful adolescence.

As pressure builds, Emma and Alyssa attempt to attend a privately arranged prom, only for Emma to be cruelly humiliated when the event proves to be a trap. Devastated, she considers leaving Edgewater. Barry reaches her in time and offers the compassion he once needed himself. Meanwhile, Alyssa finally confronts her mother and publicly declares her love for Emma. Mrs. Greene begins to face the damage caused by her actions, and the town’s resistance weakens.

The Broadway group, altered by their involvement, helps organize a genuine, inclusive prom. Emma and Alyssa dance together openly, joined by their classmates and the people who have come to understand that the evening belongs to every student.

The show explores belonging, self-acceptance, and the courage to live openly when acceptance carries a cost. It also asks whether performative allyship can grow into real empathy, and celebrates community action as a force for change.

wedding singer.en:
In 1985 New Jersey, Robbie Hart is a warm-hearted wedding singer whose band—featuring Sammy and George—keeps receptions lively while he dreams of a larger musical future. At a reception, he meets Julia Sullivan, a waitress with romantic ideas about marriage and a forthcoming wedding to her wealthy fiancé, Glen Guglia. Robbie is preparing to marry Linda, but she abandons him at the altar, leaving only a note explaining that she wants the glamour of a rock-star life rather than a future with a wedding singer.

Devastated, Robbie turns bitter and begins wrecking the very celebrations he once made joyful. His friends and his outspoken Grandma Rosie try to pull him out of his misery, while Julia becomes his most reliable source of companionship. Julia, meanwhile, is increasingly uneasy about Glen: he is rich, confident, and successful on Wall Street, but also self-absorbed and unfaithful. As Robbie and Julia spend time together, their easy friendship deepens into feelings neither is fully prepared to admit.

Robbie attempts to reinvent himself as the kind of affluent, hard-edged man he thinks Julia might choose, even seeking Glen’s advice about money and success. The effort only makes him less like himself. When Julia learns that Glen has betrayed her, she breaks off their wedding plans—yet a misunderstanding convinces her that Robbie is still tied to Linda. Hurt and resigned, Julia agrees to elope with Glen in Las Vegas.

Robbie finally understands that the person he loves is Julia and races to stop her. He catches up with her aboard the plane to Las Vegas, where he turns his talent into a public declaration of love. His song exposes Glen’s selfishness and tells Julia what she means to him. Julia rejects Glen and chooses Robbie; their friends celebrate as Robbie and Julia begin their life together.

101 dalmatians.en:
In London, Pongo is rescued from a dog shelter by the warm-hearted Tom, who becomes his devoted “pet.” Elsewhere, Danielle and her Dalmatian Perdi are living a lonely, carefully ordered life. When the dogs meet in the park, their instant attraction sparks an awkward but charming connection between Tom and Danielle. The four quickly become a family, and Pongo and Perdi welcome a lively litter of fifteen puppies.

Their happiness attracts the attention of Cruella de Vil, an extravagant fashion designer obsessed with Dalmatian fur. Determined to turn the puppies’ distinctive coats into her next sensational creation, she first tries to obtain them openly. When Tom and Danielle refuse, Cruella turns to deception and recruits her hapless relatives Jasper and Casper to carry out the theft. The puppies vanish, leaving Pongo and Perdi desperate and the human household devastated.

Refusing to wait helplessly, Pongo and Perdi launch a rescue mission. Guided by the wider canine community, they follow clues across London and beyond, discovering that Cruella’s scheme reaches far beyond their own home: Dalmatian puppies from across the city have been stolen and hidden away. At Cruella’s remote lair, the dogs find their fifteen pups among dozens of frightened captives, creating a total of one hundred and one Dalmatians.

Pongo and Perdi must keep the puppies calm, outwit Cruella’s bungling accomplices, and organise an escape before Cruella can reclaim them. The rescue becomes a fast-moving journey of disguises, near misses, unexpected allies, and canine ingenuity. As Cruella closes in, the Dalmatians rely on one another to get every puppy safely home. Their victory reunites Tom and Danielle with their beloved dogs and transforms a threatened family into an expanded household ready to care for all the rescued pups.

The musical celebrates family as something built through loyalty, care, and the decision to protect the vulnerable. It also pits Cruella’s vanity and greed against courage, cooperation, and the irrepressible joy of belonging together.

count of monte cristo.en:
On the eve of his wedding to Mercedes, the promising young sailor Edmond Dantès is betrayed by jealous and ambitious men: Fernand Mondego covets Mercedes, Danglars resents Edmond’s success, and Villefort protects his own political position. Framed as a Bonapartist conspirator, Edmond is arrested and taken without trial to the Château d’If, where the years strip away his innocence. In prison he meets Abbé Faria, an learned fellow captive who becomes his teacher and confidant. Faria reveals the location of a vast treasure hidden on Monte Cristo, but dies before he can escape with Edmond. Concealing himself in Faria’s burial shroud, Edmond breaks free from the fortress, reaches the island, and claims the fortune.

Years later, Edmond returns to the world as the wealthy, enigmatic Count of Monte Cristo. Moving between Marseilles and Paris, he carefully enters the circles of the three men who destroyed him. He uses his wealth, secrets, and influence to turn their own greed, corruption, and betrayals against them. Danglars is drawn into financial ruin; Villefort’s concealed crimes threaten to consume his household; and Fernand, now elevated in rank and married to Mercedes, faces exposure and disgrace. Edmond’s vengeance is not merely a series of punishments: each scheme pulls innocent people into danger, including the children and loved ones of his enemies.

Mercedes recognizes something familiar beneath the Count’s cold authority and confronts the man Edmond has become. Her presence, together with the suffering caused by his revenge, forces him to distinguish justice from cruelty. As his enemies fall, Edmond must decide whether to continue acting as an instrument of punishment or reclaim the compassion that imprisonment nearly destroyed.

The musical explores betrayal, obsession, and the corrosive power of vengeance. It ultimately asks whether love, mercy, and forgiveness can restore a person who has built his identity around revenge.

death note.en:
In Tokyo, brilliant student Light Yagami despairs at a justice system he believes cannot protect the innocent. When Ryuk, a bored Shinigami, drops the Death Note into the human world, Light discovers that writing a person’s name in its pages can kill them. After testing it on a hostage-taker, he resolves to purge the world of criminals. His unseen campaign of executions earns him public followers and the name “Kira,” while his father, Chief Soichiro Yagami, joins the police investigation into the murders.

The authorities call in L, a secretive and unorthodox detective. L provokes Kira through a televised trap, then deduces that the killer is a student in the Kantō region. Light recognises L as a worthy adversary and begins manipulating the investigation from within, using the notebook to eliminate FBI agents and steer suspicion away from himself. As L closes in, their confrontation becomes an increasingly personal contest of deduction, deception, and nerve.

A second Death Note enters the world and reaches Misa Amane, a pop idol whose life was once saved by the Shinigami Gelus. Convinced that Kira avenged her parents’ murder, Misa becomes his devoted ally. Her guardian, Rem, gives her the Shinigami Eyes, enabling Misa to see people’s true names. Light exploits Misa’s devotion, while L identifies her as the Second Kira and has her detained. To protect Misa, Rem removes her memories of the Death Note; Light then manoeuvres Rem into killing L, even though doing so condemns Rem herself.

With L gone and no one left to stop him, Light believes he has finally won. But Ryuk—having grown tired of the game—writes Light’s name in the Death Note. Light dies as his father and sister arrive too late to understand what has happened, while Misa mourns Rem.

The show examines the seduction and corruption of absolute power, asking who has the right to judge and punish others. It also turns justice into a tragic battle between competing ideals, where obsession, loyalty, and moral certainty destroy everyone involved.

diary of a wimpy kid.en:
Greg Heffley begins his first year at middle school convinced that survival depends on climbing the popularity ladder. Determined never to become a target like his eccentric neighbour Fregley—or even his cheerful best friend, Rowley Jefferson—Greg writes down his observations, schemes, embarrassments, and ambitions as he searches for a way to stand out. At home, he faces the everyday chaos of the Heffley family: his parents Frank and Susan try to steer him toward responsibility, his older brother Rodrick delights in humiliating him, and baby brother Manny somehow escapes every consequence.

At school, Greg treats every activity as a possible route to fame. He tries sports, student government, cartoons for the school paper, safety patrol, and the right kind of smile for the yearbook. Yet his eagerness to impress people repeatedly collides with his limited talent, bad luck, and the rivalry of classmates such as Patty Farrell and Chirag Gupta. Above all, the school is haunted by the dreaded Cheese Touch, a social curse passed from one unlucky student to another through a mouldy piece of cheese on the basketball court.

Rowley loyally joins Greg’s adventures, even when Greg’s plans place him in awkward or unfair situations. But as Rowley begins to enjoy his own successes and friendships, Greg grows jealous. His attempts to protect his image become increasingly selfish, culminating in a choice that leaves Rowley carrying blame and isolation that Greg himself fears. Faced with the consequences, Greg must decide whether popularity is worth losing the one person who has consistently stood by him. By the end, he accepts responsibility, makes amends with Rowley, and discovers that middle school may remain humiliating—but it is more manageable with a true friend beside him.

The musical explores the anxiety of fitting in, the temptation to define oneself through status, and the everyday absurdity of adolescence. Its central message is that friendship, accountability, and empathy matter more than winning the popularity contest.

finding neverland.en:
In 1903 London, playwright J.M. Barrie faces a creative crisis after the disappointing reception of his latest conventional comedy. His producer, Charles Frohman, demands another reliable success, while Barrie’s wife, Mary, grows impatient with his distraction and their increasingly hollow marriage. Escaping a society party, Barrie wanders into Kensington Park, where he meets Sylvia Llewelyn Davies, a widowed mother, and her four sons: George, Jack, Michael, and Peter. He wins the boys’ trust by turning ordinary park games into pirate battles, daring escapes, and fantastic adventures, but Peter—still grieving for his father—refuses to join in.

As Barrie becomes a cherished companion to the family, imagination begins to break through Peter’s sorrow. Their games inspire Barrie to abandon the stale play he has been writing and invent a bold new theatrical world centred on a boy who will not grow up. Yet the adult world resists. Frohman fears that audiences will reject a play about children; Mary resents Barrie’s devotion to Sylvia and her sons; and Sylvia’s formidable mother, Mrs. du Maurier, suspects scandal and tries to sever the connection. Barrie must also persuade a skeptical company of actors to embrace an unfamiliar kind of performance, including the challenge of making a boy fly onstage.

While rehearsals proceed, Sylvia’s health declines. Barrie and the boys respond by making fantasy a refuge: their home becomes a ship, their fears become pirates, and Peter slowly learns that imagination need not deny grief. On the night of the premiere, Barrie brings the family to the theatre and presents the new play as a gift to them. Its success confirms that the private games of a grieving family can become a shared world of wonder. As Sylvia nears death, Barrie gives Peter a final vision of Neverland, allowing him to imagine his mother beyond pain and to face loss with love.

The musical explores imagination as a force that transforms sorrow, failure, and social constraint. It also asks how people can preserve playfulness and emotional openness while accepting that love and childhood cannot remain unchanged.

footloose.en:
Ren McCormack and his mother, Ethel, leave Chicago after Ren’s father abandons the family and move to Bomont, a small town where Ren must live with his aunt and uncle, Lulu and Wes Warnicker. At church, Ren encounters the town’s powerful minister, Reverend Shaw Moore, whose influence has helped impose strict rules against dancing and rock music. Ren quickly finds the town’s constraints suffocating, but he forms an unlikely friendship with Willard Hewitt, a local teenager who is intimidated by the rules yet drawn to Ren’s confidence. Ren also meets Ariel Moore, the Reverend’s fiercely restless daughter, whose relationship with the volatile Chuck Cranston places her in danger and causes immediate friction with Ren.

Ren’s arrival unsettles Bomont. Chuck and his friends, Travis and Lyle, resent the newcomer, while Ariel’s friends Rusty, Wendy Jo, and Urleen encourage the growing attraction between Ariel and Ren. Ren takes Willard to a dance hall outside the town limits and teaches him to dance, helping his friend discover a freedom he has never allowed himself. Meanwhile, Ren learns that the ban on dancing grew out of Reverend Moore’s grief after the death of his son, Bobby, in a car accident. Shaw’s wife, Vi, understands both her husband’s pain and the harm caused by his rigid control, while Ariel struggles to make her father see her as someone he can trust rather than protect through prohibition.

Determined to challenge the ban, Ren studies the law and petitions the town council to permit a school dance. His request provokes anger and suspicion, and Chuck tries to discredit him. When the council refuses, Ren appeals directly to Reverend Moore, arguing that fear cannot keep young people safe. Shaw initially resists, but he confronts his unresolved grief and recognizes that his rules have pushed Ariel away. He ultimately allows the teenagers to hold the dance, and Bomont gathers as its young people finally celebrate openly.

hercules.en:
In ancient Greece, the Muses tell the story of Hercules, the infant son of Zeus and Hera. Fearing a prophecy that foretells his downfall, Hades sends his bungling henchmen, Pain and Panic, to steal the child and make him mortal. Their plan goes wrong: Hercules retains his extraordinary strength and is raised on Earth by the kindly Amphitryon and Alcmene. Though loved by his parents, Hercules grows up feeling painfully out of place, unable to understand why he is different from everyone around him.

After learning of his divine birth, Hercules travels to the Temple of Zeus, where his father tells him he may return to Mount Olympus only by becoming a true hero. Hercules seeks out Phil, a cynical satyr and once-renowned trainer of heroes, who reluctantly agrees to prepare him. With Phil’s discipline and Hercules’s determination, the awkward young man becomes a celebrated champion, defeating monsters and winning the admiration of Thebes.

Hades, however, sees a way to exploit Hercules’s greatest weakness. He sends Megara—sharp-tongued, self-reliant, and indebted to him—to gain Hercules’s trust and discover how he can be defeated. Meg initially treats Hercules as a means to an end, but his sincerity unsettles her, and she begins to care for him despite herself. When Hades frees the Titans to attack Olympus, Hercules confronts them, only to lose his strength after agreeing to surrender it in exchange for Meg’s safety. Hades breaks his promise, leaving Meg in danger and Hercules powerless.

Hercules discovers that heroism is not measured by fame, strength, or divine status. He risks his life to save Meg, proving his worth through selfless love. Restored to his full power, he defeats Hades, rescues Olympus, and is welcomed among the gods—yet chooses to remain on Earth with Meg.

The musical explores belonging, identity, and the difficult path toward becoming one’s best self. It argues that genuine heroism comes from compassion, sacrifice, and the courage to choose love over glory.

high school musical.en:
After winter break, East High School’s cliques return to their familiar territories: Troy Bolton leads the Wildcats basketball team, Gabriella Montez joins the Brainiacs, and Sharpay Evans and her brother Ryan dominate the drama department. Troy and Gabriella are startled to recognize each other: they met during a ski-trip karaoke night and shared an unexpectedly easy duet. Their connection deepens when Gabriella transfers to East High, but both fear stepping outside the roles their friends expect them to play.

Ms. Darbus announces auditions for the winter musical, Juliet and Romeo, written by the shy pianist Kelsi Nielsen. Sharpay, accustomed to claiming the leading role, intends to perform with Ryan. When Troy and Gabriella end up in detention and discover Kelsi’s discarded score, they sing through the song together. Ms. Darbus overhears them and invites them to audition, a prospect that unnerves Troy’s best friend Chad Danforth, Gabriella’s friend Taylor McKessie, and Coach Bolton, Troy’s father and basketball coach. Everyone worries that the show will distract Troy from the championship game or Gabriella from the Scholastic Decathlon.

Sharpay and Ryan discover that Troy and Gabriella may challenge them for the leads. Determined to protect her position, Sharpay arranges conflicting schedules for the callbacks, basketball championship, and Decathlon. Chad and Taylor, believing they are helping their friends, pressure Troy and Gabriella to abandon the musical. Hurt by the lack of trust around them, Troy and Gabriella withdraw from the audition process and from one another.

Kelsi, Chad, Taylor, and the other students eventually realize that they have reinforced the divisions they claim to dislike. They organize a plan that moves the championship and Decathlon forward so Troy and Gabriella can reach the callbacks. Troy and Gabriella arrive in time, perform together, and earn the leading roles. The school celebrates as students across the cliques reveal their own unexpected interests and choose to support one another.

kikis delivery service.en:
On the night of a full moon, thirteen-year-old Kiki leaves home to begin the year of independence required of a young witch. With only her broom, a small radio, and her black cat Jiji for company, she searches for a town where she can make a life of her own. After a difficult flight, she reaches the bustling seaside city of Koriko, where her arrival immediately marks her as an outsider. Her first encounter with Tombo, an enthusiastic local boy fascinated by flight, is awkward; Kiki is wary of his teasing attention and uncertain how to respond to him.

Kiki soon meets Osono, the generous owner of a bakery, and Fukuo, Osono’s husband. When a customer leaves behind a gift meant for someone else, Kiki volunteers to deliver it by broom. The errand gives her an idea: she opens a flying delivery service, earning a room above the bakery and beginning to build a place for herself in Koriko. Her work brings both mishaps and new acquaintances. During an early delivery, she loses a treasured toy and meets Ursula, a painter living in the woods, whose kindness helps Kiki complete the job.

As Kiki grows busier, she struggles with loneliness, exhaustion, and the pressure to prove that she belongs. Her feelings toward Tombo become more complicated as his friendliness alternately delights and embarrasses her. When Kiki’s confidence falters, her magic weakens: she cannot fly and can no longer understand Jiji. Unable to work, she withdraws until Ursula helps her recognize that inspiration and self-belief cannot be forced.

A crisis in Koriko gives Kiki the chance to act. When Tombo is left in danger during a public airborne accident, Kiki finds the courage to fly again and rescues him. With her confidence renewed, she returns to her deliveries and embraces Koriko as her new home.

The musical is about growing up through independence, responsibility, and resilience. It celebrates the way friendship, purposeful work, and compassion can turn an unfamiliar city into a community—and uncertainty into confidence.

little women.en:
At Mrs. Kirk’s Boarding House in New York, Jo March receives another rejection for one of her lurid adventure stories. When fellow boarder Professor Bhaer urges her to write with greater honesty, Jo resists, then remembers her family’s earlier life in Concord, Massachusetts. During the Civil War, Jo lives with Marmee and her sisters: romantic Meg, gentle Beth, and spirited Amy, while their father serves away from home. Jo stages her own melodramatic “Operatic Tragedy,” casting the family and their neighbour, Laurie Laurence, whose friendship soon makes him part of the household.

The sisters confront both hardship and growing independence. Meg falls in love with John Brooke, Laurie’s tutor, despite Aunt March’s insistence that she should make a more advantageous match. Amy, longing for elegance and experience, clashes with Jo and is eventually sent to Europe with Aunt March. Beth’s kindness brings her close to the reserved Mr. Laurence, but after helping a poor family she becomes dangerously ill. When Mr. March is wounded, Marmee travels to him, and Jo sacrifices her treasured hair to help pay for the journey. Beth recovers for a time, but her health remains fragile.

As the sisters grow older, Meg marries John, Amy returns from Europe more mature, and Laurie asks Jo to marry him. Jo loves him deeply as a friend but refuses, believing that neither of them would be happy in such a marriage. Hurt, Laurie travels abroad, where he and Amy gradually come to understand one another and fall in love. Beth’s illness worsens, and her death leaves Jo devastated. Returning to New York, Jo finally accepts Professor Bhaer’s challenge: she writes not sensational fiction, but the truthful story of her family. When Bhaer recognizes the value of her work, their mutual respect becomes love.

The musical explores the pull between family devotion and the desire to shape an independent life. It treats love, loss, ambition, and creativity as forces that help the March sisters become adults without losing the bonds that define them.

love never dies.en:
Ten years after the events at the Paris Opera, the Phantom lives in New York as the masked creator of Phantasma, a glittering Coney Island world of freak shows, music, and illusion. Known publicly only as Mr. Y, he has achieved wealth and power with the help of Madame Giry and her daughter Meg, yet remains consumed by his memory of Christine Daaé. He arranges for Christine—now an acclaimed singer—to make her American debut at Phantasma. She arrives with her husband, Raoul de Chagny, and their young son, Gustave. Raoul’s gambling and drinking have ruined much of their fortune and strained their marriage, while Gustave’s remarkable musical sensitivity immediately draws the Phantom’s attention.

The Phantom reveals himself to Christine and offers her a vast fee to sing one performance. Their encounter reawakens their unresolved feelings, and Christine admits that, before marrying Raoul, she spent one night with the Phantom; Gustave is the Phantom’s son. The Phantom is overjoyed by the discovery and asks Christine to remain with him, but she refuses to abandon Gustave or her life. Meanwhile, Madame Giry resents Christine, believing that she and Meg sacrificed everything to secure the Phantom’s future, only for him to turn again toward his former love. Meg, humiliated by the Phantom’s indifference to her own ambitions as a performer, becomes increasingly desperate.

Christine sings at Phantasma, while Raoul—wounded by the truth about Gustave—agrees to leave her if she does not return by dawn. After the performance, Christine chooses to go back to Raoul and Gustave. Meg confronts Christine backstage, demanding recognition and affection, then pulls a gun in anguish. In the struggle, Meg shoots Christine. The Phantom arrives too late; Christine dies in his arms after entrusting Gustave to him. As Meg is taken away, the Phantom and Raoul stand united in grief beside the boy.

The musical explores enduring love, obsession, and the cost of secrets left unresolved. It contrasts the longing for an imagined past with the painful responsibility of choosing how to live in the present.

madagascar.en:
At New York’s Central Park Zoo, Alex the Lion enjoys celebrity as the self-styled “King of New York,” performing daily for delighted visitors alongside his closest friends: Marty the Zebra, Gloria the Hippo, and Melman the Giraffe. While Alex is perfectly content with regular meals and applause, Marty feels trapped by the predictability of zoo life. On his birthday, he becomes determined to see the wild for himself. The resourceful penguins—Skipper, Kowalski, Rico, and Private—are already plotting their own escape, and Marty slips away toward Grand Central Station. Alex, Gloria, and the anxious, health-obsessed Melman pursue him, hoping to bring him safely home.

The animals cause chaos in the city and are captured by Animal Control. They are shipped away by sea, but the penguins seize control of the vessel, sending Alex, Marty, Gloria, and Melman overboard. The four friends wash up on Madagascar, where King Julien and his lemur court welcome them with exuberant celebration. Julien believes the newcomers may protect the lemurs from the frightening Foosa, predators who regularly threaten the island.

At first, the friends try to adapt to the unfamiliar wild. Marty is thrilled by open space and begins to embrace his freedom, while Alex struggles without the steaks and comforts of the zoo. Hunger awakens Alex’s predatory instincts, frightening him and placing particular strain on his friendship with Marty. When the Foosa attack, Alex confronts the danger and helps protect the lemurs. Realising that his friends need help, the penguins return with the ship. The group reunites, and Alex, Marty, Gloria, and Melman choose to leave the island together, carrying their hard-won understanding of one another into whatever comes next.

The show centres on friendship tested by change, the tension between safety and freedom, and learning to accept one’s true nature. It also celebrates courage, belonging, and the idea that home is shaped as much by loyal companions as by any particular place.

martin guerre.en:
In sixteenth-century Artigat, a fiercely Catholic village in France, the young Martin Guerre is forced by his uncle Pierre into marriage with Bertrande de Rols so that the community may secure a Catholic heir. The marriage brings neither happiness nor a child: Martin cannot consummate it, and the village priests humiliate and beat him for his failure. Unable to bear the shame and constraint, he abandons Bertrande and joins the Protestant Huguenot forces. Years later, amid war, Martin tells his story to a fellow soldier, Arnaud du Thil. When a battle leaves Martin apparently dead, Arnaud resolves to travel to Artigat and inform Bertrande.

On arriving, Arnaud is astonishingly mistaken for the long-lost Martin. Before he can correct the villagers, he is swept back into the life of the man he believed dead. Bertrande soon recognises that the stranger is not her husband; nevertheless, she chooses to protect him. The pair are gradually drawn together, finding in one another the tenderness and freedom that Bertrande never knew in her marriage. Arnaud assumes Martin’s name, while Guillaume—Martin’s former friend, who has long loved Bertrande—watches their closeness with growing jealousy.

Bertrande reveals that she has become a Protestant and leads Arnaud to the village’s secret worshippers. Guillaume discovers their faith and denounces them, unleashing a violent Catholic mob. Benoit, a villager who has understood the deception, exposes Arnaud as an impostor, and Arnaud is imprisoned to stand trial. Then Martin Guerre himself arrives: he survived the war and has returned to reclaim his name. Yet Martin sees that Arnaud and Bertrande’s love is real, forgives his rival, and helps free him. The village’s hatred cannot be so easily undone: as violence consumes Artigat, Guillaume fatally stabs Arnaud. Arnaud dies in Bertrande’s arms, and she and Martin finally separate.

The musical explores love as a choice rather than an obligation, contrasting imposed marriage with a bond freely made. It also confronts identity, religious persecution, jealousy, and the devastating force of communal intolerance.

oliver twist.en:
In nineteenth-century London, Oliver Twist is born in a workhouse and grows up hungry, lonely, and unwanted. When the boys draw lots to decide who will ask for more food, Oliver is chosen and makes his famous plea. The outraged Beadle, Mr Bumble, offers a reward to anyone willing to take him away. Oliver is apprenticed to the undertaker Mr Sowerberry, but after defending his mother from cruel insults by the apprentice Noah Claypole, he runs away to London.

Exhausted and starving, Oliver meets the Artful Dodger, who takes him to the den of Fagin, an elderly receiver of stolen goods. There Oliver encounters Fagin’s gang of child pickpockets, the volatile Bill Sikes, and Sikes’s kind-hearted companion Nancy. Oliver does not understand the gang’s criminal purpose until he is sent out with Dodger and Charley Bates and sees them pick the pocket of a wealthy gentleman, Mr Brownlow. Oliver is wrongly blamed for the theft and seized, but Brownlow takes pity on him and brings him into his home, where he and his housekeeper Mrs Bedwin offer safety, warmth, and education.

Fagin and Sikes fear that Oliver may expose them, so Sikes forces Nancy to help lure him back to the gang. Nancy, increasingly tormented by guilt, secretly meets Mr Brownlow and arranges to return Oliver to safety. Her plan is discovered by Sikes, who murders her in a rage. As an angry mob and the authorities close in, Sikes drags Oliver across the rooftops as a hostage but falls to his death during the escape, and the boy is saved. Oliver is finally reunited with Brownlow—revealed to be his own kin—and finds a secure home, while Fagin, his hidden fortune gone, is left to reconsider the life he has led.

The musical explores the endurance of innocence amid poverty, cruelty, and exploitation. It contrasts selfishness and violence with compassion, loyalty, and the possibility of belonging.

peter pan.en:
In the Darling nursery, Wendy, John, and Michael are preparing for bed when Peter Pan arrives with Tinker Bell to reclaim his missing shadow. Wendy sews it back on, and Peter invites her to Neverland to tell stories to the Lost Boys. Her brothers eagerly join the adventure. Following Peter’s lesson in flight—think happy thoughts—the children soar over London and arrive in Neverland, a place of mermaids, pirates, and perpetual childhood.

Tinker Bell, jealous of Wendy’s place beside Peter, deceives the Lost Boys into nearly shooting her. Peter saves Wendy, who soon takes on the role of storyteller and motherly guide to the boys. Meanwhile, Captain Hook plots revenge against Peter, who cut off his hand and fed it to the Crocodile. The beast swallowed a ticking clock as well, so Hook lives in terror of its approaching sound. Peter rescues Tiger Lily from Hook and his pirates, but his triumph deepens the rivalry among Wendy, Tinker Bell, and the inhabitants of the island.

After adventures underground and at the Mermaids’ Lagoon, Wendy begins to miss home. She decides that John and Michael should return to London, and the Lost Boys ask to come with them. Peter refuses to grow up or leave Neverland. While he is away, Hook poisons Peter’s medicine, but Tinker Bell drinks it to save him. Peter’s faith and the audience’s belief restore her.

Hook then captures Wendy, John, Michael, and the Lost Boys, taking them aboard the Jolly Roger. Wendy is tied to the mast and the boys face the plank. Peter slips aboard, defeats Hook and the pirates, and sends Hook fleeing from the Crocodile. The Darling children return home with the Lost Boys, where Mr. and Mrs. Darling welcome them. Peter remains in Neverland, still young and free, returning only from time to time to visit Wendy.

The musical explores the pull between childhood freedom and the responsibilities of growing up. It also celebrates imagination, loyalty, courage, and the enduring comfort of home.

picture of dorian gray.en:
In Victorian London, the beautiful young Dorian Gray sits for a portrait by the devoted painter Basil Hallward. At Basil’s studio, Dorian meets Lord Henry Wotton, whose seductive philosophy exalts youth, beauty, and pleasure above conscience. Horrified by the thought that the painted image will remain young while he ages, Dorian passionately wishes that the portrait might bear time’s damage in his place. The wish is granted: Dorian’s face stays flawless, while the concealed picture begins to register the corruption of his soul.

Dorian falls in love with Sibyl Vane, a gifted young actress performing Shakespeare in a shabby theatre. He idealises her as an artist, but after she experiences real love, Sibyl can no longer find truth in acting imagined passions. Dorian rejects her cruelly, and Sibyl takes her own life. When Dorian sees that the portrait has acquired a cruel expression, he understands its terrible power—yet Lord Henry persuades him to treat Sibyl’s death as a beautiful tragedy rather than a moral reckoning.

Years pass, but Dorian remains outwardly unchanged as he pursues pleasure and destroys the lives of those drawn into his orbit. Rumours surround him, while the locked-away portrait becomes increasingly grotesque. Basil confronts Dorian and begs him to repent; instead, Dorian reveals the ruined canvas and murders him. He forces the chemist Alan Campbell to dispose of Basil’s body, driving Alan toward his own death.

Dorian’s past finally closes in when Sibyl’s brother, James Vane, seeks revenge. Though James is killed before he can expose him, Dorian cannot escape his own conscience. Hoping to destroy the evidence of his corruption and begin anew, he stabs the portrait. Servants find an aged, disfigured dead man beside a painting restored to the radiant young Dorian Gray.

The musical explores the peril of worshipping beauty, youth, and sensation without responsibility. It traces how denial and self-indulgence estrange Dorian from love, empathy, and finally himself.

prince of egypt.en:
In ancient Egypt, the Hebrews endure brutal forced labour while Pharaoh Seti orders the death of their newborn sons. To save her baby, Yocheved places him in a basket on the Nile. Queen Tuya discovers the child and raises him as Moses, alongside her son Ramses. Years later, the two princes are inseparable, though Ramses struggles beneath Seti’s expectations and his impending political marriage to Nefertari. Moses, meanwhile, feels uncertain of his own purpose.

After Seti returns from a campaign against the Midianites, Moses meets Tzipporah, a captured Midianite woman who refuses to submit to life as a slave. Their encounter unsettles him further. In the city, Moses meets Miriam and Aaron, who reveal that he was born Hebrew. Miriam’s memory of Yocheved’s lullaby awakens fragments of his past, and Moses discovers evidence of Seti’s slaughter of Hebrew children. Tuya confirms the truth but begs him to remain her son and preserve the life he has known.

At a worksite, Moses sees an overseer cruelly beating a Hebrew labourer. Trying to intervene, he kills the man and flees Egypt. In the desert he is welcomed by Jethro and the Midianites, reunites with Tzipporah, and finds a new life as a shepherd. Then a burning bush commands Moses to return to Egypt and lead the Hebrews to freedom.

Moses confronts Ramses, now Pharaoh, but Ramses refuses to release the slaves. Their conflict intensifies as Egypt suffers devastating plagues, each brother torn between love, duty, and the people depending on him. After the death of Ramses’s son, Pharaoh finally lets the Hebrews go, only to send his army after them. Moses leads the people through the parted Red Sea; the pursuing army is destroyed as the waters close, leaving Moses and Ramses separated on opposite shores.

The show explores brotherhood tested by power, identity, and moral responsibility. It follows the cost of liberation, the persistence of hope, and the difficult choice to follow one’s calling even when it breaks the bonds one loves most.

robin hood.en:
Robin of Loxley grows up as a privileged nobleman in twelfth-century England, betrothed to Marian, the daughter of the Sheriff of Nottingham. Restless beneath his father’s expectations, Robin joins his friend Guy of Gisbourne on crusade. When Guy returns alone and Robin is presumed dead, Nottingham has changed: King John’s rule has brought harsh taxation, fear, and misery to ordinary people. Guy exploits Robin’s absence, hoping to win Marian and advance his own position.

A year later, Robin unexpectedly returns. His experiences abroad have left him deeply shaken, and he initially resists both responsibility and the life arranged for him. Guy’s ambitions are exposed, yet Robin seeks redress at King John’s court rather than openly opposing the new order. Marian challenges Robin’s withdrawal, urging him to see the suffering around him and act on behalf of those who cannot defend themselves. When the Sheriff is killed through the regime’s violence, Robin finally understands that the authorities will not deliver justice.

Renouncing his former place, Robin flees into Sherwood Forest, where he finds shelter among outlaws. There he becomes Robin Hood, joining their resistance against Guy, the Sheriff’s forces, and King John’s oppressive rule. As Robin learns to lead, he and Marian rebuild the trust damaged by war, absence, and divided loyalties. Their struggle gathers strength, but Guy refuses to surrender his claim to power. When he kidnaps Marian, Robin must face him in a final confrontation that will determine both Marian’s fate and the future of Nottingham.

The musical explores the making of a reluctant hero: Robin must transform personal loss and trauma into courage and public responsibility. It also centres on love, loyalty, freedom, and the conviction that injustice must be actively resisted.

rocky horror show.en:
After attending the wedding of friends Ralph Hapschatt and Betty Munroe, the newly engaged Brad Majors and Janet Weiss set out to visit their former tutor, Dr. Everett Scott. Caught in a storm, their car suffers a flat tyre near an isolated castle. They seek a telephone and are admitted by the eccentric Riff Raff, Magenta, and Columbia, who draw them into a wild gathering. The castle’s master, Dr. Frank ’N’ Furter, arrives and reveals his latest experiment: Rocky Horror, a handsome, muscular man brought to life in Frank’s laboratory.

Frank intends Rocky to be his ideal companion, but the celebration is disrupted when Eddie bursts from a freezer. Columbia recognises Eddie as her former lover, and his appearance exposes Frank’s ruthless treatment of him; Frank kills Eddie with an axe. Brad and Janet are sent separately to bed, where Frank visits each of them while disguised as the other, seducing them both. Rocky later escapes Frank’s room, and Janet finds him hiding in the laboratory. Hurt by Brad’s apparent betrayal and drawn to Rocky’s innocence, she seduces him herself.

Dr. Scott arrives looking for Eddie, his nephew, only to discover Brad and Janet at the castle. Frank accuses Scott of spying, but the group’s tensions intensify when Janet, Brad, Rocky, Columbia, and Scott are captured and transformed into statues by Frank’s Medusa Transducer. Frank dresses them for a floor-show spectacle, yet Riff Raff and Magenta turn against him. They reveal that they must return to their home planet and condemn Frank for delaying their departure. Riff Raff kills Columbia, Rocky, and finally Frank, then launches the castle into space, leaving Brad, Janet, and Dr. Scott stranded amid the wreckage.

The show explores liberation, temptation, and the collapse of conventional innocence. It contrasts Brad and Janet’s ordered romantic ideals with a chaotic world of desire, performance, power, and self-discovery.

show boat.en:
On the Mississippi River in the late 1880s, Cap’n Andy Hawks and his stern wife, Parthy, run the Cotton Blossom, a floating theatre that brings melodrama and music to river towns. Their daughter Magnolia is captivated by Gaylord Ravenal, a charming but rootless gambler she meets on the levee at Natchez. At the same time, leading lady Julie La Verne and her husband, Steve Baker, face danger when Pete, the boat’s dismissed engineer, exposes Julie’s mixed racial background. A sheriff arrives to enforce the state’s ban on interracial marriage. Steve prevents their arrest by claiming mixed ancestry himself, but he and Julie must leave the Cotton Blossom.

With the company suddenly without its romantic leads, Cap’n Andy casts Magnolia and Ravenal. Their stage romance becomes real, and, despite Parthy’s objections and revelations about Ravenal’s violent past, they marry in Greenville. Years later they are living in Chicago with their daughter, Kim. Ravenal’s gambling brings bursts of prosperity but increasingly severe losses. He sells or pawns their belongings, falls behind on rent, and finally leaves Magnolia money for Kim along with a farewell letter, convinced that his failures make him unfit to remain with them.

Magnolia is left desperate, but Frank Schultz and Ellie May Chipley, former colleagues from the Cotton Blossom, help her seek work at the Trocadero Club. There she encounters Julie again, now lonely and struggling after Steve’s departure. Julie silently gives up her own place in the club so that Magnolia can be hired. On New Year’s Eve, Magnolia begins her first performance nervously; seeing Cap’n Andy in the audience restores her confidence, and she wins over the crowd. Her career flourishes, while Kim grows into a Broadway performer. Decades later, back on the Cotton Blossom, Cap’n Andy brings Magnolia and Ravenal together again. Their long separation ends in reconciliation, joined by Kim and the surviving show-boat family.

The musical traces love tested by social prejudice, economic insecurity, and personal weakness. It also sets individual lives against the enduring flow of the river, exploring endurance, family bonds, racial injustice, and the possibility of forgiveness.

zorro.en:
In early nineteenth-century California, Don Alejandro sends his son Diego de la Vega to school in Spain, separating him from his childhood friends Luisa and Ramon. Diego soon abandons his studies for the freedom of Barcelona’s streets, where he performs with a lively band of gypsies led by the formidable Inez. Years later, Luisa finds him and brings alarming news: Ramon has seized control of their pueblo after claiming that Don Alejandro is dead. He rules through fear, crushing the people with taxes and punishment. Diego returns with Inez and the gypsies, only to discover that his father is alive but held prisoner by Ramon.

Appalled by Ramon’s brutality, Diego creates a masked alter ego: Zorro. While posing before Ramon as a foolish, harmless servant, Diego secretly becomes the daring defender of the pueblo, rescuing prisoners and humiliating the soldiers who enforce Ramon’s authority. The people rally to their mysterious hero, but the double life brings complications. Luisa, frustrated by Diego’s apparent cowardice, becomes captivated by Zorro without realizing they are the same man. Inez, who cares deeply for Diego, watches this growing attachment with uneasy amusement, while Sergeant Garcia, Ramon’s blustering but soft-hearted subordinate, becomes enchanted by Inez.

Ramon’s jealousy, ambition, and desire for Luisa drive him toward greater violence. When Zorro prevents him from attacking her, Ramon inadvertently reveals that Don Alejandro survives. Zorro frees his father and confronts Ramon, who learns that the masked enemy is Diego. In their final sword fight, Diego appeals to the bond of their shared childhood and asks Ramon to stop. Ramon refuses, and his own aggression leads to his fatal fall. Diego unmasks before Luisa; shocked but joyful, she accepts both the gentle man and the hero. With Ramon gone and Don Alejandro restored, the pueblo celebrates its liberation.

The musical explores the struggle between tyranny and justice, and the courage required to oppose cruelty even when safety lies in silence. It also treats identity, love, friendship, and forgiveness as inseparable from the choice to use power in service of others.

薄桜鬼 真改.en:
In Kyoto at the end of the shogunate, Chizuru Yukimura arrives from Edo in search of her missing father, the Western-trained doctor Kodo Yukimura. One night she is attacked by feral, white-haired men, but the Shinsengumi intervene and cut them down. Mistaking Chizuru for a boy, the warriors take her to their headquarters; after discovering her identity and her connection to Kodo, Vice-Commander Toshizo Hijikata permits her to stay under their protection while they pursue the same mystery.

Living among the Shinsengumi, Chizuru comes to know Commander Isami Kondo and his captains: the severe Hajime Saito, volatile Souji Okita, warm-hearted Heisuke Toudou, dependable Sanosuke Harada, and their comrades. As Kyoto grows more unstable, the group carries out dangerous assignments for the shogunate, facing assassinations, political violence, and enemies who challenge their role as protectors of the old order. Chizuru gradually earns their trust and becomes especially close to Hijikata, whose restraint conceals an unyielding sense of duty.

Their search leads to the Water of Life, an experimental drug connected to Kodo. It can create Rasetsu—superhuman fighters driven by an agonizing, insatiable thirst for blood. The Shinsengumi discover that this power is being exploited amid the conflict, while Chizuru herself is drawn into a deeper secret: she has oni blood, and the oni leader Chikage Kazama claims a right to her. Hijikata and the others must confront both human political enemies and supernatural forces as their world collapses around them. Losses, illness, and divided loyalties test the Shinsengumi, while Chizuru refuses to abandon the people who gave her a home. In the struggle between survival and principle, Hijikata’s bond with Chizuru becomes a source of resolve as he carries the Shinsengumi’s ideals into an increasingly hopeless future.

The musical explores loyalty tested by historical change, and the cost of holding to one’s convictions when defeat appears inevitable. It also sets love, chosen family, and human dignity against violence, sacrifice, and the fear of becoming a monster.

ケロロ軍曹.en:
Sergeant Keroro arrives on Pekopon with the Keroro Platoon under orders to prepare the planet for conquest. The mission goes wrong almost immediately: Keroro is discovered by Fuyuki Hinata and his older sister Natsumi, and the supposedly formidable alien soldier ends up living as an unwilling lodger in the Hinata household. Rather than establishing a secret base and summoning an army, he is expected to help with chores while continuing to insist that Pekopon will one day belong to Planet Keron.

Keroro reunites with his scattered comrades, each of whom brings a different complication to the campaign. The eager but volatile Private Tamama is tied to Momoka Nishizawa, whose feelings for Fuyuki turn everyday encounters into melodrama. The intense Corporal Giroro tries to remain a dedicated soldier while becoming hopelessly devoted to Natsumi. The sly Sergeant Major Kururu approaches invasion as a laboratory experiment, using inventions and manipulation to stir trouble. Meanwhile, the disciplined Lance Corporal Dororo, a ninja with a painful history of being overlooked by his own friends, finds an unexpected companion in Koyuki Azumaya.

As the platoon attempts to turn grand military ambitions into practical schemes, their plans collide with the rhythms of human domestic life: friendships, crushes, rivalries, household rules, and the sheer absurdity of trying to conquer a world while depending on its inhabitants for a place to sleep. Keroro repeatedly tries to rally the group around their original objective, but the platoon’s personal attachments and clashing temperaments transform every operation into comic chaos. Fuyuki’s open-hearted friendship with Keroro further blurs the line between captor, host, enemy, and ally, forcing the alien commander to confront how comfortable life on Pekopon has become.

At its heart, the show celebrates friendship across boundaries, the comedy of failed ambition, and the way everyday kindness can disarm even would-be invaders. It treats loyalty, belonging, and growing up as things discovered through shared mishaps rather than grand victories.

テニスの王子様.en:
Ryoma Echizen arrives at Seishun Academy with an extraordinary reputation: he has won four consecutive American junior championships, yet he carries himself with an almost infuriating calm. His goal is simple—to earn a place on Seigaku’s powerful tennis team and prove that his talent belongs on Japan’s courts. Under the watchful eye of captain Kunimitsu Tezuka, Ryoma enters a club already filled with distinctive, formidable players: dependable vice-captain Shuichiro Oishi, acrobatic Eiji Kikumaru, brilliant Syusuke Fuji, analytical Sadaharu Inui, explosive Takashi Kawamura, spirited Takeshi Momoshiro, tenacious Kaoru Kaidoh, and the reserved Tezuka himself. Ryoma’s confidence quickly draws attention, especially from Momoshiro, who becomes both a teasing guide and an early rival.

To become a regular, Ryoma must survive Seigaku’s demanding internal ranking matches. Each contest exposes him to a different approach to tennis and a different kind of opponent. Inui tries to calculate the game through exhaustive data; Kaidoh relies on endurance and stubborn will; Momoshiro plays with instinct and momentum; Fuji conceals a frighteningly precise strategic mind. Ryoma’s technical gifts repeatedly put him ahead, but the matches challenge more than his reflexes and signature shots. He begins to see that victory is not merely an individual display of brilliance: a school team is built from trust, pressure, rivalry, and the desire to stand beside players who refuse to yield.

As the regular lineup takes shape, Seigaku turns outward toward the National Middle School Tennis Tournament. Rival schools and celebrated players make clear that Seigaku’s road will be difficult, while Tezuka’s unwavering ambition gives the team a shared direction. Ryoma, once content to defeat anyone placed across the net, gradually finds a stronger reason to play: to test himself against ever-higher competition and to help carry Seigaku toward the national stage.

The musical is about youth meeting discipline, individual talent learning teamwork, and rivals pushing one another beyond their limits. Its tennis matches become expressions of friendship, pride, perseverance, and the search for a personal reason to compete.

ポーの一族.en:
Abandoned in a forest in rural England, young Edgar and his baby sister Marybell are found and raised by Old Hannah at a secluded manor. Their protectors are members of the Poe Clan, Vampanella who exist outside ordinary human time. When villagers uncover the clan’s secret and surround them, the Elder Poe acts to secure the clan’s survival: he forcibly turns Edgar into one of them. Edgar’s transformation seals him into eternal youth, and Marybell is also drawn into the clan’s immortal existence. Under the care of their adoptive parents, Baron Portsnell and Sheila, the siblings begin a life that will extend far beyond any human lifetime.

Years later, Edgar, Marybell, the Baron, and Sheila arrive in Blackpool, a growing port city. The Baron and Sheila set their sights on Jean Clifford, a physician who runs a local clinic, hoping to bring him into their world. Edgar, however, is pulled toward another encounter: Alan Twilight, heir to the town’s most prominent family. Alan is a lonely, troubled boy, and the meeting between him and Edgar feels less like chance than fate. As their bond deepens, Edgar must confront the burden of having been denied a normal life and the terrible intimacy of choosing—or refusing—to bind another person to eternity. Alan’s path becomes entwined with Edgar’s, carrying both boys into the Poe Clan’s shadowed, wandering future.

The musical explores eternal youth as a curse rather than a gift, asking what remains of identity when time, home, and ordinary human bonds are lost. It is also a story of chosen family, loneliness, devotion, and the painful consequences of love that tries to outlast death.

忍たま乱太郎.en:
At Ninjutsu Academy, Rantarō, Kirimaru, and Shinbei are swept into a crisis when they glimpse a strange “great dragon” beneath a forest pond during an unexpected orienteering exercise. The shape is no monster, but a newly imported cannon secretly concealed by Dokutake Castle. Once the three boys discover the weapon, Dokutake’s ninja force captures them to keep the plan hidden. Back at the academy, the Headmaster turns the emergency into a test for the senior students: the Sixth Years must rescue the younger pupils as their graduation examination.

The rescue mission leads the Sixth Years toward Dokutake Castle, but the journey proves far more dangerous than a straightforward infiltration. Along the way they encounter Shinkichi, an exhausted man fleeing an unknown pursuer, and soon find themselves confronted by Akakabe, a mysterious ninja whose motives and loyalties are unclear. Dokutake’s normally familiar operatives also behave in unsettling new ways, leaving the students unsure whom they can trust and forcing them to adapt their plans repeatedly.

As the Sixth Years press deeper into enemy territory, their mission becomes a test not only of stealth, combat, and ingenuity, but of their ability to act together under pressure. The captives must endure their own peril while waiting for help, and the senior students have to overcome traps, deception, and the enemy’s superior position inside the castle. What began as a school exercise grows into a genuine confrontation over Dokutake’s hidden weapon and the safety of Ninjutsu Academy. The decisive conflict demands courage from the younger students and maturity from those about to leave the academy, as the Sixth Years fight to bring Rantarō, Kirimaru, and Shinbei home.

At its heart, the show is about friendship tested by danger, teamwork forged through responsibility, and the passage from training to real-world action. It treats ninja skill not as individual bravado, but as the willingness to protect others and trust one’s companions.

新テニスの王子様.en:
After the National Middle School Tennis Tournament comes to a close, Ryoma Echizen and the finest middle-school players from schools such as Seigaku, Hyotei, Rikkaidai, and Shitenhoji are summoned to the U-17 Japan National Team training camp, established to cultivate the country’s very best talent. Rivals who once battled one another on opposite sides of the net must now strive forward side by side. What awaits them, however, is a camp far harsher than any of them imagined: high-school players whose strength lies well beyond their expectations, and a coaching staff whose methods are difficult to predict.

The camp runs on absolute merit—those who lose are cut. The boys must not only endure punishing training but prove themselves in one brutal match after another. When Ryoma clashes with a coach, he is driven out of the camp and travels alone to the United States to sharpen his game, while the players who remain in Japan confront powerful opponents from the high-school ranks and ever-escalating internal competition. Across singles, doubles, and team matches, the middle-schoolers must come to know their teammates anew and break through their own weaknesses and limits. With the return of the “Japan representatives” from their overseas expedition, the former camp members are pushed toward challenges of an even higher order.

In time, the middle-schoolers and high-schoolers cease merely to fight over a place in the ranks and instead build toward a shared goal: to represent Japan and stand against the world’s finest young players. Ryoma, too, returns from his training abroad with firmer resolve, throwing himself into a new battle. Through high-intensity tennis showdowns, the musical weaves together growth, rivalry, and cooperation, as each player searches for his own answer on the road toward becoming the best in the world.

刀剣乱舞.en:
In a distant future, the Sage sends a unit of Sword Warriors—living embodiments of legendary blades—back through time to protect decisive moments in Japanese history from the Time Retrograde Army. Each mission asks them to defeat invaders seeking to alter the past, yet the warriors cannot treat history as an abstract record: the people they meet are often the former owners of the swords they have become, and their deaths, victories, and regrets remain inseparable from the warriors’ own identities. At their citadel, Mikazuki Munechika, Kogitsunemaru, Ishikirimaru, Iwatooshi, Imanotsurugi, Kashuu Kiyomitsu, Yamatonokami Yasusada, Izuminokami Kanesada, Horikawa Kunihiro, Hachisuka Kotetsu, Nagasone Kotetsu, Higekiri, Hizamaru, and their comrades prepare for assignments whose outcome they already know but must still see through.

Their journeys bring them to periods of civil conflict and political change, including the turbulent final years of the shogunate. When a mission threatens the course of events surrounding Hijikata Toshizo and the Shinsengumi, Izuminokami Kanesada and Horikawa Kunihiro confront a particularly painful duty: Hijikata was their former master. The enemy’s plan is not merely to win a battle but to preserve a man whom history records as doomed, thereby changing the future built upon his defeat. The Sword Warriors fight beside people they respect, share moments of loyalty and resolve with them, and nevertheless must prevent them from escaping the fate history has assigned.

Elsewhere, the unit faces legends, succession struggles, betrayals, and the lingering wishes of those who once wielded them. Bonds among the Sword Warriors deepen as they learn that protecting history sometimes means accepting loss rather than correcting it. Their battles test whether devotion to a former master can coexist with obedience to the mission, and whether a weapon given human form can choose its own understanding of purpose.

The show explores the tension between memory and duty, asking what it means to honor the dead without refusing the reality of their fate. It is also a story of companionship: people and swords alike find strength in carrying grief forward together.
